policy_name: Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021

policy_goals: Accelerating KarnatakaΓÇÖs growth towards leaving a footprint in the Global Engineering R&D landscape, promoting the State as the ΓÇÿEngineering R&D Destination of ChoiceΓÇÖ and transforming into a vibrant ΓÇÿKnowledge EconomyΓÇÖ.
Attract leading Engineering R&D entities to establish and/or expand Engineering R&D capabilities in Karnataka
Create strong linkages between Industry and Academia to accelerate development of innovative Engineering R&D products, solutions and services
Support and strengthen the availability of skilled Engineering R&D human capital
Establish and offer access to advanced testing, prototyping and other allied innovation infrastructure
Facilitate Engineering R&D entities to adopt leading practices and gain marketing opportunities
Support Engineering R&D entrepreneurs/ Startups to reach Proof-of-Concept stage & run pilot programs and Facilitate access to investment opportunities
Foster new innovative Engineering R&D ecosystems and infuse capital via Industry-Government collaborative channels
Taking the Engineering R&D industry beyond Bengaluru to spur growth of regional economies
Boost domestic manufacturing capabilities and foster the spirit of Make in India

Enable Karnataka to contribute ~45% to IndiaΓÇÖs Engineering R&D during the policy period
Create an additional ~50,000 new jobs (direct & indirect) for skilled manpower in the Engineering R&D sector during the policy period
Grow regional economies by promoting innovation and Engineering R&D across Karnataka
Developing a research-oriented skilled talent pool and foster a knowledge economy
Attract Engineering R&D intensive investment into Karnataka
To augment capacity by bridging the Gap between Engineering/ Research Talent and IndustryΓÇÖs Technology Needs.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 by the Government of Karnataka aims to position Karnataka as the 'Destination of Choice' for Engineering R&D and contribute ~45% to India's ER&D revenue while creating ~50,000 new jobs. The policy focuses on 5 Priority Sectors: Aerospace & Defence; Auto, Auto Components & EV; Biotechnology, Pharma & Medical Devices; Semiconductors, Telecom, ESDM; and Software Products. It is structured around three pillars: Pillar A (Attracting MNC entities/GCCs/ESPs to establish or expand operations in Karnataka, especially beyond Bengaluru Urban District, through rental reimbursement, recruitment assistance, investment subsidies, an R&D innovation fund, testing/prototyping infrastructure grants, innovation labs, and public service digital innovation challenges); Pillar B (Marketing the State's ER&D advantages globally via Go & See Centers and funding for domestic/international events and whitepapers); and Pillar C (Bridging the talent gap through applied research grants in academia, future skills courses and lab setups in State Government engineering colleges, internship stipend reimbursements, and the Chief Minister Research Fellowship for PhD students). The policy is facilitated and implemented by Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 40% conditional R&D grant (up to Γé╣8 crores), 40% testing infrastructure grant (up to Γé╣50 crores), and up to Γé╣4.2 crores in establishment subsidies for Engineering R&D entities in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women employment (minimum 25% workforce requirement; 33% reservation in student skills & internships; 25% in PhD fellowships)
Regional development Beyond Bengaluru Urban District
Intellectual Property (IP) creation and registration in India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1 Eligibility Criteria
To avail the policy incentives and concessions, an entity must belong to one of the following categories:
a.i. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200 for Offering 3.5.A.1; and
a.ii. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with revenue of INR 200 crores and above for Offerings 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Offerings 3.5.C.1 & 3.5.C.3.
b. State Government Universities/ State Government UniversitiesΓÇÖ Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled in these academic institutions for Offerings 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.2 and 3.5.C.4.
Additionally, entities mentioned in Section 4.1.a.i and 4.1.a.ii should also fulfill the following eligibility criteria:
i. NATURE OF BUSINESS:
All legal entities operating in the Engineering R&D industry (Please refer Section 5, Definitions, Point VI.).
ii. LOCATION:
The entity should have registered office in Karnataka as per the Companies Act, 2013 or the Entity should be registered as per the Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Entities should either be setting up or expanding their Engineering R&D operations in Karnataka.
iii. EMPLOYMENT:
a. At least 50% of the entityΓÇÖs total qualified workforce should be based out of Karnataka, which should not include contract employees; and
b. The entity to provide at least 25% employment to women personnel, as may be otherwise stated in a specific Offering under Section 3.5, excluding Offerings 3.5.B.1 and 3.5.B.2.
ΓÇó The offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy, can be availed in addition to incentives and subsidies provided under any of the policies of Government of India.
ΓÇó Entities availing the offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy can avail incentives under any of the other policies of the Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka, excluding the incentives which are similar in nature.

1.5. Eligibility Criteria (Operational Guidelines)
An applicant should meet the following general eligibility for availing Incentives and Offerings
i. ApplicantΓÇÖs Category
Applicants are required to meet the following based on the incentives being applied for under the Engineering R&D Policy 2021
a. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion (~ INR 15477 Cr) (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200
Applicable for the following incentives:
1. Establishment of R&D Centers of Engineering R&D Entities (Incentive 3.5.A.1 of the Policy)
b. MNC Indian entities with revenue of INR 200 crores (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above
Applicable for the following incentives: (Incentive 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Incentive 3.5.C.1 & 3.5.C.3. of the Policy 2021)
2. Engineering R&D Fund to support Technological Innovation
3. R&D Infrastructure Program to create and strengthen the testing and prototyping infrastructure
4. Innovation Labs Program to encourage open innovation
5. Digital Innovation for Services Challenges
6. Applied Research in Academia Program to support industrial application of Academic Research
7. Promote Internship for Engineering Students to bridge the gap between academic skills and the needs of the Engineering R&D industry
c. ESP with revenue of INR 200 crores and above (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) Applicable for the following incentives:
1. Applied Research in Academia Program to support industrial application of Academic Research
2. Promote Internship for Engineering Students to bridge the gap between academic skills and the needs of the Engineering R&D industry
3. Chief Minister (CM) Research Fellowship Program
d. State Government Universities/ State Government UniversitiesΓÇÖ Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled in these academic institutions
Applicable for the following incentives: (For Incentive 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.2 and 3.5.C.4. of the Policy)
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Entities availing the offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of the Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka, which are similar in nature. R&D projects that have received support from another Government source will not be eligible to receive further assistance through the Engineering R&D Fund. In the software products context, system Integration (SI), maintenance, implementation of software or enhancements and testing in the context of end custom applications are not part of Engineering services they provide.

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum turnover requirements apply to corporate entities: Global revenue of USD 2 billion (~INR 15,477 Cr) and above (highest of last 3 financial years) for Offering 3.5.A.1; Revenue of INR 200 crores and above (highest of last 3 financial years) for MNC GCCs and ESPs for Offerings 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Pillar C industry-linked offerings. Must operate in one of the 5 Priority Sectors: (i) Aerospace & Defence, (ii) Auto, Auto Components & EV, (iii) Biotechnology (Bt), Pharma & Medical Devices, (iv) Semiconductors, Telecom, ESDM, (v) Software Products.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The entity should have registered office in Karnataka as per the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or should be registered as per the Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Offerings 3.5.A.1, 3.5.A.3, and 3.5.A.4 require setup beyond Bengaluru Urban District (which comprises 5 Taluks: Bengaluru North, Bengaluru North (Addl.), Bengaluru South, Bengaluru East and Anekal).

ER&D GCCs and ESPs availing benefits under the policy must be registered with KITS as an ER&D entity (one-time non-refundable registration processing fee of Rs. 10,000 + 18% GST).
special_category_benefits: Women personnel (mandatory minimum 25% employment in general; 33% women reservation in student skill training and internships; 25% women candidates in CM Research Fellowship)

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of rent for MNC Indian entities setting up new or expanding existing Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in Engineering R&D in regions beyond Bengaluru Urban District. Reimbursement is provided for a duration of 5 years or the policy validity period, up to the maximum limit, considering only technical workforce/employees.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% rental reimbursement or Γé╣1,666 per employee per month, up to Γé╣2 crores for setting up or expanding GCCs beyond Bengaluru Urban District.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online on KITS/Department website (www.itbtst.karnataka.gov.in) in response to Call for Proposal or directly to KITS after obtaining SLSWCC/SHLCC/DLSWCC approval. Evaluated by a sub-committee, ER&DRC, and approved by Executive Committee (EC), which issues a Letter of Intent valid for 3 years.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 by the Government of Karnataka aims to position Karnataka as the 'Destination of Choice' for Engineering R&D and contribute ~45% to India's ER&D revenue while creating ~50,000 new jobs. policy_details.policy_summary: The Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 by the Government of Karnataka aims to position Karnataka as the 'Destination of Choice' for Engineering R&D and contribute ~45% to India's ER&D revenue while creating ~50,000 new jobs. The policy focuses on 5 Priority Sectors: Aerospace & Defence; Auto, Auto Components & EV; Biotechnology, Pharma & Medical Devices; Semiconductors, Telecom, ESDM; and Software Products. It is structured around three pillars: Pillar A (Attracting MNC entities/GCCs/ESPs to establish or expand operations in Karnataka, especially beyond Bengaluru Urban District, through rental reimbursement, recruitment assistance, investment subsidies, an R&D innovation fund, testing/prototyping infrastructure grants, innovation labs, and public service digital innovation challenges); Pillar B (Marketing the State's ER&D advantages globally via Go & See Centers and funding for domestic/international events and whitepapers); and Pillar C (Bridging the talent gap through applied research grants in academia, future skills courses and lab setups in State Government engineering colleges, internship stipend reimbursements, and the Chief Minister Research Fellowship for PhD students). The policy is facilitated and implemented by Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM).

policy_details.policy_summary: The Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 by the Government of Karnataka aims to position Karnataka as the 'Destination of Choice' for Engineering R&D and contribute ~45% to India's ER&D revenue while creating ~50,000 new jobs. The policy focuses on 5 Priority Sectors: Aerospace & Defence; Auto, Auto Components & EV; Biotechnology, Pharma & Medical Devices; Semiconductors, Telecom, ESDM; and Software Products. It is structured around three pillars: Pillar A (Attracting MNC entities/GCCs/ESPs to establish or expand operations in Karnataka, especially beyond Bengaluru Urban District, through rental reimbursement, recruitment assistance, investment subsidies, an R&D innovation fund, testing/prototyping infrastructure grants, innovation labs, and public service digital innovation challenges); Pillar B (Marketing the State's ER&D advantages globally via Go & See Centers and funding for domestic/international events and whitepapers); and Pillar C (Bridging the talent gap through applied research grants in academia, future skills courses and lab setups in State Government engineering colleges, internship stipend reimbursements, and the Chief Minister Research Fellowship for PhD students). The policy is facilitated and implemented by Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM).

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1 Eligibility Criteria
To avail the policy incentives and concessions, an entity must belong to one of the following categories:
a.i. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200 for Offering 3.5.A.1; and
a.ii. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with revenue of INR 200 crores and above for Offerings 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Offerings 3.5.C.1 & 3.5.C.3.
b. State Government Universities/ State Government UniversitiesΓÇÖ Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled in these academic institutions for Offerings 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.2 and 3.5.C.4.
Additionally, entities mentioned in Section 4.1.a.i and 4.1.a.ii should also fulfill the following eligibility criteria:
i. NATURE OF BUSINESS:
All legal entities operating in the Engineering R&D industry (Please refer Section 5, Definitions, Point VI.).
ii. LOCATION:
The entity should have registered office in Karnataka as per the Companies Act, 2013 or the Entity should be registered as per the Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Entities should either be setting up or expanding their Engineering R&D operations in Karnataka.
iii. EMPLOYMENT:
a. At least 50% of the entityΓÇÖs total qualified workforce should be based out of Karnataka, which should not include contract employees; and
b. The entity to provide at least 25% employment to women personnel, as may be otherwise stated in a specific Offering under Section 3.5, excluding Offerings 3.5.B.1 and 3.5.B.2.
ΓÇó The offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy, can be availed in addition to incentives and subsidies provided under any of the policies of Government of India.
ΓÇó Entities availing the offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy can avail incentives under any of the other policies of the Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka, excluding the incentives which are similar in nature.

1.5. Eligibility Criteria (Operational Guidelines)
An applicant should meet the following general eligibility for availing Incentives and Offerings
i. ApplicantΓÇÖs Category
Applicants are required to meet the following based on the incentives being applied for under the Engineering R&D Policy 2021
a. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion (~ INR 15477 Cr) (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200
Applicable for the following incentives:
1. Establishment of R&D Centers of Engineering R&D Entities (Incentive 3.5.A.1 of the Policy)
b. MNC Indian entities with revenue of INR 200 crores (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above
Applicable for the following incentives: (Incentive 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Incentive 3.5.C.1 & 3.5.C.3. of the Policy 2021)
2. Engineering R&D Fund to support Technological Innovation
3. R&D Infrastructure Program to create and strengthen the testing and prototyping infrastructure
4. Innovation Labs Program to encourage open innovation
5. Digital Innovation for Services Challenges
6. Applied Research in Academia Program to support industrial application of Academic Research
7. Promote Internship for Engineering Students to bridge the gap between academic skills and the needs of the Engineering R&D industry
c. ESP with revenue of INR 200 crores and above (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) Applicable for the following incentives:
1. Applied Research in Academia Program to support industrial application of Academic Research
2. Promote Internship for Engineering Students to bridge the gap between academic skills and the needs of the Engineering R&D industry
3. Chief Minister (CM) Research Fellowship Program
d. State Government Universities/ State Government UniversitiesΓÇÖ Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled in these academic institutions
Applicable for the following incentives: (For Incentive 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.2 and 3.5.C.4. of the Policy)
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Entities availing the offerings under Section 3.5 of this policy cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of the Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka, which are similar in nature. R&D projects that have received support from another Government source will not be eligible to receive further assistance through the Engineering R&D Fund. In the software products context, system Integration (SI), maintenance, implementation of software or enhancements and testing in the context of end custom applications are not part of Engineering services they provide.

policy_goals: Accelerating KarnatakaΓÇÖs growth towards leaving a footprint in the Global Engineering R&D landscape, promoting the State as the ΓÇÿEngineering R&D Destination of ChoiceΓÇÖ and transforming into a vibrant ΓÇÿKnowledge EconomyΓÇÖ.

Support and strengthen the availability of skilled Engineering R&D human capital
Establish and offer access to advanced testing, prototyping and other allied innovation infrastructure
Facilitate Engineering R&D entities to adopt leading practices and gain marketing opportunities
Support Engineering R&D entrepreneurs/ Startups to reach Proof-of-Concept stage & run pilot programs and Facilitate access to investment opportunities
Foster new innovative Engineering R&D ecosystems and infuse capital via Industry-Government collaborative channels
Taking the Engineering R&D industry beyond Bengaluru to spur growth of regional economies
Boost domestic manufacturing capabilities and foster the spirit of Make in India
Promote IP Creation, Registration and Retention in Karnataka
Enable Karnataka to contribute ~45% to IndiaΓÇÖs Engineering R&D during the policy period
Create an additional ~50,000 new jobs (direct & indirect) for skilled manpower in the Engineering R&D sector during the policy period
Grow regional economies by promoting innovation and Engineering R&D across Karnataka
Developing a research-oriented skilled talent pool and foster a knowledge economy
Attract Engineering R&D intensive investment into Karnataka
To augment capacity by bridging the Gap between Engineering/ Research Talent and IndustryΓÇÖs Technology Needs.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 by the Government of Karnataka aims to position Karnataka as the 'Destination of Choice' for Engineering R&D and contribute ~45% to India's ER&D revenue while creating ~50,000 new jobs. The policy focuses on 5 Priority Sectors: Aerospace & Defence; Auto, Auto Components & EV; Biotechnology, Pharma & Medical Devices; Semiconductors, Telecom, ESDM; and Software Products. It is structured around three pillars: Pillar A (Attracting MNC entities/GCCs/ESPs to establish or expand operations in Karnataka, especially beyond Bengaluru Urban District, through rental reimbursement, recruitment assistance, investment subsidies, an R&D innovation fund, testing/prototyping infrastructure grants, innovation labs, and public service digital innovation challenges); Pillar B (Marketing the State's ER&D advantages globally via Go & See Centers and funding for domestic/international events and whitepapers); and Pillar C (Bridging the talent gap through applied research grants in academia, future skills courses and lab setups in State Government engineering colleges, internship stipend reimbursements, and the Chief Minister Research Fellowship for PhD students). The policy is facilitated and implemented by Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM).

Create additional employment opportunities (direct and indirect) of 60,000 persons during the policy period of 5 years.
To develop Karnataka as the Aerospace & Defence manufacturing hub including MRO and space applications for both Indian market and exports.

policy_goals: Attract investments to the tune of INR 45,000 crore (USD 6 Bn) in the Aerospace & Defence sector during the policy period of 5 years.
Create additional employment opportunities (direct and indirect) of 60,000 persons during the policy period of 5 years.
To develop Karnataka as the Aerospace & Defence manufacturing hub including MRO and space applications for both Indian market and exports.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme addresses the lack of accessible testing infrastructure and skilled manpower in the domestic aerospace and defence sector. It provides financial assistance of 25% up to INR 50 Crore to private sector entities for setting up common Defence Testing Infrastructure (DTI) and certification facilities across 16+ specified technical verticals (including drones, EMI/EMC, radar, ballistic, environmental, and metallographic testing). Additionally, it promotes skill development by subsidizing 50% of in-plant training stipends up to INR 10,000 per month per trainee for up to 50 trainees per industry annually.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 25% capital assistance up to Γé╣50 Crore for setting up common Defence Testing Infrastructure and 50% stipend subsidy up to Γé╣10,000/month for in-plant trainee skilling.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
The policy aims at setting up Defence Testing Infrastructure (required for defence and aerospace related production), as a common facility under private sector with Government assistance. The Scheme would provide financial assistance to the private sector for setting up testing and certification facilities for manufacturers of defence equipment/systems.
For in-plant training provided by the industries, the cost of training would be subsidized by way of offering stipend up to 50% of the cost of training subject to a limit of INR 10,000/ per month per trainee. This incentive shall be available for a maximum of 50 trainees per industry per annum. The benefit shall be available for 1000 candidates per annum.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Testing infrastructure must cover verticals such as Drones/UAVs/RPAs, EMI/EMC Testing, Rubber Testing, Radiated Noise and Shock, Electronic Warfare, Software Testing, Specialized Test-Driving Tracks, Ship Motion, Ballistic and Blast Testing, Environmental Test Facilities, Physical/chemical/metallographic testing, Optical/mechanical surface properties, Audits/approvals of heat/surface treatment, upgrading existing facilities to OEM approvals, or testing of system integrators/sub-assemblies.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Encouraged within Aerospace & Defence parks in Karnataka.

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015

policy_goals: To achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in the State

To position Karnataka in a sustained growth path in the field of agricultural and allied sectors through global technologies and innovative tools, by creating enabling frameworks and state of the art infrastructure facilities, thereby generating higher returns to farming communities
To make Karnataka as the most sought after investment destination for the agribusiness and food processing with focussed attention and handholding
To provide more and more opportunities for the agribusiness and food processing sector, thereby generating large scale employment in rural and semi urban areas of the State
To give special thrust for skill development
To create conducive environment for optimal utilization of agriculture and allied sector resources for the sustainable industrial development
To increase the value addition and reduce wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
To maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities
To create necessary supply chain like transportation, warehouses, and cold storage in the agro processing sector
To increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
To extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunity in rural area
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 aims to increase agro-processing in Karnataka from 3% to 10% by 2020 and 25% by 2025, thereby reducing post-harvest wastage, generating rural employment, and increasing farm returns. The policy declares the entire State of Karnataka as a single zone so that fiscal incentives and concessions apply equally across all districts irrespective of promoter or zonal classification. It covers a wide range of activities including warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics, export, processing and handling of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, and organic produce, as well as R&D, biotechnology, food testing labs, irradiation units, food-grade packaging, Horticulture Hubs, Food Parks, Sea Food Parks, and Spice Parks. Key incentives include a 35% Investment Promotion Subsidy (up to Rs. 65 Lakhs) for MSMEs, 6% interest subsidy on term loans for Micro enterprises for 7 years, 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges (Rs. 0.50 per Rs. 1000), 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, 100% entry tax exemption (3 to 7 years), capital subsidy up to Rs. 200 Lakhs for Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), 100% electricity tariff tax exemption for 8 years, net VAT reimbursement (60% to 80% for 5 years), 50% subsidy for technology adoption from national labs for MSMEs, and a 10-year APMC market fee exemption for new processing and export units.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 35% capital subsidy up to Γé╣65 lakhs for MSMEs, 60%-80% net VAT reimbursement for 5 years, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, and 100% stamp duty & land conversion fee waiver across all of Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Department of Horticulture, Department of Animal Husbandry & Fisheries, Department of Co-operation, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Export-oriented agribusiness units (Sanitary & Phytosanitary Facilitation Cell)
Sea Food Parks and Spice Parks

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
Scope and Coverage: Policy shall cover the warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics related to agribusiness, export, processing, handling, storage of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, organic produce, research for varietal development, bio-technology, bio-informatics, food testing laboratories, quality certifications in entire value chain, tissue culture laboratories, seed processing units, irradiation units, food-grade packaging material units and preservatives, horticulture hub, food parks, sea food parks and spice park.

Value of Eligible Fixed Assets (VFA): Shall mean the total investment made on land, building, plant and machinery and such other equipments like reefer vans, material handling equipment, weighing machines, diesel generator sets, boilers, equipment required for research & development including testing laboratories and all other connected equipments. Whatever is not defined / mentioned here will have the same meaning as given in the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2014-19 for all purposes and also for calculating the eligibility criteria, claiming incentives and benefits.

Declaring the entire State as Single Zone: In order to give fillip to the sector in all parts of the State, the entire State has been classified as the single zone and the incentives and concessions proposed will be applicable equally in all parts of the State.

Annexure - III: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES
As per the MSMED Act, 2006 manufacturing enterprises have been defined based on the investment in Plant and Machinery and classified into:
Micro Enterprises: Investment up to Rs.25 Lakhs
Small Enterprise: Investment above Rs.25 Lakhs and up to Rs.500 Lakhs
Medium Enterprises: Investment above Rs.500 Lakhs and up to Rs.1000 Lakhs
As per the MSMED Act, 2006 service enterprises have been defined based on the investment in equipment and classified into:
Micro Enterprises: Investment up to Rs.10 Lakhs
Small Enterprise: Investment above Rs.10 Lakhs and up to Rs.200 Lakhs
Medium Enterprises: Investment above Rs.200 Lakhs and up to Rs.500 Lakhs
'A' CATEGORY ENTERPRISES: Projects with an investment in fixed assets above Rs.10 Crores and up to Rs.75 Crores.
'B' CATEGORY ENTERPRISES: Projects with an investment in fixed assets above Rs.75 Crores and up to Rs.150 Crores.
'C' CATEGORY ENTERPRISES: Projects with an investment in fixed assets above Rs.150 Crores.
'D' CATEGORY ENTERPRISES: The first two agro food processing enterprises in a taluka providing a minimum direct employment of 100 persons with a minimum investment of Rs.150 Crores.

ΓÇó Masala making without Cold Process Grinding, powder of Chilly, Turmeric, Masala, Spices, Curry, Sambar, Papad etc., except those having FSSAI certification.

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015

policy_goals: To achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in the State

To position Karnataka in a sustained growth path in the field of agricultural and allied sectors through global technologies and innovative tools, by creating enabling frameworks and state of the art infrastructure facilities, thereby generating higher returns to farming communities
To make Karnataka as the most sought after investment destination for the agribusiness and food processing with focussed attention and handholding
To provide more and more opportunities for the agribusiness and food processing sector, thereby generating large scale employment in rural and semi urban areas of the State
To give special thrust for skill development
To create conducive environment for optimal utilization of agriculture and allied sector resources for the sustainable industrial development
To increase the value addition and reduce wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
To maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities
To create necessary supply chain like transportation, warehouses, and cold storage in the agro processing sector
To increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
To extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunity in rural area
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 aims to increase agro-processing in Karnataka from 3% to 10% by 2020 and 25% by 2025, thereby reducing post-harvest wastage, generating rural employment, and increasing farm returns. The policy declares the entire State of Karnataka as a single zone so that fiscal incentives and concessions apply equally across all districts irrespective of promoter or zonal classification. It covers a wide range of activities including warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics, export, processing and handling of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, and organic produce, as well as R&D, biotechnology, food testing labs, irradiation units, food-grade packaging, Horticulture Hubs, Food Parks, Sea Food Parks, and Spice Parks. Key incentives include a 35% Investment Promotion Subsidy (up to Rs. 65 Lakhs) for MSMEs, 6% interest subsidy on term loans for Micro enterprises for 7 years, 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges (Rs. 0.50 per Rs. 1000), 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, 100% entry tax exemption (3 to 7 years), capital subsidy up to Rs. 200 Lakhs for Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), 100% electricity tariff tax exemption for 8 years, net VAT reimbursement (60% to 80% for 5 years), 50% subsidy for technology adoption from national labs for MSMEs, and a 10-year APMC market fee exemption for new processing and export units.

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015

policy_goals: To achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in the State

To position Karnataka in a sustained growth path in the field of agricultural and allied sectors through global technologies and innovative tools, by creating enabling frameworks and state of the art infrastructure facilities, thereby generating higher returns to farming communities
To make Karnataka as the most sought after investment destination for the agribusiness and food processing with focussed attention and handholding
To provide more and more opportunities for the agribusiness and food processing sector, thereby generating large scale employment in rural and semi urban areas of the State
To give special thrust for skill development
To create conducive environment for optimal utilization of agriculture and allied sector resources for the sustainable industrial development
To increase the value addition and reduce wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
To maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities
To create necessary supply chain like transportation, warehouses, and cold storage in the agro processing sector
To increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
To extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunity in rural area
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 aims to increase agro-processing in Karnataka from 3% to 10% by 2020 and 25% by 2025, thereby reducing post-harvest wastage, generating rural employment, and increasing farm returns. The policy declares the entire State of Karnataka as a single zone so that fiscal incentives and concessions apply equally across all districts irrespective of promoter or zonal classification. It covers a wide range of activities including warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics, export, processing and handling of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, and organic produce, as well as R&D, biotechnology, food testing labs, irradiation units, food-grade packaging, Horticulture Hubs, Food Parks, Sea Food Parks, and Spice Parks. Key incentives include a 35% Investment Promotion Subsidy (up to Rs. 65 Lakhs) for MSMEs, 6% interest subsidy on term loans for Micro enterprises for 7 years, 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges (Rs. 0.50 per Rs. 1000), 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, 100% entry tax exemption (3 to 7 years), capital subsidy up to Rs. 200 Lakhs for Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), 100% electricity tariff tax exemption for 8 years, net VAT reimbursement (60% to 80% for 5 years), 50% subsidy for technology adoption from national labs for MSMEs, and a 10-year APMC market fee exemption for new processing and export units.

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015
incentive_name: Subsidy for setting up Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP)

policy_goals: To achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in the State

To position Karnataka in a sustained growth path in the field of agricultural and allied sectors through global technologies and innovative tools, by creating enabling frameworks and state of the art infrastructure facilities, thereby generating higher returns to farming communities
To make Karnataka as the most sought after investment destination for the agribusiness and food processing with focussed attention and handholding
To provide more and more opportunities for the agribusiness and food processing sector, thereby generating large scale employment in rural and semi urban areas of the State
To give special thrust for skill development
To create conducive environment for optimal utilization of agriculture and allied sector resources for the sustainable industrial development
To increase the value addition and reduce wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
To maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities
To create necessary supply chain like transportation, warehouses, and cold storage in the agro processing sector
To increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
To extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunity in rural area
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 aims to increase agro-processing in Karnataka from 3% to 10% by 2020 and 25% by 2025, thereby reducing post-harvest wastage, generating rural employment, and increasing farm returns. The policy declares the entire State of Karnataka as a single zone so that fiscal incentives and concessions apply equally across all districts irrespective of promoter or zonal classification. It covers a wide range of activities including warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics, export, processing and handling of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, and organic produce, as well as R&D, biotechnology, food testing labs, irradiation units, food-grade packaging, Horticulture Hubs, Food Parks, Sea Food Parks, and Spice Parks. Key incentives include a 35% Investment Promotion Subsidy (up to Rs. 65 Lakhs) for MSMEs, 6% interest subsidy on term loans for Micro enterprises for 7 years, 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges (Rs. 0.50 per Rs. 1000), 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, 100% entry tax exemption (3 to 7 years), capital subsidy up to Rs. 200 Lakhs for Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), 100% electricity tariff tax exemption for 8 years, net VAT reimbursement (60% to 80% for 5 years), 50% subsidy for technology adoption from national labs for MSMEs, and a 10-year APMC market fee exemption for new processing and export units.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 35% capital subsidy up to Γé╣65 lakhs for MSMEs, 60%-80% net VAT reimbursement for 5 years, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, and 100% stamp duty & land conversion fee waiver across all of Karnataka.

parent_policy_name: Karnataka Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics - Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 3.0 (2024-2029)
policy_name: Karnataka Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029)

policy_goals: Strive to make Karnataka a leader in emerging technologies such as AI, AR/VR, within the AVGC-XR sector
Transform Karnataka into a Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR related skills, attracting students and professionals to Karnataka for education and career development in this sector.
Establish emerging clusters, in addition to Bengaluru, as hubs for AVGC-XR, to distribute economic benefits more evenly across the state.
Incorporate sustainability and inclusivity in the AVGC-XR industry by 2029. Embed ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) criteria into the AVGC-XR sector's operational ethos.
Establish Karnataka as a pioneering state in IPP within the AVGC-XR sector where strong legislative frameworks foster a secure and thriving ecosystem for creators, investors, and consumers.

Position India as a global leader in the AVGC-XR sector by harnessing and amplifying the country's rich cultural heritage, developing immersive experiences representing India's diverse traditions, stories, art forms and elevating them to international acclaim and fostering cultural exchange.
Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 200 AVGC-XR companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile.

By 2029, achieve a 30% increase in operational efficiencies, a 20% boost in creative output, and a 25% expansion in digital marketing reach in the AVGC-XR sector, enabled by targeted investments in digital infrastructure, skill building programs and regulatory reforms.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the AVGC-XR sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 50,000 individuals in AVGC-XR specific and standardized skills.
Aim for exports to constitute at least 80% of the sector's total revenue, thereby also positively impacting the state's balance of trade.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029) is the third 5-year policy by the Government of Karnataka aimed at making the state a global innovation hub for the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector. With a total budget outlay of Rs. 150 crore over 5 years, the policy focuses on six strategic pillars: skill development, sustainable infrastructure (such as an AVGC-XR Park SEZ, Centres of Excellence, and Digital Art Centers), empowering startups and MSMEs, global market access, financial incentives, and multiplatform AVGC-XR products. Financial incentives include skill development and job creation subsidies (50% course fee reimbursement up to Rs. 7.5 Lakhs and PF/ESI reimbursement up to Rs. 12 Lakhs), an Early-Stage Startup Support Program (reimbursements for marketing, leasing, server, and compliance costs), Infrastructure subsidies (20% capital subsidy on IT hardware up to Rs. 20 Lakhs and 20% rental subsidy up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), IP Creation and Protection support (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 20 Lakhs for International IP and Rs. 5 Lakhs for Domestic IP), Production Grants (20% reimbursement of qualified expenditure ranging from Rs. 5 Lakhs for gaming up to Rs. 1 Crore for international productions), Quality Assurance certification support (30% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), and International Market Access trade show support (40% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs per year). Additionally, it provides ecosystem support via Technology Business Incubators (up to Rs. 10 Crore funding per TBI) and venture capital via KITVEN Fund-4 (Rs. 20 Crore corpus).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% production grants (capped up to Γé╣1 Crore for international productions and Γé╣50 Lakhs for domestic films/VFX), 50% IP filing reimbursement up to Γé╣20 Lakhs, and 20% IT hardware capital subsidy up to Γé╣20 Lakhs for AVGC-XR companies in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Export-oriented units (International Productions and Global Market Access)
Regional cluster development beyond Bengaluru (Mangalore, Mysore, Hubli/Dharwad)
Multi-platform Gaming and mobile-based AI tools
ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) sustainability and inclusivity

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form. There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of "Managing Director, KITS". If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka IT-BT company, there is no charge. Instead, the company may attach a copy of the Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate along with its application. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are not a part of interactive games and are excluded from the AVGC-XR sector definition. Contract employees are not included in the 50% Karnataka workforce calculation. Companies already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Company must employ at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract employees). All applications/sanctions are restricted to the proposed numbers on a first-cum-first-serve basis within the overall budget limit of Rs. 150 crores for 5 years. Mandatory documents include audited financial statements for the last one year (or detailed project reports with 3-year financial projections for newly incorporated companies) and incorporation/registration certificates.

parent_policy_name: Karnataka Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics - Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 3.0 (2024-2029)
policy_name: Karnataka Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029)

policy_goals: Strive to make Karnataka a leader in emerging technologies such as AI, AR/VR, within the AVGC-XR sector
Transform Karnataka into a Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR related skills, attracting students and professionals to Karnataka for education and career development in this sector.
Establish emerging clusters, in addition to Bengaluru, as hubs for AVGC-XR, to distribute economic benefits more evenly across the state.
Incorporate sustainability and inclusivity in the AVGC-XR industry by 2029. Embed ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) criteria into the AVGC-XR sector's operational ethos.
Establish Karnataka as a pioneering state in IPP within the AVGC-XR sector where strong legislative frameworks foster a secure and thriving ecosystem for creators, investors, and consumers.

Position India as a global leader in the AVGC-XR sector by harnessing and amplifying the country's rich cultural heritage, developing immersive experiences representing India's diverse traditions, stories, art forms and elevating them to international acclaim and fostering cultural exchange.
Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 200 AVGC-XR companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile.

By 2029, achieve a 30% increase in operational efficiencies, a 20% boost in creative output, and a 25% expansion in digital marketing reach in the AVGC-XR sector, enabled by targeted investments in digital infrastructure, skill building programs and regulatory reforms.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the AVGC-XR sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 50,000 individuals in AVGC-XR specific and standardized skills.
Aim for exports to constitute at least 80% of the sector's total revenue, thereby also positively impacting the state's balance of trade.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029) is the third 5-year policy by the Government of Karnataka aimed at making the state a global innovation hub for the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector. With a total budget outlay of Rs. 150 crore over 5 years, the policy focuses on six strategic pillars: skill development, sustainable infrastructure (such as an AVGC-XR Park SEZ, Centres of Excellence, and Digital Art Centers), empowering startups and MSMEs, global market access, financial incentives, and multiplatform AVGC-XR products. Financial incentives include skill development and job creation subsidies (50% course fee reimbursement up to Rs. 7.5 Lakhs and PF/ESI reimbursement up to Rs. 12 Lakhs), an Early-Stage Startup Support Program (reimbursements for marketing, leasing, server, and compliance costs), Infrastructure subsidies (20% capital subsidy on IT hardware up to Rs. 20 Lakhs and 20% rental subsidy up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), IP Creation and Protection support (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 20 Lakhs for International IP and Rs. 5 Lakhs for Domestic IP), Production Grants (20% reimbursement of qualified expenditure ranging from Rs. 5 Lakhs for gaming up to Rs. 1 Crore for international productions), Quality Assurance certification support (30% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), and International Market Access trade show support (40% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs per year). Additionally, it provides ecosystem support via Technology Business Incubators (up to Rs. 10 Crore funding per TBI) and venture capital via KITVEN Fund-4 (Rs. 20 Crore corpus).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% production grants (capped up to Γé╣1 Crore for international productions and Γé╣50 Lakhs for domestic films/VFX), 50% IP filing reimbursement up to Γé╣20 Lakhs, and 20% IT hardware capital subsidy up to Γé╣20 Lakhs for AVGC-XR companies in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Export-oriented units (International Productions and Global Market Access)

Multi-platform Gaming and mobile-based AI tools
ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) sustainability and inclusivity

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form. There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of "Managing Director, KITS". If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka IT-BT company, there is no charge. Instead, the company may attach a copy of the Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate along with its application. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are not a part of interactive games and are excluded from the AVGC-XR sector definition. Contract employees are not included in the 50% Karnataka workforce calculation. Companies already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Company must employ at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract employees). All applications/sanctions are restricted to the proposed numbers on a first-cum-first-serve basis within the overall budget limit of Rs. 150 crores for 5 years. Mandatory documents include audited financial statements for the last one year (or detailed project reports with 3-year financial projections for newly incorporated companies) and incorporation/registration certificates.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Operating in Karnataka; emerging clusters targeted include Mangalore, Mysore, and Hubli/Dharwad in addition to Bengaluru.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961, and registered with KITS as a KAVGC Company (one-time fee of INR 10,000, waived if already registered as a Karnataka IT-BT company).

incentive_details.description: Capital subsidy providing reimbursement for the one-time purchase of new IT hardware, gaming, and data storage equipment from Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) or their authorized suppliers/resellers/distributors for KAVGC companies.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% capital subsidy on IT hardware purchases, capped at Γé╣20 Lakhs per company.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Application Form for Infrastructure along with KAVGC Registration Certificate, Proof of Company Registration, valid GST invoices/bills from OEMs/authorized suppliers, Declaration of Equipment Status, and Statutory Declaration.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: capped at INR 20 Lakhs limited to up to 5 sanction per company during the policy period
quantified_benefits.conditions: Equipment must be new (not refurbished or pre-owned), purchased one-time from OEMs or authorized distributors with valid GST invoice. Software, licenses, leasing, and annual subscriptions are not eligible.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of cost incurred for one-time purchase of IT hardware, gaming, and data storage equipment from OEMs.
quantified_benefits.source_text: IT Infrastructure: Up to 20% of the cost incurred, capped at INR 20 Lakhs limited to up to 5 sanction per company during the policy period. Purchases of IT Hardware equipment applicable for an AVGC-XR company. Software and licenses are not eligible.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New and existing KAVGC companies

incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Approval Committee
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: New and existing KAVGC companies operating in the AVGC-XR sectors. Equipment must be purchased from OEMs or authorized suppliers only, and must not be used, refurbished, or certified pre-owned. Software, licenses, equipment leasing, and annual subscriptions are excluded.

There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of "Managing Director, KITS". If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka IT-BT company, there is no charge. Instead, the company may attach a copy of the Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate along with its application. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are not a part of interactive games and are excluded from the AVGC-XR sector definition. Contract employees are not included in the 50% Karnataka workforce calculation. Companies already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Company must employ at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract employees). All applications/sanctions are restricted to the proposed numbers on a first-cum-first-serve basis within the overall budget limit of Rs. 150 crores for 5 years. Mandatory documents include audited financial statements for the last one year (or detailed project reports with 3-year financial projections for newly incorporated companies) and incorporation/registration certificates.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Operating in Karnataka; emerging clusters targeted include Mangalore, Mysore, and Hubli/Dharwad in addition to Bengaluru.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961, and registered with KITS as a KAVGC Company (one-time fee of INR 10,000, waived if already registered as a Karnataka IT-BT company).

policy_goals: Strive to make Karnataka a leader in emerging technologies such as AI, AR/VR, within the AVGC-XR sector
Transform Karnataka into a Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR related skills, attracting students and professionals to Karnataka for education and career development in this sector.
Establish emerging clusters, in addition to Bengaluru, as hubs for AVGC-XR, to distribute economic benefits more evenly across the state.
Incorporate sustainability and inclusivity in the AVGC-XR industry by 2029. Embed ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) criteria into the AVGC-XR sector's operational ethos.
Establish Karnataka as a pioneering state in IPP within the AVGC-XR sector where strong legislative frameworks foster a secure and thriving ecosystem for creators, investors, and consumers.

Position India as a global leader in the AVGC-XR sector by harnessing and amplifying the country's rich cultural heritage, developing immersive experiences representing India's diverse traditions, stories, art forms and elevating them to international acclaim and fostering cultural exchange.
Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 200 AVGC-XR companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile.

By 2029, achieve a 30% increase in operational efficiencies, a 20% boost in creative output, and a 25% expansion in digital marketing reach in the AVGC-XR sector, enabled by targeted investments in digital infrastructure, skill building programs and regulatory reforms.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the AVGC-XR sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 50,000 individuals in AVGC-XR specific and standardized skills.
Aim for exports to constitute at least 80% of the sector's total revenue, thereby also positively impacting the state's balance of trade.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029) is the third 5-year policy by the Government of Karnataka aimed at making the state a global innovation hub for the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector. With a total budget outlay of Rs. 150 crore over 5 years, the policy focuses on six strategic pillars: skill development, sustainable infrastructure (such as an AVGC-XR Park SEZ, Centres of Excellence, and Digital Art Centers), empowering startups and MSMEs, global market access, financial incentives, and multiplatform AVGC-XR products. Financial incentives include skill development and job creation subsidies (50% course fee reimbursement up to Rs. 7.5 Lakhs and PF/ESI reimbursement up to Rs. 12 Lakhs), an Early-Stage Startup Support Program (reimbursements for marketing, leasing, server, and compliance costs), Infrastructure subsidies (20% capital subsidy on IT hardware up to Rs. 20 Lakhs and 20% rental subsidy up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), IP Creation and Protection support (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 20 Lakhs for International IP and Rs. 5 Lakhs for Domestic IP), Production Grants (20% reimbursement of qualified expenditure ranging from Rs. 5 Lakhs for gaming up to Rs. 1 Crore for international productions), Quality Assurance certification support (30% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs), and International Market Access trade show support (40% up to Rs. 5 Lakhs per year). Additionally, it provides ecosystem support via Technology Business Incubators (up to Rs. 10 Crore funding per TBI) and venture capital via KITVEN Fund-4 (Rs. 20 Crore corpus).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% production grants (capped up to Γé╣1 Crore for international productions and Γé╣50 Lakhs for domestic films/VFX), 50% IP filing reimbursement up to Γé╣20 Lakhs, and 20% IT hardware capital subsidy up to Γé╣20 Lakhs for AVGC-XR companies in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Export-oriented units (International Productions and Global Market Access)
Regional cluster development beyond Bengaluru (Mangalore, Mysore, Hubli/Dharwad)
Multi-platform Gaming and mobile-based AI tools
ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) sustainability and inclusivity

policy_goals: Strive to make Karnataka a leader in emerging technologies such as AI, AR/VR, within the AVGC-XR sector
Transform Karnataka into a Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR related skills, attracting students and professionals to Karnataka for education and career development in this sector.
Establish emerging clusters, in addition to Bengaluru, as hubs for AVGC-XR, to distribute economic benefits more evenly across the state.

Aim for exports to constitute at least 80% of the sector's total revenue, thereby also positively impacting the state's balance of trade.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-2029) is the third 5-year policy by the Government of Karnataka aimed at making the state a global innovation hub for the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector. policy_goals: To emerge as the top Biotechnology destination in the world with focus for sustainable, safe, and secure future.
Grow Karnataka's bioeconomy to $100 billion by 2030, registering a 19% CAGR and increasing Karnataka's share to one-third of India's bioeconomy.

Elevate biopharma's contribution to $30 billion, bio-agricultural segment to $15 billion, bio-industrial domain to $30 billion, and R&D, marine biotechnology, and bioinformatics services (including AI and Deep Tech) to $15 billion by FY2030.
Strengthen educational institutions for skilling in biotechnology, not just from an employability perspective but also from an entrepreneurship perspective.
Attempt to streamline biotech and other related regulations to ease business establishment and clarity in operations thereby promoting more investments.

Support biomanufacturing for products aligning with health, climate, and energy goals, enhancing food security and the state's bioeconomy, making Karnataka as the next global hub for biomanufacturing.

Continue to support the robust startup ecosystem with funding, incubation, and mentorship for early-stage biotech ventures; and acceleration, grow out facilities and market access through preferential procurement of local products for mid-stage biotech ventures.

Enable preferential government procurement norms for Made-in-Karnataka Biotech Products & Services and facilitate quick use of products developed to treat rare diseases and med/health-tech innovation through Regulatory Sandbox Mechanism.

Continue to support R&D and Commercialization efforts in Emerging Technology Areas of Biotechnology, aiming to make Karnataka a Global Hub for Genomics and Molecular Biology innovations in materials, micro and nanotechnologies for Health, Food, and Energy Security.

Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 300 Biotechnology companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile by providing a lucrative package of incentives and subsidies.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the Biotechnology sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 20,000 individuals in Biotechnology specific and standardized skills.

policy_name: Fiscal Incentives for MSMEs (Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029)

policy_goals: To emerge as the top Biotechnology destination in the world with focus for sustainable, safe, and secure future.
Grow Karnataka's bioeconomy to $100 billion by 2030, registering a 19% CAGR and increasing Karnataka's share to one-third of India's bioeconomy.

Elevate biopharma's contribution to $30 billion, bio-agricultural segment to $15 billion, bio-industrial domain to $30 billion, and R&D, marine biotechnology, and bioinformatics services (including AI and Deep Tech) to $15 billion by FY2030.
Strengthen educational institutions for skilling in biotechnology, not just from an employability perspective but also from an entrepreneurship perspective.
Attempt to streamline biotech and other related regulations to ease business establishment and clarity in operations thereby promoting more investments.

Support biomanufacturing for products aligning with health, climate, and energy goals, enhancing food security and the state's bioeconomy, making Karnataka as the next global hub for biomanufacturing.

Continue to support the robust startup ecosystem with funding, incubation, and mentorship for early-stage biotech ventures; and acceleration, grow out facilities and market access through preferential procurement of local products for mid-stage biotech ventures.

Enable preferential government procurement norms for Made-in-Karnataka Biotech Products & Services and facilitate quick use of products developed to treat rare diseases and med/health-tech innovation through Regulatory Sandbox Mechanism.

Continue to support R&D and Commercialization efforts in Emerging Technology Areas of Biotechnology, aiming to make Karnataka a Global Hub for Genomics and Molecular Biology innovations in materials, micro and nanotechnologies for Health, Food, and Energy Security.

Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 300 Biotechnology companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile by providing a lucrative package of incentives and subsidies.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the Biotechnology sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 20,000 individuals in Biotechnology specific and standardized skills.
policy_details.policy_summary: This sub-policy under the Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029 offers a comprehensive suite of fiscal incentives and concessions to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the biotechnology sector in Karnataka. policy_details.benefit_headline: 6% interest subsidy on loans, 100% stamp duty & land conversion fee waiver, 50% prototyping support up to Γé╣50 Lakhs, and 75% patent reimbursement for Biotech MSMEs.

policy_goals: To emerge as the top Biotechnology destination in the world with focus for sustainable, safe, and secure future.
Grow Karnataka's bioeconomy to $100 billion by 2030, registering a 19% CAGR and increasing Karnataka's share to one-third of India's bioeconomy.

Elevate biopharma's contribution to $30 billion, bio-agricultural segment to $15 billion, bio-industrial domain to $30 billion, and R&D, marine biotechnology, and bioinformatics services (including AI and Deep Tech) to $15 billion by FY2030.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4. General Eligibility Criteria
a. Applicant should be registered as a Karnataka based biotech company under the Karnataka Biotechnology policy 2024-2029
b. Applicant should produce KYC (Know Your Customer). KYC includes PAN, AADHAAR, UDYOG AADHAAR, GST certificate, Letter from Bank with account details including RTGS, and Cancelled Cheque. If GST is not applicable, applicant to declare that they do not fall under GST.
c. All rules and regulations are followed as per guidance from the Government of India, case basis, time to time.
d. Currency rate conversion should be as per Bank Certificate.
e. All expense certificates should be CA certified.

4.1. For a Startup
a. The Startup should be working towards innovation/ improvement of existing products, services and processes and should have the potential to generate employment/ create wealth.
b. It is not formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business already in existence.
c. An entity will be considered as a Startup on fulfilling the below mentioned conditions defined by Government of Karnataka which is in line with the definition of Government of India (GoI) notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02.2019). However, the policy will adopt the amendments and changes made to the definition by GoI from time to time.
a. The Startup should be incorporated as a private limited company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under Section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008) in Karnataka.
b. Turnover: Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/registration should not have exceeded Γé╣100 crores.
c. Tenure for startups: An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
d. The entity should be working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or if it is a scalable business model with a high potential of employment generation or wealth creation.
d. Exclusions: A company, in order to qualify as a startup under this policy, should not have been:
a. Formed by demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence
b. A Section 8 company or Trust/Association/Society
c. Public-private partnership company/firm
d. A franchisee of an existing business or promoted/sponsored/related to an industrial group in the state
e. A subsidiary of a firm in the state other than the startup itself
e. Inclusions: A company shall qualify as a startup if it is a:
a. Subsidiary of a startup
b. Combined entity formed by merger of startups/subsidiaries of a startup
f. Exit Clause: A startup will cease to receive benefits under this policy on completion of ten years from the date of its incorporation/registration or if its turnover for any previous year exceeds Γé╣100 Crore.

Elevate biopharma's contribution to $30 billion, bio-agricultural segment to $15 billion, bio-industrial domain to $30 billion, and R&D, marine biotechnology, and bioinformatics services (including AI and Deep Tech) to $15 billion by FY2030.
Strengthen educational institutions for skilling in biotechnology, not just from an employability perspective but also from an entrepreneurship perspective.
Attempt to streamline biotech and other related regulations to ease business establishment and clarity in operations thereby promoting more investments.

Support biomanufacturing for products aligning with health, climate, and energy goals, enhancing food security and the state's bioeconomy, making Karnataka as the next global hub for biomanufacturing.

Continue to support the robust startup ecosystem with funding, incubation, and mentorship for early-stage biotech ventures; and acceleration, grow out facilities and market access through preferential procurement of local products for mid-stage biotech ventures.

Enable preferential government procurement norms for Made-in-Karnataka Biotech Products & Services and facilitate quick use of products developed to treat rare diseases and med/health-tech innovation through Regulatory Sandbox Mechanism.

Continue to support R&D and Commercialization efforts in Emerging Technology Areas of Biotechnology, aiming to make Karnataka a Global Hub for Genomics and Molecular Biology innovations in materials, micro and nanotechnologies for Health, Food, and Energy Security.

Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 300 Biotechnology companies, including 50 that are particularly innovative or high-profile by providing a lucrative package of incentives and subsidies.

Create awareness among youth about the opportunities encompassing both education and employment prospects within the Biotechnology sector and create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the sector by 2029, with a focus on roles requiring specialized skills in emerging technologies; partner with 200 or more educational institutions and industry, including MOOC platforms, to train at least 20,000 individuals in Biotechnology specific and standardized skills.
policy_details.policy_summary: This sub-policy under the Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029 provides fiscal incentives and concessions specifically tailored for Biotechnology Startups and Biotechnology Incubation/Acceleration Centres in Karnataka. The objective is to lower the capital and operational burden on early-stage biotech ventures, enabling them to overcome the 'valley of death', protect intellectual property, achieve quality certifications, access international markets, and scale operations. It offers 100% SGST reimbursement for startups outside Bengaluru Urban, 30% marketing cost reimbursement, 100% patent cost reimbursement, 50% quality certification reimbursement, and up to Γé╣1 Crore capital grants for setting up or expanding biotech incubation/acceleration centres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4. General Eligibility Criteria
a. Applicant should be registered as a Karnataka based biotech company under the Karnataka Biotechnology policy 2024-2029
b. Applicant should produce KYC (Know Your Customer). KYC includes PAN, AADHAAR, UDYOG AADHAAR, GST certificate, Letter from Bank with account details including RTGS, and Cancelled Cheque. If GST is not applicable, applicant to declare that they do not fall under GST.
c. All rules and regulations are followed as per guidance from the Government of India, case basis, time to time.
d. Currency rate conversion should be as per Bank Certificate.
e. All expense certificates should be CA certified.

4.1. For a Startup
a. The Startup should be working towards innovation/ improvement of existing products, services and processes and should have the potential to generate employment/ create wealth.
b. It is not formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business already in existence.
c. An entity will be considered as a Startup on fulfilling the below mentioned conditions defined by Government of Karnataka which is in line with the definition of Government of India (GoI) notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02.2019). However, the policy will adopt the amendments and changes made to the definition by GoI from time to time.
a. The Startup should be incorporated as a private limited company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under Section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008) in Karnataka.
b. Turnover: Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/registration should not have exceeded Γé╣100 crores.
c. Tenure for startups: An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
d. The entity should be working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or if it is a scalable business model with a high potential of employment generation or wealth creation.
d. Exclusions: A company, in order to qualify as a startup under this policy, should not have been:
a. Formed by demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence
b. A Section 8 company or Trust/Association/Society
c. Public-private partnership company/firm
d. A franchisee of an existing business or promoted/sponsored/related to an industrial group in the state
e. A subsidiary of a firm in the state other than the startup itself
e. Inclusions: A company shall qualify as a startup if it is a:
a. Subsidiary of a startup
b. Combined entity formed by merger of startups/subsidiaries of a startup
f. Exit Clause: A startup will cease to receive benefits under this policy on completion of ten years from the date of its incorporation/registration or if its turnover for any previous year exceeds Γé╣100 Crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: A company should not have been: a. Formed by splitting up, demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence; b. A franchisee of an existing business or promoted/sponsored/related to an industrial group in the state; e. A subsidiary of a firm in the state other than the startup itself.

eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incorporated/registered in Karnataka. Specific incentives (SGST, Quality Certification, Incubator Capital Cost) require registration outside Bengaluru Urban and/or Bengaluru Rural districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) under the Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029, and registered with Startup Karnataka / Karnataka Startup Cell.
