incentive_name: R&D Cost Reimbursement for Advanced Chemistry Batteries

policy_goals: Attracting investments of Rs 50,000 Cr across the entire clean mobility vehicle value chain
Generating approximately 100,000 new jobs during the Policy Period
Making Karnataka #1 in Asia in Future Clean Mobility, fueled by Equitable and Sustainable Development
Accelerating Clean Mobility Vehicle Adoption in Karnataka through a Robust Charging Infrastructure Network or hydrogen stations
Create a Clean Mobility Vehicle ecosystem that fosters innovation in the State of Karnataka
Develop sizable clusters at the right price point to attract manufacturing units
Provide initial incentives to stimulate interest from players across the complete Clean Mobility Vehicle value chain
Accelerate identification of strategically located land parcels aligned with power infrastructure and leverage OMCs (Oil Marketing Companies) for rapid development of stations
Offer favorable power tariffs to charging stations
Encourage the establishment of common facilities and testing infrastructure within the clusters
Foster collaborative linkages between industry, academia, and start ups to create clean mobility specific curriculum
Promote Research & Development, spurring innovations in future mobility
Encourage the recycling industry, fostering a circular economy within the State
policy_details.policy_summary: This component of the Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-30 covers demand-side tax exemptions to accelerate EV adoption as well as R&D support for advanced battery technologies. On the demand side, the Government of Karnataka exempts payment of road taxes and registration charges on all categories of transport and non-transport electric vehicles (including e-rickshaws and e-carts), except for electric motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, and private service vehicles costing over Rs. 25 lakhs. On the R&D side, the Government reimburses 30% of the R&D cost up to Rs. 1.00 crore incurred by the first enterprise operating in the state that achieves world-class benchmarks in advanced chemistry batteries (high energy density, long cycle life, high recyclability, safety credentials, and low upfront cost).
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% road tax and registration fee exemption for EVs costing up to Γé╣25 lakh, plus 30% R&D cost reimbursement up to Γé╣1 crore for pioneering advanced battery R&D.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1.2.1 Road tax and registration charges
To encourage the widespread adoption of electric vehicles, Government of Karnataka exempts from payment of taxes on all categories of electric vehicles both transport and non-transport vehicles including e-rickshaws and e-carts, except for motor cars, jeeps, omni buses and private service vehicles run on electricity having cost of the vehicle which exceeds Rs. 25 lakhs under Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 vide Notification No. TD/07/TDR/2024, dated 30.03.2024.

4.5 Support for Research & Skill Development
Technology in Advanced chemistry batteries are evolving at a faster pace with a view to have batteries with high energy density, long cycle life, high recyclability and safety credentials with low upfront cost. To encourage research and development, in these areas, Government of Karnataka will support enterprises achieving these world class bench marks by reimbursing 30 percent of the R& D cost incurred by the first such enterprise operating in the state, subject to a maximum of Rs 1.00 crore during the policy period. The modalities and other eligibility criterion etc., will be decided by the technical committee.

policy_details.policy_summary: This sub-scheme provides a standard package of supply-side incentives and concessions for Large (investment up to INR 300 crore), Mega (investment above INR 300 crore up to INR 1000 crore), and Ultra-Mega (investment above INR 1000 crore) enterprises establishing or expanding clean mobility manufacturing, recycling, or testing units in Karnataka. Benefits include a Capital Investment Subsidy of 20% to 25% of the Value of Fixed Assets (disbursed in 5 equal annual installments after commercial production, with land included up to 50 acres in districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural), 100% stamp duty exemption/reimbursement, concessional registration charges of INR 1 per INR 1,000, 100% reimbursement of land conversion fees, and a 50% one-time capital subsidy up to INR 250 lakh for setting up Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs).
policy_details.benefit_headline: 20% to 25% capital investment subsidy on fixed assets, 100% stamp duty and land conversion fee waiver, and up to Γé╣250 lakh ETP subsidy for Large, Mega, and Ultra-Mega clean mobility enterprises in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1.1 Eligibility and Coverage
Following activities/products for which investments are made during the policy period as per Section 7 would be eligible for availing incentives under this policy.
1. Clean mobility vehicle and Clean Mobility components
ΓÇó Manufacturing/Assembly of Electric Vehicles (fixed battery/swappable battery), hydrogen based vehicles, fuel cell based electric vehicles.
ΓÇó Manufacturing of clean mobility cells, clean mobility battery pack/module manufacturing and assembly (Li Ion cells, fuel cells, hydrogen cells or any advanced chemistry battery cells).
ΓÇó Manufacturing of clean mobility vehicle components
2. Li-ion & fuel cell components
3. Manufacturing of Electric Vehicle Charging/Swapping Infrastructure Equipment and Hydrogen stations
4. Re-use and Recycling of batteries through recycling centers set up by clean mobility battery manufacturers and other players.
5. Clean Mobility vehicle testing facility includes testing of battery/cell materials and components.
Note: Components manufacturers shall supply minimum 50% of their products to EV and clean mobility OEM (original equipment manufacturer).

4.1.3.2 Capital Investment Subsidy: New/Expansion/Modernization/Diversification projects in manufacturing as defined in section 4.1.1 shall be eligible for a capital subsidy of 20-25 % of investment in Value of Fixed Assets, based on the zone, to be disbursed over 5 equal annual payments subject to subsidy on land applicable for maximum of 50 acres.

Appendix 1:
2. Large Enterprise: An Industrial Unit that is not classified as a Medium Enterprise and with an investment in fixed assets up to INR 300 crore shall be classified as a large-scale enterprise.
3. Mega Enterprise: Projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and up to INR 1000 crore.
4. Ultra-Mega Enterprise: Projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 1000 crore.
8. Quantum of Incentive for Expansion/Diversification/Modernization: To be eligible for incentives under expansion / diversification / modernization program, the Enterprise has to increase the installed capacity by at least 25% of the declared capacity or average production during immediate 3 years prior to commencement of the commercial production in the expansion/ diversification/ modernization program, whichever is more and has to make an additional investment of at least 25% of the original fixed investment of the existing unit.
10. a. All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category will be insisted] and this will be monitored during disbursement of incentives and concessions.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: For Capital Investment Subsidy calculation of Value of Fixed Assets (VFA), land in Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts is excluded (Land will include only districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural up to an extent of 50 acres).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Components manufacturers shall supply minimum 50% of their products to EV and clean mobility OEM (original equipment manufacturer). All new EV Enterprises shall provide a minimum 70% of employment to local people on overall basis (100% in case of Group D category). Contract labour engaged in production line should not exceed 40% of total labour force. For expansion/diversification/modernization, the enterprise must increase installed capacity by at least 25% and make an additional investment of at least 25% of the original fixed investment.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Classified across Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3 taluks of Karnataka as per Appendix 2.

incentive_details.description: Capital investment subsidy of 20% to 25% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) for New/Expansion/Modernization/Diversification projects in manufacturing under Large, Mega, and Ultra Mega categories. policy_details.policy_summary: This sub-scheme under the Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-30 provides a comprehensive package of supply-side incentives and concessions for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) operating across the clean mobility value chain in Karnataka. policy_details.policy_summary: This sub-scheme under the Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-30 provides a comprehensive package of supply-side incentives and concessions for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) operating across the clean mobility value chain in Karnataka. Eligible activities include manufacturing and assembly of electric vehicles (fixed/swappable battery), hydrogen and fuel cell vehicles, battery cells and packs, EV components, Li-ion and fuel cell materials, charging/swapping equipment, battery recycling centers, and testing facilities. eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1.1 Eligibility and Coverage
Following activities/products for which investments are made during the policy period as per Section 7 would be eligible for availing incentives under this policy.
1. Clean mobility vehicle and Clean Mobility components
ΓÇó Manufacturing/Assembly of Electric Vehicles (fixed battery/swappable battery), hydrogen based vehicles, fuel cell based electric vehicles.
Note: In the policy document, Clean Mobility Vehicle to refer to all the above technologies, unless specified otherwise
ΓÇó Manufacturing of clean mobility cells, clean mobility battery pack/module manufacturing and assembly (Li Ion cells, fuel cells, hydrogen cells or any advanced chemistry battery cells).
ΓÇó Manufacturing of clean mobility vehicle components as follows:
- Electric motor & drive including Electric motors, Electric driveline systems, Integrated power box unit, Electric Axles/Half Shafts, and power transfer units
- Motor Controllers/Power Control Units, Inverters/converters, Battery pack Controllers and on-board chargers
- AC/DC charging inlet
- Battery system including Battery Cells/Pack, Battery Management System, Thermal management system
- Auxiliary Battery System
- EV specific electrical infrastructure including high voltage wiring and components
- Electric compressor
2. Li-ion & fuel cell components
ΓÇó Cathode Active Materials using advanced technologies like NMC, LFP etc.
ΓÇó Anode Materials using Graphite, Copper, Silicon, Carbon black etc.
ΓÇó Separator (Polyethylene & Polypropylene)
ΓÇó Carbonate Solvents like Lithium hexafluorophosphate, Ethylene carbonate, Diethyl carbonate etc.
ΓÇó Processing of minerals used for Li-ion processing only, e.g Li, Ni, Co, Mn
ΓÇó Consumables like
- Packaging foil-Pouches/Cans/Cases
- Steel casing
- Cylindrical ΓÇô Metal housing, Insulation Ring, heat Shrinkable PVC, Foam
- Prismatic ΓÇô Metal Housing, Insulation Foil
3. Manufacturing of Electric Vehicle Charging/Swapping Infrastructure Equipment and Hydrogen stations
4. Re-use and Recycling of batteries through recycling centers set up by clean mobility battery manufacturers and other players.
5. Clean Mobility vehicle testing facility includes testing of battery/cell materials and components.
Note: Components manufacturers shall supply minimum 50% of their products to EV and clean mobility OEM (original equipment manufacturer).

Appendix 1:
1. As per the MSMED Act, 2006, MSMEs have been defined as follows:
ΓÇó Micro Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 1 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 5 crore.
ΓÇó Small Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 10 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 50 crore.
ΓÇó Medium Enterprises ΓÇô Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 50 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 250 crore.
For the calculation purpose of incentives for MSMEs, the following definitions will be used irrespective of the definitions under the MSMED Act.
Category: Micro | Criteria: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment < INR 1 Crore
Category: Small | Criteria: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 1 Crore to INR 10 Crore
Category: Medium | Criteria: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 10 Crore to INR 50 Crore

8. Quantum of Incentive for Expansion/Diversification/Modernization: To be eligible for incentives under expansion / diversification / modernization program, the Enterprise has to increase the installed capacity by at least 25% of the declared capacity or average production during immediate 3 years prior to commencement of the commercial production in the expansion/ diversification/ modernization program, whichever is more and has to make an additional investment of at least 25% of the original fixed investment of the existing unit.
10. a. All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category will be insisted] and this will be monitored during disbursement of incentives and concessions.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Components manufacturers shall supply minimum 50% of their products to EV and clean mobility OEM (original equipment manufacturer). All new EV Enterprises shall provide a minimum 70% of employment to local people on overall basis (100% in case of Group D category). Contract labour engaged in production line should not exceed 40% of total labour force. For expansion/diversification/modernization, the enterprise must increase installed capacity by at least 25% and make an additional investment of at least 25% of the original fixed investment.

eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Activities/products falling outside section 4.1.1 require certification/validation from the Technical Committee.

policy_name: Cyber Security Policy 2024 - Part I (Public)
incentive_name: Internship for undergraduate and graduate students in the field of cyber security

policy_goals: To make Karnataka the leading cyber security hub in the country by instilling a culture of cyber security and data privacy amongst citizens and businesses, and promoting a thriving cyber security industry and start-up ecosystem in the state.
To build a dynamic, secure and resilient cyberspace for all the G2G, G2B and G2C services of Govt of Karnataka.
Building awareness amongst citizens, government departments, and vulnerable groups.
Skill building to create a skilled cyber security talent pool and workforce.
Promoting research and innovation in the cyber security domain.
Promotion of Industry and Start-ups in the cyber security sector.
Partnerships and Collaborations for Capacity Building.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Cyber Security Policy 2024 (Public Part) aims to make Karnataka the leading cyber security hub in India by fostering a culture of cyber security and data privacy, and promoting a thriving industry and start-up ecosystem. Structured around five pillarsΓÇöBuilding Awareness, Skill Building, Promoting Research and Innovation, Promotion of Industry and Start-ups, and Partnerships for Capacity BuildingΓÇöthe policy provides targeted fiscal and non-fiscal support to Karnataka-based start-ups, MSMEs, MNCs, and academic institutions working in the cyberspace domain. Key fiscal incentives include matching grants of up to 50% (capped at Rs. 50 lakhs) for collaborative R&D projects, internship stipend reimbursements (Rs. 10,000/month for UG and Rs. 15,000/month for PG interns for up to 3 months) for companies hiring cyber security interns, and reimbursement of up to Rs. 1 lakh for start-ups engaging CERT-In empanelled providers for cyber security audits and incident management. Non-fiscal measures include incubation support, government-backed pilot projects, preferential public procurement for local start-ups, and the establishment of K-CERT and Regional Centres of Excellence.

The remaining 50% of R&D costs must be borne by the start-up and/or collaborating academic institution/industry partner. Five such projects will be funded each year.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Matching grant up to 50% of approved R&D project cost, up to a maximum of Γé╣50 lakhs.

Two-phase evaluation by R&D Sub-Committee (Techno-Financial presentation and physical/virtual onsite due diligence) followed by final sanction by Approval Committee and signing of Project Funding Agreement (PFA).

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: up to Rs. 50 lakhs, whichever is lower
quantified_benefits.value_raw: up to a maximum of 50% of the total project R&D cost
quantified_benefits.conditions: May be availed by an entity once over the policy period. R&D costs borne before application approval are not eligible.
quantified_benefits.description: Conditional matching grant for approved R&D expenditures in the domain of cyber security.

These grants may be availed by an entity once over the policy period. Five such projects will be funded in each year.

policy_goals: To make Bengaluru the Electrical Vehicle Capital of India

To make Karnataka a preferred investment destination for manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (EVs) by leveraging advantages and opportunities available for sustained development of this promising segment
To make Karnataka a preferred destination for development of Electric Mobility
To promote a conducive manufacturing ecosystem in collaboration with the industry
To develop human capital to meet the need of the Industry
To maintain the lead share of Karnataka as a preferred destination for attracting investments in manufacture of Electric Vehicles
To attract investments of Rs 31,000 crore and create employment opportunities to 55,000 persons both from supply & demand side
To create a conducive environment for transition to Electric Vehicle environment from Internal Combustion (IC) engines

To invite investments in setting up to 5 GWh of EV Battery manufacturing capacity which is expected to generate 5,000 direct employment in this industry and around 7,500 more in the overall EV Battery manufacturing/assembly supply chain
policy_details.policy_summary: Aimed at establishing 5 GWh of EV battery manufacturing capacity and generating 12,500 direct and indirect jobs in Karnataka, this sub-policy offers fiscal incentives to EV Battery Cell Manufacturing and EV Battery Pack/Module Assembly enterprises using advanced battery chemistries (such as lithium-ion). Amended in June 2021 to remove caps on the number of eligible units, it offers an Investment Promotion Subsidy (up to 25% of VFA for MSMEs and 15% of VFA over 5 years for Large/Mega/Ultra/Super Mega enterprises), a 1% Production Linked Subsidy on turnover for 5 years (for Large and above units), 100% stamp duty waiver, concessional registration charges (Re. 1 per Rs. 1,000), 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, 5-year electricity duty exemption for MSMEs, and up to 50% ETP capital subsidy.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital subsidy for MSMEs (15% VFA + 1% turnover-linked subsidy for Large/Mega units), 100% stamp duty waiver, and 5-year electricity duty exemption for EV battery cell & pack manufacturers.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
All the EV Battery manufacturing/Assembly Enterprises will be eligible for the incentives and concessions.
Manufacturing and assembly of the major component required for Electric Vehicles such as lithium ion batteries, will be eligible for incentives as per the policy subject to approval of the Technical Committee which would be constituted & mandated to certify/define EV battery manufacturing enterprises.
Note: These incentives are applicable to advanced battery chemistries only as defined by the technical committee and applicable to both battery cell manufacturing and battery pack/ module assembly.
Total quantum of incentives sanctioned to a manufacturing/assembly unit under this policy shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) created by the unit.
1 Definition of Micro, Small and Medium EV Enterprises shall be as defined in the MSMED Act, 2006 of Govt. of India.
2 Large EV Enterprises is one where investment on plant & machinery is more than Rs.10 crore in respect of manufacturing activities and Rs. 5 crore in respect of service oriented activities and the upper limit is up to Rs. 250 crore of the project cost.
3 Mega EV Enterprise is one where the project cost of the proposed project is more than Rs. 250 crore and up to Rs. 500 crore and employment for at least 150 persons.
4 Ultra Mega EV Enterprise is one where the investment on the project is more than Rs. 500 crore and up to Rs. 1,000 crore and employment for at least 250 persons.
5 Super Mega EV Enterprise is one where the investment on the project is more than Rs.1,000 crore and direct employment for at least 500 persons.
8 Sanction of Incentives & Concessions as per this Government Order is subject to the following terms and Conditions:
a) All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category will be insisted] and this will be monitored during disbursement of incentives and concessions.
c) The incentives and concessions under this policy will be available to all new investments both for establishment of new Enterprises or for expansion, diversification and modernization of existing industries. To be eligible for considering as expansion/diversification/ modernization, enterprises shall make an additional investment of at least 50% of the original investment of the existing unit.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Battery chemistries not defined/approved as advanced battery chemistries by the Technical Committee.

(Minimum 70% local employment overall and 100% in Group D category required for all enterprises).

policy_details.policy_summary: To facilitate the penetration, adoption, and use of Electric Vehicles in Karnataka, this sub-policy provides tax exemptions for EV buyers/operators and capital subsidies for EV charging and battery swapping service providers. All electric non-transport and transport vehicles (including e-rickshaws and e-carts) are exempted from Motor Vehicle Taxes under the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957 (effective 01/04/2016). Additionally, EV mobility service providers receive a 25% capital subsidy on charging/swapping equipment and machinery: up to Rs. 10 lakh per station for the first 100 fast charging stations, up to Rs. 3 lakh per station for the first 100 2-wheeler/3-wheeler battery swapping stations, up to Rs. 5 lakh per station for the first 50 car battery swapping stations, and up to Rs. 10 lakh per station for the first 50 bus battery swapping stations in the State.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% Motor Vehicle Tax exemption on all EVs and 25% capital subsidy on equipment (up to Rs. 10 lakh per station) for EV fast charging and battery swapping stations.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
To facilitate penetration and use of EV, it is proposed to provide the following incentives to EV in non-transport and transport vehicles & service providers.
1. EV in non-transport and transport vehicles
a) In order to promote adoptability of EVs, Government of Karnataka has exempted from payment of taxes on all electric non-transport and transport vehicles including e-rickshaws and e-cart under Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957 with effect from 01/04/2016 vide Notification No. SARIE 76 SAEPA 2016 dtd 31/03/2016.
2. Service Providers for EV mobility
a) All fast charging stations for electric 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, cars and buses will be offered the following incentives: Capital subsidy of 25% on the equipments /Machinery subject to maximum of Rs 10,00,000/- per station for the first 100 fast charging stations in the State.
b) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 3,00,000 per station for the first 100 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
c) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric cars: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 5,00,000 per station for the first 50 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
d) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric buses: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 10,00,000 per station for the first 50 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
b) Government of Karnataka will encourage private players to set up Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI)-compliant/BIS Standard, EV charging Systems/infrastructure.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: EV charging systems/infrastructure should be Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI)-compliant / BIS Standard. Capital subsidies are restricted to the first 100 fast charging stations, first 100 2W/3W swapping stations, first 50 car swapping stations, and first 50 bus swapping stations in the State.

policy_details.policy_summary: To facilitate the penetration, adoption, and use of Electric Vehicles in Karnataka, this sub-policy provides tax exemptions for EV buyers/operators and capital subsidies for EV charging and battery swapping service providers. All electric non-transport and transport vehicles (including e-rickshaws and e-carts) are exempted from Motor Vehicle Taxes under the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957 (effective 01/04/2016). Additionally, EV mobility service providers receive a 25% capital subsidy on charging/swapping equipment and machinery: up to Rs. 10 lakh per station for the first 100 fast charging stations, up to Rs. 3 lakh per station for the first 100 2-wheeler/3-wheeler battery swapping stations, up to Rs. 5 lakh per station for the first 50 car battery swapping stations, and up to Rs. 10 lakh per station for the first 50 bus battery swapping stations in the State.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% Motor Vehicle Tax exemption on all EVs and 25% capital subsidy on equipment (up to Rs. 10 lakh per station) for EV fast charging and battery swapping stations.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
To facilitate penetration and use of EV, it is proposed to provide the following incentives to EV in non-transport and transport vehicles & service providers.
1. EV in non-transport and transport vehicles
a) In order to promote adoptability of EVs, Government of Karnataka has exempted from payment of taxes on all electric non-transport and transport vehicles including e-rickshaws and e-cart under Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957 with effect from 01/04/2016 vide Notification No. SARIE 76 SAEPA 2016 dtd 31/03/2016.
2. Service Providers for EV mobility
a) All fast charging stations for electric 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, cars and buses will be offered the following incentives: Capital subsidy of 25% on the equipments /Machinery subject to maximum of Rs 10,00,000/- per station for the first 100 fast charging stations in the State.
b) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 3,00,000 per station for the first 100 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
c) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric cars: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 5,00,000 per station for the first 50 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
d) All EV battery switching/swapping stations for electric buses: Capital subsidy of 25% on the charging equipments/machinery subject to maximum of Rs. 10,00,000 per station for the first 50 battery switching/swapping stations in the State.
b) Government of Karnataka will encourage private players to set up Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI)-compliant/BIS Standard, EV charging Systems/infrastructure.

Capital subsidies are restricted to the first 100 fast charging stations, first 100 2W/3W swapping stations, first 50 car swapping stations, and first 50 bus swapping stations in the State.

policy_goals: Stimulate the growth of 2000 ESDM startups during the policy period.
Enhance value addition done in Karnataka by 50%.
Create 20 Lacs new jobs in the ESDM industry by 2025, both direct and indirect, thereby increasing the total workforce in the sector to ten times the present number.
Effect a quantum jump in the overall revenues of KarnatakaΓÇÖs ESDM companies to USD 40 billion by 2025.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) Policy 2017-2022 (extended up to September 2030 via subsequent Government Orders) aims to develop Karnataka into a global ESDM hub and a hotbed of innovation. It targets key focus sectors including Medical Electronics, Industrial Automation/Robotics, Automotive Electronics, Nano Electronics, and Consumer Electronics. The policy provides comprehensive support across skill development (including a 50% internship stipend subsidy up to Γé╣15,000 per student), quality infrastructure (Common Instrumentation Facilities, Centres of Excellence, and Electronics Manufacturing Clusters), local ecosystem development (Preferential Market Access, pilots, and venture funds), ease-of-doing-business reforms (self-certification under labor laws and single-window clearance via KBITS), and a wide array of financial incentives. Financial benefits for registered KESDM companies include Patent Registration reimbursement (up to Γé╣2 lakhs domestic / Γé╣10 lakhs international), International Marketing reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣5 lakhs/year), R&D Grants (25% for Startups/MSMEs and 10% for Large/Mega units, up to Γé╣2 crores/year), Capital Subsidy for anchor units in greenfield clusters (up to 10%, capped at Γé╣10 crores), Quality Certification reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣10 lakhs/year), Prototyping cost reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣10 lakhs/year), PF/ESI reimbursement (Γé╣2,000/employee/month for 2 years up to Γé╣12 lakhs), Interest Subsidy (up to 6% on loans up to Γé╣50 lakhs for 5 years), Stamp Duty Exemption (100% for Startups/MSMEs, 75% for Large/Mega), Concessional Registration Charges (Γé╣1 per Γé╣1,000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% for Startups/MSMEs, 50% for Large/Mega), Industrial Power Tariff Concession, ETP setup subsidy (50% up to Γé╣50 lakhs for Startups/MSMEs and Γé╣1 crore for Large/Mega), and tailor-made packages for Mega Enterprises. Total reimbursements (excluding Capital Subsidy) are capped at Γé╣3 crores per year and Γé╣10 crores over the policy period per company.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive financial support including up to 25% R&D grant (up to Γé╣2 Cr/year), 100% stamp duty exemption, 6% interest subsidy, and 50% reimbursement on prototyping, quality certification, and international marketing for ESDM companies in Karnataka (plus up to Γé╣10 Cr capital subsidy for greenfield cluster anchor units).
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women members (preference in International Marketing Incentive)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.2 Eligibility for Availing Financial Support
To avail these incentives/concessions, an ESDM company must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company. Companies which are already registered under KESDM Policy need not register again under the new policy.
The old KESDM Policy 2013 ceases to exist in view of the new policy 2017-2022 which is announced on 1st December 2017 vide Government Order No. ITD 09 PRM 2017.Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered.
For the Financial Year 2017-18, companies can only claim incentives from April 2017 to March 2018 which would be considered under the guidelines of KESDM Policy 2017 -22.
Application for any incentives/concessions for each financial year should be submitted half yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year. If the applications are submitted after this duration it would be rejected. This condition is relaxed for Patent Incentive.
Nature of business:
The company or entity should be engaged in one of the following businesses:
ΓÇó Manufacturing and or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems And Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defence & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment / etc.
ΓÇó Manufacturing of intermediates such as PCBs / semiconductors / chip components / ICs / components
ΓÇó Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)
ΓÇó Design / IP / Software services for electronics products
ΓÇó Any other electronics verticals / products covered by the National Policy on Electronics (NPE) / National Manufacturing Policy (NPM) and related notifications, as issued by the Govt. of India from time to time
Location:
The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
Employment:
The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees.
Value Addition:
The company or entity should do value addition within the state, in-line with the below formulae:
Year 1: Minimum percentage of value addition 25%
Year 2: Minimum percentage of value addition 30%
Year 3: Minimum percentage of value addition 35%
Year 4: Minimum percentage of value addition 40%
Year 5: Minimum percentage of value addition 45%
Product Price (Ex-factory): A
Cost of Bill of Material (BOM) in ΓÇÿAΓÇÖ: B (including software design, IP)
BOM sourced from domestic manufacturers: C (including software design and IP design)
Value addition in terms of BOM: (C/B) * 100
For those companies who may have multiple offices in India/abroad, they must have their 60% workforce residing in Karnataka and if Karnataka design centre is directly involved in claimed activity (patent development/marketing/R&D/quality certification/prototyping), would they be considered as eligible for that particular incentive/concession.
For the purpose of incentives, companies have been categorized into different classifications of Startups & MSMEs, Large Enterprises and Mega Enterprises. The categorization of companies is as mentioned below:
Category: Startups and MSMEs | Investments on Fixed Assets: Less than INR 10 Cr
Category: Large Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: Between INR 10 Cr up to INR 250 Cr
Category: Mega Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: More than INR 250 Cr
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered. Those incentives which are common in Karnataka Industrial Policy and Karnataka Start-up Policy can only be claimed from any one source. Any irregularity/misrepresentation in this regard will disqualify the company from availing any incentives in any of the policies of Govt. of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees (60% for companies with multiple offices in India/abroad). Value Addition within the state (BOM sourced from domestic manufacturers / Total Cost of BOM * 100): Year 1: min 25%, Year 2: min 30%, Year 3: min 35%, Year 4: min 40%, Year 5: min 45%. Categorization by Investment on Fixed Assets: Startups and MSMEs (< INR 10 Cr), Large Enterprises (INR 10 Cr to 250 Cr), Mega Enterprises (> INR 250 Cr). Overall cap: Maximum amount reimbursed to a single company under various incentives/concessions, excluding Capital Subsidy, is capped at INR 3 Crores for a single year and INR 10 Crores during the policy period.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. For companies with multiple offices in India/abroad, 60% workforce must reside in Karnataka and the Karnataka design centre must be directly involved in the claimed activity.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company (one-time fee of INR 10,000 + GST, waived if already registered as a Karnataka IT or BT company or under the old KESDM policy), and registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
special_category_benefits: Women members (preference for reimbursement under International Marketing Incentive)

incentive_details.description: Capital subsidy of up to 10% of total eligible fixed capital investment (land excluding leasehold, building and civil works excluding residential quarters/guest houses, plant and machinery, and IT infrastructure) up to a maximum of Γé╣10 Crores, applicable exclusively to the first two anchor units (Large and Mega Enterprises) in each Greenfield cluster.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 10% capital subsidy up to Γé╣10 Crores for the first two Large or Mega anchor units in each Greenfield cluster.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Form 4 (Application Form for Capital Subsidy) with KESDM Registration Certificate, incorporation document, investment invoices/POs, financial institution letter, CA/Cost accountant certificate of total investment, and copy of first sale invoice to esdmcell@karnataka.gov.in and hard copy to KBITS. Post approval, submit an undertaking on Rs. 100 stamp paper.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: up to a maximum of INR 10 Crores
quantified_benefits.conditions: Unit must be certified as one of the first two anchor units in a Greenfield cluster, have commenced commercial production (first sale invoice required), and execute an undertaking on Rs. 100 stamp paper committing to maintain location/investment for 3 years and local employment (Kannadigas) for 5 years.
quantified_benefits.description: Capital subsidy on eligible fixed capital investment for the first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Govt. of Karnataka will provide up to 10% capital subsidy, up to a maximum of INR 10 Crores to registered KESDM companies, which will be applicable to the first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster. This subsidy is not applicable to Startups and MSMEΓÇÖs.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Large and Mega Enterprises (first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster)

incentive_details.application_deadline: Half-yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year.
incentive_details.application_authority: ESDM Cell, Karnataka Biotechnology and Information Technology Services (KBITS)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Applicable only to the first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster. Only Large and Mega Enterprises are eligible; this subsidy is NOT applicable to Startups and MSMEs.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.2 Eligibility for Availing Financial Support
To avail these incentives/concessions, an ESDM company must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company. Companies which are already registered under KESDM Policy need not register again under the new policy.
The old KESDM Policy 2013 ceases to exist in view of the new policy 2017-2022 which is announced on 1st December 2017 vide Government Order No. ITD 09 PRM 2017.Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered.
For the Financial Year 2017-18, companies can only claim incentives from April 2017 to March 2018 which would be considered under the guidelines of KESDM Policy 2017 -22.
Application for any incentives/concessions for each financial year should be submitted half yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year. If the applications are submitted after this duration it would be rejected. This condition is relaxed for Patent Incentive.
Nature of business:
The company or entity should be engaged in one of the following businesses:
ΓÇó Manufacturing and or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems And Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defence & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment / etc.
ΓÇó Manufacturing of intermediates such as PCBs / semiconductors / chip components / ICs / components
ΓÇó Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)
ΓÇó Design / IP / Software services for electronics products
ΓÇó Any other electronics verticals / products covered by the National Policy on Electronics (NPE) / National Manufacturing Policy (NPM) and related notifications, as issued by the Govt. of India from time to time
Location:
The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
Employment:
The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees.
Value Addition:
The company or entity should do value addition within the state, in-line with the below formulae:
Year 1: Minimum percentage of value addition 25%
Year 2: Minimum percentage of value addition 30%
Year 3: Minimum percentage of value addition 35%
Year 4: Minimum percentage of value addition 40%
Year 5: Minimum percentage of value addition 45%
Product Price (Ex-factory): A
Cost of Bill of Material (BOM) in ΓÇÿAΓÇÖ: B (including software design, IP)
BOM sourced from domestic manufacturers: C (including software design and IP design)
Value addition in terms of BOM: (C/B) * 100
For those companies who may have multiple offices in India/abroad, they must have their 60% workforce residing in Karnataka and if Karnataka design centre is directly involved in claimed activity (patent development/marketing/R&D/quality certification/prototyping), would they be considered as eligible for that particular incentive/concession.
For the purpose of incentives, companies have been categorized into different classifications of Startups & MSMEs, Large Enterprises and Mega Enterprises. The categorization of companies is as mentioned below:
Category: Startups and MSMEs | Investments on Fixed Assets: Less than INR 10 Cr
Category: Large Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: Between INR 10 Cr up to INR 250 Cr
Category: Mega Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: More than INR 250 Cr
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered. Those incentives which are common in Karnataka Industrial Policy and Karnataka Start-up Policy can only be claimed from any one source. Any irregularity/misrepresentation in this regard will disqualify the company from availing any incentives in any of the policies of Govt. of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees (60% for companies with multiple offices in India/abroad). eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. For companies with multiple offices in India/abroad, 60% workforce must reside in Karnataka and the Karnataka design centre must be directly involved in the claimed activity.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company (one-time fee of INR 10,000 + GST, waived if already registered as a Karnataka IT or BT company or under the old KESDM policy), and registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.

Capped at 2 employees for participation in up to 2 international events/conferences/tradeshows per company per year.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% reimbursement of international marketing, trade show stall, and travel expenses up to Γé╣5 Lakhs per year.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: up to a maximum 0f INR 5 Lacs per year
quantified_benefits.conditions: Capped at 2 employees for participation in up to 2 international events/conferences/tradeshows per company per year; economy air travel only and DA up to $100 a day (excluding journey days); preference given to women members.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of 50% of actual costs incurred in registration, economy class travel, boarding/lodging (DA up to $100/day), trade show participation, and exhibition stall rentals for international events.
quantified_benefits.source_text: For export promotion of ESDM products and building brand equity of KESDM companies as credible players internationally, Govt. of Karnataka will provide reimbursements of 50% of the actual cost incurred in - Registration, economy class travel, boarding and lodging expenses for international marketing, events, and conferences; Trade show participation and exhibition stall rentals. A single KESDM company will be eligible to claim the reimbursement for up to a maximum 0f INR 5 Lacs per year.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Applicable to Startups, MSMEs, Large, and Mega Enterprises. Preference for reimbursement will be given to woman members.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of actual costs incurred by registered KESDM companies for filing domestic and international patents (including filing fees paid to the patent office, attorney fees, search fees, and maintenance fees). Up to 75% of eligible expenses or the upper limit is reimbursed upon filing, and the remaining 25% is paid upon grant of the patent. Alternatively, 100% of eligible costs can be claimed at once after the patent is granted. A single company can claim a maximum of 5 reimbursements during the policy period, in addition to any Government of India scheme.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% reimbursement of patent filing costs up to Γé╣2 Lakhs for domestic patents and Γé╣10 Lakhs for international patents (up to 5 patents per company).
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Form 1 (Application Form for Patent Registration Incentive) along with KESDM registration certificate, patent filing application/receipts, grant certificate (if granted), invoices, and bank statement online to esdmcell@karnataka.gov.in and mail hard copy to ESDM Cell, KBITS. A separate application must be submitted for each patent claim.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: up to a maximum of INR 2 Lac
quantified_benefits.conditions: Patent must be filed or granted within the policy period; maximum of five reimbursements (inclusive of domestic or international patents) per company during the policy period.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of actual patent filing and grant costs for a domestic (Indian) patent (75% on filing and 25% on grant, or 100% post-grant).
quantified_benefits.source_text: Registered KESDM companies will be reimbursed the actual costs, up to a maximum of INR 2 Lac for filing a domestic patent; and up to a maximum of INR 10 Lacs for filing an international patent, provided such patent is filed or granted within the policy period. Up to 75% of the eligible expense amount or 75% of the upper limit (INR 2 Lacs for domestic patent; INR 10 Lacs for international patent), will be reimbursed once the patent is filed. The balance 25% will be paid after the patent has been granted. However, the full reimbursement can also be claimed after the grant of the patent, in which case 100% of the eligible costs will be reimbursed post the application, subject to the maximum grant amount.

It targets key focus sectors including Medical Electronics, Industrial Automation/Robotics, Automotive Electronics, Nano Electronics, and Consumer Electronics. The policy provides comprehensive support across skill development (including a 50% internship stipend subsidy up to Γé╣15,000 per student), quality infrastructure (Common Instrumentation Facilities, Centres of Excellence, and Electronics Manufacturing Clusters), local ecosystem development (Preferential Market Access, pilots, and venture funds), ease-of-doing-business reforms (self-certification under labor laws and single-window clearance via KBITS), and a wide array of financial incentives. Financial benefits for registered KESDM companies include Patent Registration reimbursement (up to Γé╣2 lakhs domestic / Γé╣10 lakhs international), International Marketing reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣5 lakhs/year), R&D Grants (25% for Startups/MSMEs and 10% for Large/Mega units, up to Γé╣2 crores/year), Capital Subsidy for anchor units in greenfield clusters (up to 10%, capped at Γé╣10 crores), Quality Certification reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣10 lakhs/year), Prototyping cost reimbursement (50% up to Γé╣10 lakhs/year), PF/ESI reimbursement (Γé╣2,000/employee/month for 2 years up to Γé╣12 lakhs), Interest Subsidy (up to 6% on loans up to Γé╣50 lakhs for 5 years), Stamp Duty Exemption (100% for Startups/MSMEs, 75% for Large/Mega), Concessional Registration Charges (Γé╣1 per Γé╣1,000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% for Startups/MSMEs, 50% for Large/Mega), Industrial Power Tariff Concession, ETP setup subsidy (50% up to Γé╣50 lakhs for Startups/MSMEs and Γé╣1 crore for Large/Mega), and tailor-made packages for Mega Enterprises. Total reimbursements (excluding Capital Subsidy) are capped at Γé╣3 crores per year and Γé╣10 crores over the policy period per company.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.2 Eligibility for Availing Financial Support
To avail these incentives/concessions, an ESDM company must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company. Companies which are already registered under KESDM Policy need not register again under the new policy.
The old KESDM Policy 2013 ceases to exist in view of the new policy 2017-2022 which is announced on 1st December 2017 vide Government Order No. ITD 09 PRM 2017.Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered.
For the Financial Year 2017-18, companies can only claim incentives from April 2017 to March 2018 which would be considered under the guidelines of KESDM Policy 2017 -22.
Application for any incentives/concessions for each financial year should be submitted half yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year. If the applications are submitted after this duration it would be rejected. This condition is relaxed for Patent Incentive.
Nature of business:
The company or entity should be engaged in one of the following businesses:
ΓÇó Manufacturing and or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems And Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defence & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment / etc.
ΓÇó Manufacturing of intermediates such as PCBs / semiconductors / chip components / ICs / components
ΓÇó Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)
ΓÇó Design / IP / Software services for electronics products
ΓÇó Any other electronics verticals / products covered by the National Policy on Electronics (NPE) / National Manufacturing Policy (NPM) and related notifications, as issued by the Govt. of India from time to time
Location:
The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
Employment:
The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees.
Value Addition:
The company or entity should do value addition within the state, in-line with the below formulae:
Year 1: Minimum percentage of value addition 25%
Year 2: Minimum percentage of value addition 30%
Year 3: Minimum percentage of value addition 35%
Year 4: Minimum percentage of value addition 40%
Year 5: Minimum percentage of value addition 45%
Product Price (Ex-factory): A
Cost of Bill of Material (BOM) in ΓÇÿAΓÇÖ: B (including software design, IP)
BOM sourced from domestic manufacturers: C (including software design and IP design)
Value addition in terms of BOM: (C/B) * 100
For those companies who may have multiple offices in India/abroad, they must have their 60% workforce residing in Karnataka and if Karnataka design centre is directly involved in claimed activity (patent development/marketing/R&D/quality certification/prototyping), would they be considered as eligible for that particular incentive/concession.
For the purpose of incentives, companies have been categorized into different classifications of Startups & MSMEs, Large Enterprises and Mega Enterprises. The categorization of companies is as mentioned below:
Category: Startups and MSMEs | Investments on Fixed Assets: Less than INR 10 Cr
Category: Large Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: Between INR 10 Cr up to INR 250 Cr
Category: Mega Enterprises | Investments on Fixed Assets: More than INR 250 Cr
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered. Those incentives which are common in Karnataka Industrial Policy and Karnataka Start-up Policy can only be claimed from any one source. Any irregularity/misrepresentation in this regard will disqualify the company from availing any incentives in any of the policies of Govt. of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Employment: Company employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees (60% for companies with multiple offices in India/abroad). Value Addition within the state (BOM sourced from domestic manufacturers / Total Cost of BOM * 100): Year 1: min 25%, Year 2: min 30%, Year 3: min 35%, Year 4: min 40%, Year 5: min 45%. Categorization by Investment on Fixed Assets: Startups and MSMEs (< INR 10 Cr), Large Enterprises (INR 10 Cr to 250 Cr), Mega Enterprises (> INR 250 Cr). Overall cap: Maximum amount reimbursed to a single company under various incentives/concessions, excluding Capital Subsidy, is capped at INR 3 Crores for a single year and INR 10 Crores during the policy period.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. For companies with multiple offices in India/abroad, 60% workforce must reside in Karnataka and the Karnataka design centre must be directly involved in the claimed activity.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company (one-time fee of INR 10,000 + GST, waived if already registered as a Karnataka IT or BT company or under the old KESDM policy), and registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
special_category_benefits: Women members (preference for reimbursement under International Marketing Incentive)

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of Provident Fund (PF) or Employee's State Insurance (ESI) contributions of Γé╣2,000 per employee per month (or actual employer contribution, whichever is less) for two years, up to a total maximum of Γé╣12 Lakhs (note: flowchart on page 33 of guidelines mentions INR 24 Lacs, while text states INR 12 Lacs), for new employment created during the policy period by newly established KESDM Startups and MSMEs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: PF/ESI reimbursement of up to Γé╣2,000 per employee per month for 2 years (up to Γé╣12 Lakhs total) for newly established Startups and MSMEs.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Form 8 (Application Form for PF/ESI Incentive) with KESDM Registration Certificate, Chartered Accountant certified letter with employee details, PF/ESI numbers and contributions, employment records for last 2 years, and PF/ESI contribution receipts/challans to esdmcell@karnataka.gov.in and hard copy to KBITS.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: subject to total reimbursement of up to INR 12 Lacs
quantified_benefits.value_raw: INR 2,000 per employee per month for two years
quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable only for new employment created during the policy period for a continuous period of two years; reimbursement will be made only once per company during the policy period.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of employer's PF or ESI contribution per new employee per month for two continuous years.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Registered KESDM Startups and MSMEs will be reimbursed Provident Fund (PF) / EmployeeΓÇÖs State Insurance (ESI) of INR 2,000 per employee per month for two years subject to total reimbursement of up to INR 12 Lacs. This is only applicable for all new employment created during the policy period, provided the employment is for a continuous period of two years. In case the employerΓÇÖs contribution is less than INR 2000, the actual amount of employerΓÇÖs contribution will be reimbursed.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New Startups and MSMEs (registered or established new subsidiary/branch in Karnataka within the last two years as on application date)

incentive_details.application_deadline: Half-yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year.
incentive_details.application_authority: ESDM Cell, Karnataka Biotechnology and Information Technology Services (KBITS)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Applicable only to registered KESDM Startups and MSMEs that are new companies (registered within the last two years as on the date of application) or companies that have started a new subsidiary or branch office in Karnataka within the last two years as on the date of application.

1.2 Eligibility for Availing Financial Support
To avail these incentives/concessions, an ESDM company must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company. Companies which are already registered under KESDM Policy need not register again under the new policy.
The old KESDM Policy 2013 ceases to exist in view of the new policy 2017-2022 which is announced on 1st December 2017 vide Government Order No. ITD 09 PRM 2017.Any applications for incentives/concessions prior to the Financial Year 2017-18 would not be considered.
For the Financial Year 2017-18, companies can only claim incentives from April 2017 to March 2018 which would be considered under the guidelines of KESDM Policy 2017 -22.
Application for any incentives/concessions for each financial year should be submitted half yearly (only one time) within six months from the end of each half year. If the applications are submitted after this duration it would be rejected. This condition is relaxed for Patent Incentive.
Nature of business:
The company or entity should be engaged in one of the following businesses:
ΓÇó Manufacturing and or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems And Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defence & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment / etc.
ΓÇó Manufacturing of intermediates such as PCBs / semiconductors / chip components / ICs / components
ΓÇó Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)
ΓÇó Design / IP / Software services for electronics products
ΓÇó Any other electronics verticals / products covered by the National Policy on Electronics (NPE) / National Manufacturing Policy (NPM) and related notifications, as issued by the Govt. of India from time to time
Location:
The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
Employment:
The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees.
Value Addition:
The company or entity should do value addition within the state, in-line with the below formulae:
Year 1: Minimum percentage of value addition 25%
Year 2: Minimum percentage of value addition 30%
Year 3: Minimum percentage of value addition 35%
Year 4: Minimum percentage of value addition 40%
Year 5: Minimum percentage of value addition 45%
Product Price (Ex-factory): A
Cost of Bill of Material (BOM) in ΓÇÿAΓÇÖ: B (including software design, IP)

policy_goals: Make Karnataka a preferred investment destination for electronics manufacturing and assembly units

policy_details.policy_summary: The Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (subsequently extended for 5 years from 7th September 2025) by the Government of Karnataka aims to attract investments and boost employment in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector across the state. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the scheme applies to new projects (with a minimum eligible capital expenditure of INR 15 crore on Plant & Machinery) and expansion of existing units (minimum INR 50 crore on P&M) in target segments including electronics products, semiconductors, electronic manufacturing services (EMS), SPECS/PLI eligible products, solar cells, and LED products. The scheme offers a comprehensive package of Capital Investment SubsidiesΓÇöincluding a 20% subsidy on Plant & Machinery, a 25% subsidy on land (up to 50 acres, capped at INR 12.5 crore outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural), and 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, registration charges, and land conversion feesΓÇöalongside Operational Subsidies for 5 years, which include a 1.00% Production Linked Incentive (PLI) on annual net sales turnover, INR 1.00 per unit power tariff reimbursement, and 100% exemption from electricity duty.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 20% capital subsidy on Plant & Machinery, 25% land subsidy up to Γé╣12.5 crore, 100% stamp duty & electricity duty waiver, Γé╣1/unit power subsidy, and 1% Production Linked Incentive for 5 years for ESDM units in Karnataka.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.1 Applicant: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme is a legal entity i.e., Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India, proposing to, and making an application for seeking incentive against investment in a Project / Unit for manufacturing of eligible goods as per the Target Segment under the Scheme mentioned in Section 2.2 of these Guidelines.
2. Eligibility Criteria 
2.1. Applicability of the provisions of the Scheme: 
An Applicant will be permitted to apply for incentives under this Scheme, if the SHLCC/ SLSWCC approval is obtained within the Scheme Period.
2.2. Target Segments
The Applicant under Government of KarnatakaΓÇÖs Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (ΓÇ£SchemeΓÇ¥) should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities (ΓÇ£Eligible Products/ActivitiesΓÇ¥): 
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI). 
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
In case the project/unit in Karnataka involves production of more than one product, only the capex on P&M involved in production falling under the Target segment will be considered eligible under the Scheme.
2.3. Location
a. The Applicant should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
b. A project / unit proposed under the Scheme may include multiple manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations in Karnataka. It will be considered as one project, subject to a) if multiple locations of the Project / Unit are registered with a single GST ID b) prior SLSWCC/SHLCC approval is obtained which clearly identifies this as one Project / Unit. The details of all the units needs to be mentioned in the Common Application Form which need to be in line with the SLSWCC/SHLCC approval document. There is no limit on the number of applications for an Applicant. 
2.4. Employment 
Employment Criteria for enterprises Applicants availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
1. > INR 15 crores: 15 jobs per INR 15 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2. INR 50 to INR 250 crores: 50 jobs per INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
3. INR 250 to INR 500 crores: 200 jobs per INR 250 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
4. Above INR 500 crores: 400 jobs per INR 500 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2.5. Minimum Investment
The minimum investment to be undertaken by the Applicant to be eligible for the Scheme, as measured by Eligible Capital Expenditure is as follows:
1. New Project / Unit: 15 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2. Expansion of Capacity of existing unit: 50 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2.6. Applicability of Incentives
b. Incentives under Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020 ΓÇô 2025 shall be provided only for New Project Unit or Expansion of Capacity of exiting unit. 
c. The incentives under this Scheme can be availed in addition to incentives and subsidies provided under any of the policies of Government of India. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit. Any irregularity / misrepresentation in this regard may disqualify the Applicant from availing any incentives under this Scheme.
d. Maximum incentive amount sanctioned to a single Application under the Scheme shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets. In case of solar cells manufacturing, if Value of Fixed Assets is INR 500 Crore or more, incentives will be capped at 50% of the Value of Fixed Assets. Total incentive disbursement for this category will be capped when total Value of Fixed Assets of firms applying under this category (regardless of number of firms) touches INR 3,000 crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit.
2. The expenditure incurred on building (including factory building / construction) required for the Project / Unit is not covered under the Scheme and, therefore, shall not be considered towards computation of Eligible Capital Expenditure.
3. Expenditure on consumables and raw material used for manufacturing shall not be considered as Capital Expenditure.
4. Any payment, including payment under a Letter of Credit with a bank or any other mode of settlement with vendors, prior to the scheme start date (viz. 7th September 2020) shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M under the Scheme.
5. Self-fabricated plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities, if they are used/ second hand/ refurbished shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure under the Scheme.
6. Applicants or their non-independent directors/promoters/partners/proprietor must not figure in any list of defaulters/willful defaulters/debarred list/fraud list circulated by RBI, CIBIL, SEBI, or any Bank/Financial Institution, must not be declared insolvent/bankrupt, and must not be blacklisted by any Government/Government Agency/PSU/CPSE in India.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.1 Applicant: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme is a legal entity i.e., Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India, proposing to, and making an application for seeking incentive against investment in a Project / Unit for manufacturing of eligible goods as per the Target Segment under the Scheme mentioned in Section 2.2 of these Guidelines.
2. Eligibility Criteria 
2.1. Applicability of the provisions of the Scheme: 
An Applicant will be permitted to apply for incentives under this Scheme, if the SHLCC/ SLSWCC approval is obtained within the Scheme Period.
2.2. Target Segments
The Applicant under Government of KarnatakaΓÇÖs Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (ΓÇ£SchemeΓÇ¥) should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities (ΓÇ£Eligible Products/ActivitiesΓÇ¥): 
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI). 
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
In case the project/unit in Karnataka involves production of more than one product, only the capex on P&M involved in production falling under the Target segment will be considered eligible under the Scheme.
2.3. Location
a. The Applicant should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
b. A project / unit proposed under the Scheme may include multiple manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations in Karnataka. It will be considered as one project, subject to a) if multiple locations of the Project / Unit are registered with a single GST ID b) prior SLSWCC/SHLCC approval is obtained which clearly identifies this as one Project / Unit. The details of all the units needs to be mentioned in the Common Application Form which need to be in line with the SLSWCC/SHLCC approval document. There is no limit on the number of applications for an Applicant. 
2.4. Employment 
Employment Criteria for enterprises Applicants availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
1. > INR 15 crores: 15 jobs per INR 15 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2. INR 50 to INR 250 crores: 50 jobs per INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
3. INR 250 to INR 500 crores: 200 jobs per INR 250 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
4. Above INR 500 crores: 400 jobs per INR 500 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2.5. Minimum Investment
The minimum investment to be undertaken by the Applicant to be eligible for the Scheme, as measured by Eligible Capital Expenditure is as follows:
1. New Project / Unit: 15 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2. Expansion of Capacity of existing unit: 50 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2.6. Applicability of Incentives
b. Incentives under Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020 ΓÇô 2025 shall be provided only for New Project Unit or Expansion of Capacity of exiting unit. 
c. The incentives under this Scheme can be availed in addition to incentives and subsidies provided under any of the policies of Government of India. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit. Any irregularity / misrepresentation in this regard may disqualify the Applicant from availing any incentives under this Scheme.
d. Maximum incentive amount sanctioned to a single Application under the Scheme shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets. In case of solar cells manufacturing, if Value of Fixed Assets is INR 500 Crore or more, incentives will be capped at 50% of the Value of Fixed Assets. Total incentive disbursement for this category will be capped when total Value of Fixed Assets of firms applying under this category (regardless of number of firms) touches INR 3,000 crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit.
2. The expenditure incurred on building (including factory building / construction) required for the Project / Unit is not covered under the Scheme and, therefore, shall not be considered towards computation of Eligible Capital Expenditure.
3. Expenditure on consumables and raw material used for manufacturing shall not be considered as Capital Expenditure.
4. Any payment, including payment under a Letter of Credit with a bank or any other mode of settlement with vendors, prior to the scheme start date (viz. 7th September 2020) shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M under the Scheme.
5. Self-fabricated plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities, if they are used/ second hand/ refurbished shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure under the Scheme.
6. Applicants or their non-independent directors/promoters/partners/proprietor must not figure in any list of defaulters/willful defaulters/debarred list/fraud list circulated by RBI, CIBIL, SEBI, or any Bank/Financial Institution, must not be declared insolvent/bankrupt, and must not be blacklisted by any Government/Government Agency/PSU/CPSE in India.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (subsequently extended for 5 years from 7th September 2025) by the Government of Karnataka aims to attract investments and boost employment in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector across the state. The scheme offers a comprehensive package of Capital Investment SubsidiesΓÇöincluding a 20% subsidy on Plant & Machinery, a 25% subsidy on land (up to 50 acres, capped at INR 12.5 crore outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural), and 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, registration charges, and land conversion feesΓÇöalongside Operational Subsidies for 5 years, which include a 1.00% Production Linked Incentive (PLI) on annual net sales turnover, INR 1.00 per unit power tariff reimbursement, and 100% exemption from electricity duty.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (subsequently extended for 5 years from 7th September 2025) by the Government of Karnataka aims to attract investments and boost employment in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector across the state. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the scheme applies to new projects (with a minimum eligible capital expenditure of INR 15 crore on Plant & Machinery) and expansion of existing units (minimum INR 50 crore on P&M) in target segments including electronics products, semiconductors, electronic manufacturing services (EMS), SPECS/PLI eligible products, solar cells, and LED products. The scheme offers a comprehensive package of Capital Investment SubsidiesΓÇöincluding a 20% subsidy on Plant & Machinery, a 25% subsidy on land (up to 50 acres, capped at INR 12.5 crore outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural), and 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, registration charges, and land conversion feesΓÇöalongside Operational Subsidies for 5 years, which include a 1.00% Production Linked Incentive (PLI) on annual net sales turnover, INR 1.00 per unit power tariff reimbursement, and 100% exemption from electricity duty.
