eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.1 Applicant: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme is a legal entity i.e., Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India, proposing to, and making an application for seeking incentive against investment in a Project / Unit for manufacturing of eligible goods as per the Target Segment under the Scheme mentioned in Section 2.2 of these Guidelines.
2. Eligibility Criteria 
2.1. Applicability of the provisions of the Scheme: 
An Applicant will be permitted to apply for incentives under this Scheme, if the SHLCC/ SLSWCC approval is obtained within the Scheme Period.
2.2. Target Segments
The Applicant under Government of KarnatakaΓÇÖs Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020-2025 (ΓÇ£SchemeΓÇ¥) should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities (ΓÇ£Eligible Products/ActivitiesΓÇ¥): 
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI). 
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
In case the project/unit in Karnataka involves production of more than one product, only the capex on P&M involved in production falling under the Target segment will be considered eligible under the Scheme.
2.3. Location
a. The Applicant should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
b. A project / unit proposed under the Scheme may include multiple manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations in Karnataka. It will be considered as one project, subject to a) if multiple locations of the Project / Unit are registered with a single GST ID b) prior SLSWCC/SHLCC approval is obtained which clearly identifies this as one Project / Unit. The details of all the units needs to be mentioned in the Common Application Form which need to be in line with the SLSWCC/SHLCC approval document. There is no limit on the number of applications for an Applicant. 
2.4. Employment 
Employment Criteria for enterprises Applicants availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
1. > INR 15 crores: 15 jobs per INR 15 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2. INR 50 to INR 250 crores: 50 jobs per INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
3. INR 250 to INR 500 crores: 200 jobs per INR 250 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
4. Above INR 500 crores: 400 jobs per INR 500 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
2.5. Minimum Investment
The minimum investment to be undertaken by the Applicant to be eligible for the Scheme, as measured by Eligible Capital Expenditure is as follows:
1. New Project / Unit: 15 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2. Expansion of Capacity of existing unit: 50 Crore (Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M in INR)
2.6. Applicability of Incentives
b. Incentives under Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020 ΓÇô 2025 shall be provided only for New Project Unit or Expansion of Capacity of exiting unit. 
c. The incentives under this Scheme can be availed in addition to incentives and subsidies provided under any of the policies of Government of India. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit. Any irregularity / misrepresentation in this regard may disqualify the Applicant from availing any incentives under this Scheme.
d. Maximum incentive amount sanctioned to a single Application under the Scheme shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets. In case of solar cells manufacturing, if Value of Fixed Assets is INR 500 Crore or more, incentives will be capped at 50% of the Value of Fixed Assets. Total incentive disbursement for this category will be capped when total Value of Fixed Assets of firms applying under this category (regardless of number of firms) touches INR 3,000 crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project / Unit.
2. The expenditure incurred on building (including factory building / construction) required for the Project / Unit is not covered under the Scheme and, therefore, shall not be considered towards computation of Eligible Capital Expenditure.
3. Expenditure on consumables and raw material used for manufacturing shall not be considered as Capital Expenditure.
4. Any payment, including payment under a Letter of Credit with a bank or any other mode of settlement with vendors, prior to the scheme start date (viz. 7th September 2020) shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure on P&M under the Scheme.
5. Self-fabricated plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities, if they are used/ second hand/ refurbished shall not be considered for determining Eligible Capital Expenditure under the Scheme.
6. Applicants or their non-independent directors/promoters/partners/proprietor must not figure in any list of defaulters/willful defaulters/debarred list/fraud list circulated by RBI, CIBIL, SEBI, or any Bank/Financial Institution, must not be declared insolvent/bankrupt, and must not be blacklisted by any Government/Government Agency/PSU/CPSE in India.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Farmer Producers Organizations Policy-2018 aims to mobilize and collectivize primary agricultural producersΓÇöespecially small, marginal, and medium farmersΓÇöinto Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act 2013 or Cooperative Societies Act. The policy seeks to form at least one FPO in every hobli jurisdiction to collectivize around 5 lakh farmers over five years across agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries, and allied sectors. It outlines a 3-phase implementation strategy: (1) Formation/initial phase (1-2 years) involving mobilization into Farmer Interest Groups (FIGs) and federation into FPOs via Resource Institutions (RIs), supported by grants for registration, management, honorariums, and capacity building; (2) Business incubation/growth phase (2 years) providing working capital, basic infrastructure, APMC sub-yard declaration and trading licenses, land allocation, and access to incubation/stabilization funds; and (3) Maturity/business expansion phase (2 years) facilitating scaling up through Venture Capital, Angel Investors, interest subvention, credit guarantees, and viability gap assistance. FPOs are declared at par with cooperatives to receive equivalent state benefits, given priority allotment of government land for output business, and supported by an institutional framework including a State-level Empowered Committee, Department of Agriculture as Nodal Department, Center of Excellence for FPO (CoE-FPO), and KAPPEC as the FPO Business Development Agency (FPO-BDA).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive lifecycle support for Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in Karnataka including 5-year Union tax exemption, phase-wise grants, working capital and interest subvention, priority government land allotment, and parity with cooperative societies.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Tribal, malnad, and coastal area farmers

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
5. Purview
The provisions of this policy shall be applicable to existing FPOs already registered under the Companies Act 2013 / Cooperative Societies Act and those FPOs that shall be registered subsequent to the issue of this policy. The primary agriculture co-operatives may also aggregate and register as FPOs. FPOs formed in agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries and allied sectors will come under the ambit of this policy. This policy shall be common for all departments and developmental agencies involved in the formation of farmer producer organisations in Karnataka.

6.1. A FPO is a registered company under the Companies Act 2013/Cooperative Societies Act, consisting of farmers who are the primary producers of a particular commodity or group of commodities.

7.1. The FPOs shall initially comprise of 200-500 farmers, which may be upscaled to 1000 members or more. However, FPOs formed in tribal, malnad, coastal and other local specific areas may comprise of lesser numbers also.

7.3. The FPO shall be a business entity with a detailed business plan as well as share capital from all members who are farmers, producing a specified commodity/commodities

7.4. FPOs would be registered as a producer's company under the Companies Act 2013 / Cooperative Societies Act.

8.4.3 Provision of assistance to FPOs who have evolved on their own without any support from the Government and FPOs which are formed with support from NABARD or other agency for output business marketing.

10.1. Sectors under which FPO can be formed: Formation of FPO's will be encouraged in agriculture, horticulture sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries and allied sectors.

10.2. Beneficiaries for formation of FPO: The target beneficiaries of FPOs are farmers with preference to medium, small & marginal farmers, including women farmers.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Farmer Producers Organizations Policy-2018 aims to mobilize and collectivize primary agricultural producersΓÇöespecially small, marginal, and medium farmersΓÇöinto Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act 2013 or Cooperative Societies Act. Mobilising farmers into groups of around 20 members at the village level (FIGs) and building up their associations into FPOs, so as to plan and implement product-specific cluster/commercial crop cycles

Strengthening farmer capacity through training on Good Agricultural Practices (GAPs) and facilitating access to steady and timely supply of quality inputs and services, including credit and insurance for increasing agricultural productivity and enhancing competitiveness at cluster level
Facilitating access to fair and remunerative markets, including linking of FPOs to marketing opportunities
Providing institutional support for capacity building and handholding of FPOs
Develop common guidelines to bring synergies across various departments and for effective implementation and functioning
Create platform for exchange of information, product and services between FPOs and the other stakeholders in the supply and market chain for business networking
Guide in monitoring and evaluation of FPOs
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Farmer Producers Organizations Policy-2018 aims to mobilize and collectivize primary agricultural producersΓÇöespecially small, marginal, and medium farmersΓÇöinto Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act 2013 or Cooperative Societies Act. The policy seeks to form at least one FPO in every hobli jurisdiction to collectivize around 5 lakh farmers over five years across agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries, and allied sectors. It outlines a 3-phase implementation strategy: (1) Formation/initial phase (1-2 years) involving mobilization into Farmer Interest Groups (FIGs) and federation into FPOs via Resource Institutions (RIs), supported by grants for registration, management, honorariums, and capacity building; (2) Business incubation/growth phase (2 years) providing working capital, basic infrastructure, APMC sub-yard declaration and trading licenses, land allocation, and access to incubation/stabilization funds; and (3) Maturity/business expansion phase (2 years) facilitating scaling up through Venture Capital, Angel Investors, interest subvention, credit guarantees, and viability gap assistance. FPOs are declared at par with cooperatives to receive equivalent state benefits, given priority allotment of government land for output business, and supported by an institutional framework including a State-level Empowered Committee, Department of Agriculture as Nodal Department, Center of Excellence for FPO (CoE-FPO), and KAPPEC as the FPO Business Development Agency (FPO-BDA).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive lifecycle support for Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in Karnataka including 5-year Union tax exemption, phase-wise grants, working capital and interest subvention, priority government land allotment, and parity with cooperative societies.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Tribal, malnad, and coastal area farmers

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
5. Purview
The provisions of this policy shall be applicable to existing FPOs already registered under the Companies Act 2013 / Cooperative Societies Act and those FPOs that shall be registered subsequent to the issue of this policy. The primary agriculture co-operatives may also aggregate and register as FPOs. FPOs formed in agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries and allied sectors will come under the ambit of this policy. This policy shall be common for all departments and developmental agencies involved in the formation of farmer producer organisations in Karnataka.

6.1. A FPO is a registered company under the Companies Act 2013/Cooperative Societies Act, consisting of farmers who are the primary producers of a particular commodity or group of commodities.

7.1. The FPOs shall initially comprise of 200-500 farmers, which may be upscaled to 1000 members or more. However, FPOs formed in tribal, malnad, coastal and other local specific areas may comprise of lesser numbers also.

7.3. The FPO shall be a business entity with a detailed business plan as well as share capital from all members who are farmers, producing a specified commodity/commodities

7.4. FPOs would be registered as a producer's company under the Companies Act 2013 / Cooperative Societies Act.

8.4.3 Provision of assistance to FPOs who have evolved on their own without any support from the Government and FPOs which are formed with support from NABARD or other agency for output business marketing.

10.1. Sectors under which FPO can be formed: Formation of FPO's will be encouraged in agriculture, horticulture sericulture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries and allied sectors.

10.2. Beneficiaries for formation of FPO: The target beneficiaries of FPOs are farmers with preference to medium, small & marginal farmers, including women farmers.

policy_goals: To attract establishment of 500 new GCCs in Karnataka achieving a total number of 1,000 GCCs in Karnataka by 2029
To support creation of 3.5 lakh new jobs in Karnataka by 2029
To generate economic output of US$50 billion in Karnataka through the GCCs being established by 2029
Create an investor-friendly business environment for GCCs to establish and expand their operations in Karnataka.
Provide platforms that enable GCCs to collaborate seamlessly with Karnataka's vibrant local innovation ecosystem.
Position Karnataka as a global leader in Artificial Intelligence (AI) with the most comprehensive AI R&D ecosystem tailored for GCCs.
Foster a research and development driven environment focused on emerging technologies and deep-tech, making Karnataka a hub for cutting-edge innovation.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Global Capability Centre (GCC) Policy 2024ΓÇô2029 and its Operational Guidelines aim to reinforce Karnataka's position as India's premier destination for GCCs while promoting balanced regional development through the 'Beyond Bengaluru' initiative (covering clusters such as Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Tumakuru, Shivamogga, and Kalaburagi). The policy targets establishing 500 new GCCs (reaching 1,000 total), creating 3.5 lakh new jobs, and generating US$50 billion in economic output by 2029. It is structured around four pillars: Talent, Local Ecosystem, Infrastructure and Incentives, and Regulatory Easing. Key fiscal offerings include rental assistance up to Γé╣2 crore, EPF reimbursement of Γé╣3,000/month per employee, recruitment assistance up to Γé╣7 crore, 100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years, industrial power tariff concessions, 30% property tax reimbursement, internet expense reimbursement, operational subsidies for co-working spaces, R&D infrastructure grants up to Γé╣50 crore, capex support for Innovation Labs/CoEs up to Γé╣5 crore, startup lab utilization reimbursements, joint research funding, internship stipends, skilling grants, quality certification reimbursements, and patent filing support. Special provisions are also made for Nano GCCs (5-50 employees) in Beyond Bengaluru regions and customized packages for Mega Projects.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive incentives for GCCs in Karnataka including up to 40% R&D infrastructure grant (max Γé╣50 crore), 50% rental reimbursement (up to Γé╣2 crore), 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years, and recruitment assistance up to Γé╣7 crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Beyond Bengaluru regional development (Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Tumakuru, Shivamogga, Kalaburagi)
Equitable internship opportunities for women candidates

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Applicant: Means an entity incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 / a Partnership Firm registered under the Partnership Act 1932 / a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008. Further, the term will also include State Government Universities, its affiliated colleges, and industry associations.
8. Eligible GCC Unit: Means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/ or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year.
14. Existing GCC Unit: Means a GCC unit located in Karnataka that is already operational before the effective date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
15. Global Capability Centre ('GCC'): Global Capability Centre (GCCs) are fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations that are headquartered outside India, to leverage global talent, build intellectual property, and enhance operational efficiency. These centres serve the parent organization, managing a range of global functions like research and development, IT services, business process outsourcing, and more, ultimately driving innovation, reducing costs, value addition, and expanding the corporation's global impact.
19. Mega Enterprise: Means projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and upto INR 1000 crore.
20. Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people.
21. New GCC Unit:
i. Means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
ii. The term also includes one or more GCC unit(s) being set-up by an Existing GCC unit in a different premise or location within Karnataka.
a. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the State and is setting up a new GCC unit in Bengaluru Urban District, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit, provided that number of employees moving or shifting from existing unit to the new unit shall not exceed 20% of total employees of the new unit.
b. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the state and is setting up a new GCC unit in Beyond Bengaluru Districts, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit.
28. Start-up: An entity will be considered as a Start-up on fulfilling below conditions defined by Government of Karnataka (in line with the definition of GoI notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02,2019).
(a) The Startup should be incorporated as a Company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008), having its registered office in Karnataka.
(b) Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores.
(c) An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
4.1 Registration Procedure: 1. GCC entities that are registered with KITS shall only be eligible for availing incentives and offerings under the Policy.
6.21 Incentives for Nano GCCs: Nano GCCs setting up operations during the policy period in the Beyond Bengaluru Region shall be entitled to same incentives as available to other GCCs setting up operations (during the policy period), in the state. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas.

Contractual employees, apprentices, interns, Board of Directors, and Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) are excluded from the definition of 'Employee' on payroll.

minimum_employees.raw_text: Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people. eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Applicant: Means an entity incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 / a Partnership Firm registered under the Partnership Act 1932 / a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008. Further, the term will also include State Government Universities, its affiliated colleges, and industry associations.
8. Eligible GCC Unit: Means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/ or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year.
14. Existing GCC Unit: Means a GCC unit located in Karnataka that is already operational before the effective date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
15. Global Capability Centre ('GCC'): Global Capability Centre (GCCs) are fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations that are headquartered outside India, to leverage global talent, build intellectual property, and enhance operational efficiency. These centres serve the parent organization, managing a range of global functions like research and development, IT services, business process outsourcing, and more, ultimately driving innovation, reducing costs, value addition, and expanding the corporation's global impact.
19. Mega Enterprise: Means projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and upto INR 1000 crore.
20. Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people.
21. New GCC Unit:
i. Means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
ii. The term also includes one or more GCC unit(s) being set-up by an Existing GCC unit in a different premise or location within Karnataka.
a. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the State and is setting up a new GCC unit in Bengaluru Urban District, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit, provided that number of employees moving or shifting from existing unit to the new unit shall not exceed 20% of total employees of the new unit.
b. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the state and is setting up a new GCC unit in Beyond Bengaluru Districts, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit.
28. Start-up: An entity will be considered as a Start-up on fulfilling below conditions defined by Government of Karnataka (in line with the definition of GoI notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02,2019).
(a) The Startup should be incorporated as a Company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008), having its registered office in Karnataka.
(b) Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores.
(c) An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
4.1 Registration Procedure: 1. GCC entities that are registered with KITS shall only be eligible for availing incentives and offerings under the Policy.
6.21 Incentives for Nano GCCs: Nano GCCs setting up operations during the policy period in the Beyond Bengaluru Region shall be entitled to same incentives as available to other GCCs setting up operations (during the policy period), in the state. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GCCs where the value of services provided directly to third parties (other than parent organisation or group affiliates) exceeds 10% of the GCC's revenue in a financial year. For New GCC units set up by an existing GCC in Bengaluru Urban District, units where the number of employees moving or shifting from the existing unit to the new unit exceeds 20% of total employees of the new unit. Contractual employees, apprentices, interns, Board of Directors, and Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) are excluded from the definition of 'Employee' on payroll.

minimum_employees.raw_text: Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas. (Many standard Beyond Bengaluru incentives require New GCCs setting up with 100+ employees; Mega Projects require >5,000 new jobs in Bengaluru or >1,000 new jobs Beyond Bengaluru).

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) must be fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations headquartered outside India. eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Must be located or being set up in Karnataka. Specific incentives are restricted to 'Beyond Bengaluru Districts' (any region in Karnataka other than Bengaluru Urban District, such as Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Mangaluru, Tumakuru, Shivamogga, and Kalaburagi) or 'Bengaluru Urban District' (Bengaluru North, Bengaluru North (Additional)/Yelahanka, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru East and Anekal).

special_category_benefits: Nano GCCs (5 to 50 employees in Beyond Bengaluru areas exempt from 100+ employee threshold)

incentive_details.description: Proposal-based funding to empower GCCs with access to government departments to pilot and deploy innovative digital solutions addressing critical public service challenges and societal issues. Government will fund 5 challenges every year.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Grant up to Γé╣1.50 Crores per challenge (for 5 challenges annually) for GCCs deploying innovative solutions to public service challenges.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply against KITS Call for Proposal (Section 7.14.1 & 7.14.8) with detailed solution roadmap, timelines, team profile, 5-minute MVP demo video, and project cost. Shortlisted applicants pitch before the Executive Committee.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: capping of INR 1.50 Crores for the deployment of a solution
quantified_benefits.conditions: Company must mandatorily have a functional prototype / Minimum Viable Product (MVP) ready for field test/pilot; pilot must be completed within 12-15 months from approval; tri-partite MoA signed between applicant, line department, and KITS; availed once per applicant.
quantified_benefits.description: Funding for pilot and deployment cost (hardware, software tools, networking, manpower, servers, prototyping, testing, certifications) of a solution to a public service challenge.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Government will fund 05 challenges every year, (with a capping of INR 1.50 Crores for the deployment of a solution).
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New and Existing GCC units across Karnataka (5 challenges funded per year)

incentive_details.application_deadline: In response to Call for Proposal issued by KITS.
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Executive Committee
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: New and Existing GCC units with a ready functional prototype / Minimum Viable Product (MVP).

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: up to a maximum of INR 2 Lakh per domestic patent

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Applicant: Means an entity incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 / a Partnership Firm registered under the Partnership Act 1932 / a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008. Further, the term will also include State Government Universities, its affiliated colleges, and industry associations.
8. Eligible GCC Unit: Means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/ or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year.
14. Existing GCC Unit: Means a GCC unit located in Karnataka that is already operational before the effective date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
15. Global Capability Centre ('GCC'): Global Capability Centre (GCCs) are fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations that are headquartered outside India, to leverage global talent, build intellectual property, and enhance operational efficiency. These centres serve the parent organization, managing a range of global functions like research and development, IT services, business process outsourcing, and more, ultimately driving innovation, reducing costs, value addition, and expanding the corporation's global impact.
19. Mega Enterprise: Means projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and upto INR 1000 crore.
20. Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people.
21. New GCC Unit:
i. Means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
ii. The term also includes one or more GCC unit(s) being set-up by an Existing GCC unit in a different premise or location within Karnataka.
a. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the State and is setting up a new GCC unit in Bengaluru Urban District, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit, provided that number of employees moving or shifting from existing unit to the new unit shall not exceed 20% of total employees of the new unit.
b. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the state and is setting up a new GCC unit in Beyond Bengaluru Districts, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit.
28. Start-up: An entity will be considered as a Start-up on fulfilling below conditions defined by Government of Karnataka (in line with the definition of GoI notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02,2019).
(a) The Startup should be incorporated as a Company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008), having its registered office in Karnataka.
(b) Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores.
(c) An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
4.1 Registration Procedure: 1. GCC entities that are registered with KITS shall only be eligible for availing incentives and offerings under the Policy.
6.21 Incentives for Nano GCCs: Nano GCCs setting up operations during the policy period in the Beyond Bengaluru Region shall be entitled to same incentives as available to other GCCs setting up operations (during the policy period), in the state. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GCCs where the value of services provided directly to third parties (other than parent organisation or group affiliates) exceeds 10% of the GCC's revenue in a financial year. For New GCC units set up by an existing GCC in Bengaluru Urban District, units where the number of employees moving or shifting from the existing unit to the new unit exceeds 20% of total employees of the new unit. Contractual employees, apprentices, interns, Board of Directors, and Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) are excluded from the definition of 'Employee' on payroll.

minimum_employees.raw_text: Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people. (Many standard Beyond Bengaluru incentives require New GCCs setting up with 100+ employees; Mega Projects require >5,000 new jobs in Bengaluru or >1,000 new jobs Beyond Bengaluru).

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) must be fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations headquartered outside India. incentive_details.application_process: Submit proposal as per Section 7.14.1 & 7.14.7 with entity profiles, detailed project proposal, budget & funding structure, milestone timeline, IP sharing strategy, and MoU/Letter of Consent.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: capped at INR 1 Crore (Summary table also notes up to INR 75 lakh and up to INR 1 crore for projects with two institutions)

quantified_benefits.description: Government funding of 50% of the approved joint research project budget (Capex on equipment, software, testing instruments, IP, and up to 10% manpower expenses).

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New GCCs, Existing GCCs, and State Government Universities / Affiliated / Colleges across Karnataka (up to 5 projects annually)

incentive_details.application_deadline: In response to Call for Proposal / EOI issued by KITS.
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Executive Committee
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Joint participation of a New/Existing GCC and State Government Universities/Affiliated Colleges in Karnataka.

incentive_details.description: Option for New GCC entities registered with KITS across the State to switch between commercial and industrial power tariffs, depending on whichever is financially feasible, in accordance with KERC tariff orders.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Option for New GCCs across Karnataka to switch from commercial to lower industrial power tariffs.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply to KITS using Form 7.5.1 with ESCOM power service letter, last 3 months electricity bills, and lease/ownership deed. After KITS inspection and committee approval, KITS issues a PTC sanction letter to the Associate Executive Engineer (AEE) of the concerned ESCOM.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Option to switch between commercial and industrial power tariffs
quantified_benefits.conditions: RR No. must be in applicant's name, or applicant must be sole occupant of developer-owned premise, or have an ESCOM-installed submeter in a multi-tenant building; no litigation pending with ESCOMs or Dept of IT & Bt.
quantified_benefits.description: Concession allowing GCCs to switch from commercial power tariffs to industrial power tariffs.
quantified_benefits.source_text: GCCs will have the option to switch between commercial and industrial power tariffs, depending on whichever is financially feasible.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New GCCs across the State (Bengaluru Urban District and Beyond Bengaluru Districts)

incentive_details.application_deadline: During the policy period.
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) and concerned ESCOM (BESCOM, MESCOM, HESCOM, GESCOM, CESC)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: New GCCs across the State. Applicant or associated subsidiaries/affiliates must not be under litigation/court cases with ESCOMs or Dept of IT & Bt. Multi-tenant occupants without an ESCOM submeter are ineligible.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Applicant: Means an entity incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 / a Partnership Firm registered under the Partnership Act 1932 / a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008. Further, the term will also include State Government Universities, its affiliated colleges, and industry associations.
8. Eligible GCC Unit: Means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/ or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year.
14. Existing GCC Unit: Means a GCC unit located in Karnataka that is already operational before the effective date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
15. Global Capability Centre ('GCC'): Global Capability Centre (GCCs) are fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations that are headquartered outside India, to leverage global talent, build intellectual property, and enhance operational efficiency. These centres serve the parent organization, managing a range of global functions like research and development, IT services, business process outsourcing, and more, ultimately driving innovation, reducing costs, value addition, and expanding the corporation's global impact.
19. Mega Enterprise: Means projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and upto INR 1000 crore.
20. Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people.
21. New GCC Unit:
i. Means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
ii. The term also includes one or more GCC unit(s) being set-up by an Existing GCC unit in a different premise or location within Karnataka.
a. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the State and is setting up a new GCC unit in Bengaluru Urban District, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit, provided that number of employees moving or shifting from existing unit to the new unit shall not exceed 20% of total employees of the new unit.
b. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the state and is setting up a new GCC unit in Beyond Bengaluru Districts, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit.
28. Start-up: An entity will be considered as a Start-up on fulfilling below conditions defined by Government of Karnataka (in line with the definition of GoI notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02,2019).
(a) The Startup should be incorporated as a Company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008), having its registered office in Karnataka.
(b) Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores.
(c) An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
4.1 Registration Procedure: 1. GCC entities that are registered with KITS shall only be eligible for availing incentives and offerings under the Policy.
6.21 Incentives for Nano GCCs: Nano GCCs setting up operations during the policy period in the Beyond Bengaluru Region shall be entitled to same incentives as available to other GCCs setting up operations (during the policy period), in the state. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GCCs where the value of services provided directly to third parties (other than parent organisation or group affiliates) exceeds 10% of the GCC's revenue in a financial year. For New GCC units set up by an existing GCC in Bengaluru Urban District, units where the number of employees moving or shifting from the existing unit to the new unit exceeds 20% of total employees of the new unit. Contractual employees, apprentices, interns, Board of Directors, and Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) are excluded from the definition of 'Employee' on payroll.

minimum_employees.raw_text: Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas. (Many standard Beyond Bengaluru incentives require New GCCs setting up with 100+ employees; Mega Projects require >5,000 new jobs in Bengaluru or >1,000 new jobs Beyond Bengaluru).

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) must be fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations headquartered outside India. policy_goals: To attract establishment of 500 new GCCs in Karnataka achieving a total number of 1,000 GCCs in Karnataka by 2029
To support creation of 3.5 lakh new jobs in Karnataka by 2029
To generate economic output of US$50 billion in Karnataka through the GCCs being established by 2029
Create an investor-friendly business environment for GCCs to establish and expand their operations in Karnataka.
Provide platforms that enable GCCs to collaborate seamlessly with Karnataka's vibrant local innovation ecosystem.
Position Karnataka as a global leader in Artificial Intelligence (AI) with the most comprehensive AI R&D ecosystem tailored for GCCs.
Foster a research and development driven environment focused on emerging technologies and deep-tech, making Karnataka a hub for cutting-edge innovation.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Global Capability Centre (GCC) Policy 2024ΓÇô2029 and its Operational Guidelines aim to reinforce Karnataka's position as India's premier destination for GCCs while promoting balanced regional development through the 'Beyond Bengaluru' initiative (covering clusters such as Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Tumakuru, Shivamogga, and Kalaburagi). The policy targets establishing 500 new GCCs (reaching 1,000 total), creating 3.5 lakh new jobs, and generating US$50 billion in economic output by 2029. It is structured around four pillars: Talent, Local Ecosystem, Infrastructure and Incentives, and Regulatory Easing. Key fiscal offerings include rental assistance up to Γé╣2 crore, EPF reimbursement of Γé╣3,000/month per employee, recruitment assistance up to Γé╣7 crore, 100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years, industrial power tariff concessions, 30% property tax reimbursement, internet expense reimbursement, operational subsidies for co-working spaces, R&D infrastructure grants up to Γé╣50 crore, capex support for Innovation Labs/CoEs up to Γé╣5 crore, startup lab utilization reimbursements, joint research funding, internship stipends, skilling grants, quality certification reimbursements, and patent filing support. Special provisions are also made for Nano GCCs (5-50 employees) in Beyond Bengaluru regions and customized packages for Mega Projects.

incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 40% grant on approved R&D capex budget or Γé╣50 Crores (whichever is less) for establishing emerging tech testing and prototyping facilities.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online via https://eitbt.karnataka.gov.in/ against KITS Call for Proposal (Section 7.14.1 & 7.14.2) with detailed concept note, Capex/Opex budget, Chartered Engineer certificate for 30% AI allocation, and timelines. quantified_benefits.conditions: Proposal-based approval by Executive Committee; 30% of total allocation must be dedicated to AI and related facilities (certified by a Chartered Engineer); only Capex incurred after 03.12.2024 is eligible (land purchase excluded if grant is financial).
quantified_benefits.description: Grant of 40% of approved R&D capex budget (including equipment, software, testing instruments, IP/patents, and up to 10% manpower costs) or INR 50 Crores, whichever is less.
quantified_benefits.source_text: 40% of approved budget or INR 50 Crores (whichever is less), for establishing testing and prototyping facilities for emerging technologies. Assistance available in form of land, building or financial assistance.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New and Existing GCCs setting up with 100+ employees (and Nano GCCs in Beyond Bengaluru) across the State (max 3 GCCs during policy period)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Applicant: Means an entity incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 / a Partnership Firm registered under the Partnership Act 1932 / a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008. Further, the term will also include State Government Universities, its affiliated colleges, and industry associations.
8. Eligible GCC Unit: Means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/ or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year.
14. Existing GCC Unit: Means a GCC unit located in Karnataka that is already operational before the effective date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
15. Global Capability Centre ('GCC'): Global Capability Centre (GCCs) are fully owned, integrated hubs established by multinational corporations that are headquartered outside India, to leverage global talent, build intellectual property, and enhance operational efficiency. These centres serve the parent organization, managing a range of global functions like research and development, IT services, business process outsourcing, and more, ultimately driving innovation, reducing costs, value addition, and expanding the corporation's global impact.
19. Mega Enterprise: Means projects with an investment in fixed assets above INR 300 crore and upto INR 1000 crore.
20. Nano GCC Unit: Means a GCC Unit, operating as a R&D unit, in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the policy (i.e., 03.12.2024), and employs between 5 to 50 people.
21. New GCC Unit:
i. Means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (i.e. 03.12.2024).
ii. The term also includes one or more GCC unit(s) being set-up by an Existing GCC unit in a different premise or location within Karnataka.
a. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the State and is setting up a new GCC unit in Bengaluru Urban District, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit, provided that number of employees moving or shifting from existing unit to the new unit shall not exceed 20% of total employees of the new unit.
b. If an entity has an existing GCC unit in the state and is setting up a new GCC unit in Beyond Bengaluru Districts, then such new unit shall be eligible for incentives as New GCC Unit.
28. Start-up: An entity will be considered as a Start-up on fulfilling below conditions defined by Government of Karnataka (in line with the definition of GoI notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02,2019).
(a) The Startup should be incorporated as a Company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008), having its registered office in Karnataka.
(b) Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores.
(c) An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation.
4.1 Registration Procedure: 1. GCC entities that are registered with KITS shall only be eligible for availing incentives and offerings under the Policy.
6.21 Incentives for Nano GCCs: Nano GCCs setting up operations during the policy period in the Beyond Bengaluru Region shall be entitled to same incentives as available to other GCCs setting up operations (during the policy period), in the state. Further, the requirement of minimum 100 employees shall not be applicable to Nano GCCs setting up operations in Beyond Bengaluru areas.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GCCs where the value of services provided directly to third parties (other than parent organisation or group affiliates) exceeds 10% of the GCC's revenue in a financial year. For New GCC units set up by an existing GCC in Bengaluru Urban District, units where the number of employees moving or shifting from the existing unit to the new unit exceeds 20% of total employees of the new unit. Contractual employees, apprentices, interns, Board of Directors, and Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) are excluded from the definition of 'Employee' on payroll.

incentive_name: Base Subsidy for Medium Industries (Capital Subsidy or Production Linked Incentive)

policy_goals: To position Karnataka as the #1 destination for High-technology manufacturing investments in Asia through equitable and sustainable development.

To establish an investor-friendly ecosystem in Karnataka by fostering a conducive manufacturing environment through collaboration with the industry and developing human capital to meet the industry's demands.
Attracting investments of INR 7,50,000 Cr across the sectors, generating approximately 20,00,000 new jobs during the Policy Period, and attaining leadership in sunrise sectors in the State.
Achieve an accelerated annual growth rate of 12% for the manufacturing sector with an investment target of INR 7,50,000 Cr
Provide flexibility in incentives to stimulate interest from players across the sectors targeted by Industrial Policy
Create employment opportunities for 20,00,000 people by 2030

Become a pioneer in sustainability by incentivizing green and sustainable initiatives by investors: Offer sustainability-linked incentives to promote green measures by the existing and new investors while also promoting green industrial areas

Balanced and Inclusive Regional Development of Karnataka: Differential incentives for different regions of Karnataka based on the level of industrial growth; Rationalization of minimum employment threshold with employment booster and additional incentives for women participation in the workforce
Attain Leadership in sunrise and new age sectors: Focus on innovation driver sectors like ESDM, Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace and Defence, Future Mobility, Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality, etc
Create a seamless experience for investors by digital enablement of Single Window System and dedicated Nodal Officers
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme provides comprehensive financial and non-financial support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Karnataka. Micro and Small enterprises receive Capital Subsidy (10% to 35% of VFA) disbursed in 2 installments, with enhanced rates and caps for Special Category entrepreneurs (SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, Ex-Servicemen). Medium enterprises can choose between Capital Subsidy (10% to 25% of VFA up to INR 10 Cr, disbursed in 4 annual installments) or Production Linked Incentives (1.0% to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years, capped at 30% to 60% of VFA). Additional top-up subsidies apply in Most Backward and More Backward Taluks. Additional support includes Stamp Duty exemption (75% to 100%), concessional registration charges (INR 1/1000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% to 100%), Electricity Tariff Tax exemption (100% for 4 to 8 years), Power Subsidy for Micro and Small units (INR 1.00/unit for 3 years in Zones 1 & 2), 50% reimbursement up to INR 5 Lakh each for Quality Certifications and Export Readiness Certifications, up to INR 5 Lakh subsidy for Industry 5.0 implementation, public procurement preferences (15% price preference), and dedicated SC/ST entrepreneurial support under SCP/TSP (75% land subsidy, 60% bank loan subsidy, soft seed capital, Rs 2/unit power subsidy).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% Capital Subsidy for Micro & Small units and up to 25% Capital Subsidy (up to Γé╣10 Cr) or 2.5% PLI for Medium units, plus 100% stamp duty & electricity tax exemptions, Γé╣1/unit power subsidy, and Γé╣5 Lakh certification grants.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Backward taluks (Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee Report)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: As per the MSMED Act, 2006, MSMEs have been defined as follows: Micro Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 1 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 5 crore. Small Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 10 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 50 crore. Medium Enterprises ΓÇô Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 50 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 250 crore. For the calculation purpose of incentives for MSMEs, the following definitions will be used irrespective of the definitions under the MSMED Act or future Government of India Guidelines: Micro: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment < INR 1 Crore (Upto 1). Small: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 1 Crore to INR 10 Crore (>1-10). Medium: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 10 Crore to INR 50 Crore (>10-50). Existing Enterprise: Additional investment of at least 25% of existing fixed assets. Special Category Units: Units established exclusively by an SC / ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged & Ex-Servicemen Entrepreneurs as a proprietary concern or all the partners or directors of the partnership firm / Co-operative Society/Private limited companies or any other legal entity belonging to above-mentioned categories respectively. Eligible MSMEs shall commence commercial production within 3 years from the date of approval from the DLSWCC/SLSWCC. All new industrial investment projects shall create the maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 (29 excluded activities such as breweries, tobacco, sawmills, etc., except for ETP investments). Micro and Small service enterprises are excluded from Annexure 4 service package. Units in Zone 3 outside Bengaluru Rural are excluded from Capital Subsidy/PLI. Trading and resale turnover excluded.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Must commence commercial production within 3 years from DLSWCC/SLSWCC approval or possession of land/building. Name board of the unit must have minimum 60% of the upper portion in Kannada language. For Small and Medium enterprises in rented/leased premises, registered rent/lease agreement for a minimum period of 10 years is required (renewal basis accepted for Micro enterprises). Wherever MSMEs avail any kind of subsidy or grant on fixed assets under any other GoK/GoI schemes, only differential amount of subsidy would be sanctioned.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Capital Subsidy and PLI in Zone 3 are limited only to Bengaluru Rural District. Power subsidy for Micro & Small enterprises is applicable in Zone 1 & Zone 2 only. Special Category MSMEs get 75% Stamp Duty/Land Conversion exemption and 4 years Electricity Tax exemption in Zone 3.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration Certificate. Separate GST registration for Medium enterprises claiming PLI. Export enterprises must hold Importer Exporter Code (IEC) for export certification support.

incentive_details.application_process: Submit Annexure-12.1 and Annexure-12.2 to DIC. For PLI release, submit annual turnover certificate certified by GST Auditor in Annexure-12.10 based on Row 5N of GSTR 9.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme provides comprehensive financial and non-financial support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Karnataka. Micro and Small enterprises receive Capital Subsidy (10% to 35% of VFA) disbursed in 2 installments, with enhanced rates and caps for Special Category entrepreneurs (SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, Ex-Servicemen). Medium enterprises can choose between Capital Subsidy (10% to 25% of VFA up to INR 10 Cr, disbursed in 4 annual installments) or Production Linked Incentives (1.0% to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years, capped at 30% to 60% of VFA). Additional top-up subsidies apply in Most Backward and More Backward Taluks. Additional support includes Stamp Duty exemption (75% to 100%), concessional registration charges (INR 1/1000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% to 100%), Electricity Tariff Tax exemption (100% for 4 to 8 years), Power Subsidy for Micro and Small units (INR 1.00/unit for 3 years in Zones 1 & 2), 50% reimbursement up to INR 5 Lakh each for Quality Certifications and Export Readiness Certifications, up to INR 5 Lakh subsidy for Industry 5.0 implementation, public procurement preferences (15% price preference), and dedicated SC/ST entrepreneurial support under SCP/TSP (75% land subsidy, 60% bank loan subsidy, soft seed capital, Rs 2/unit power subsidy).

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: As per the MSMED Act, 2006, MSMEs have been defined as follows: Micro Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 1 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 5 crore. Small Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 10 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 50 crore. Medium Enterprises ΓÇô Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 50 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 250 crore. For the calculation purpose of incentives for MSMEs, the following definitions will be used irrespective of the definitions under the MSMED Act or future Government of India Guidelines: Micro: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment < INR 1 Crore (Upto 1). Small: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 1 Crore to INR 10 Crore (>1-10). Medium: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 10 Crore to INR 50 Crore (>10-50). Existing Enterprise: Additional investment of at least 25% of existing fixed assets. Special Category Units: Units established exclusively by an SC / ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged & Ex-Servicemen Entrepreneurs as a proprietary concern or all the partners or directors of the partnership firm / Co-operative Society/Private limited companies or any other legal entity belonging to above-mentioned categories respectively. Eligible MSMEs shall commence commercial production within 3 years from the date of approval from the DLSWCC/SLSWCC. All new industrial investment projects shall create the maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 (29 excluded activities such as breweries, tobacco, sawmills, etc., except for ETP investments). Micro and Small service enterprises are excluded from Annexure 4 service package. Units in Zone 3 outside Bengaluru Rural are excluded from Capital Subsidy/PLI. Trading and resale turnover excluded.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Must commence commercial production within 3 years from DLSWCC/SLSWCC approval or possession of land/building. Name board of the unit must have minimum 60% of the upper portion in Kannada language. For Small and Medium enterprises in rented/leased premises, registered rent/lease agreement for a minimum period of 10 years is required (renewal basis accepted for Micro enterprises). Wherever MSMEs avail any kind of subsidy or grant on fixed assets under any other GoK/GoI schemes, only differential amount of subsidy would be sanctioned.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Capital Subsidy and PLI in Zone 3 are limited only to Bengaluru Rural District. Power subsidy for Micro & Small enterprises is applicable in Zone 1 & Zone 2 only. Special Category MSMEs get 75% Stamp Duty/Land Conversion exemption and 4 years Electricity Tax exemption in Zone 3.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration Certificate. Separate GST registration for Medium enterprises claiming PLI. Export enterprises must hold Importer Exporter Code (IEC) for export certification support.

policy_goals: To position Karnataka as the #1 destination for High-technology manufacturing investments in Asia through equitable and sustainable development.

To establish an investor-friendly ecosystem in Karnataka by fostering a conducive manufacturing environment through collaboration with the industry and developing human capital to meet the industry's demands.
Attracting investments of INR 7,50,000 Cr across the sectors, generating approximately 20,00,000 new jobs during the Policy Period, and attaining leadership in sunrise sectors in the State.
Achieve an accelerated annual growth rate of 12% for the manufacturing sector with an investment target of INR 7,50,000 Cr
Provide flexibility in incentives to stimulate interest from players across the sectors targeted by Industrial Policy
Create employment opportunities for 20,00,000 people by 2030

Become a pioneer in sustainability by incentivizing green and sustainable initiatives by investors: Offer sustainability-linked incentives to promote green measures by the existing and new investors while also promoting green industrial areas

Balanced and Inclusive Regional Development of Karnataka: Differential incentives for different regions of Karnataka based on the level of industrial growth; Rationalization of minimum employment threshold with employment booster and additional incentives for women participation in the workforce
Attain Leadership in sunrise and new age sectors: Focus on innovation driver sectors like ESDM, Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace and Defence, Future Mobility, Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality, etc
Create a seamless experience for investors by digital enablement of Single Window System and dedicated Nodal Officers
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme provides comprehensive financial and non-financial support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Karnataka. Micro and Small enterprises receive Capital Subsidy (10% to 35% of VFA) disbursed in 2 installments, with enhanced rates and caps for Special Category entrepreneurs (SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, Ex-Servicemen). Medium enterprises can choose between Capital Subsidy (10% to 25% of VFA up to INR 10 Cr, disbursed in 4 annual installments) or Production Linked Incentives (1.0% to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years, capped at 30% to 60% of VFA). Additional top-up subsidies apply in Most Backward and More Backward Taluks. Additional support includes Stamp Duty exemption (75% to 100%), concessional registration charges (INR 1/1000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% to 100%), Electricity Tariff Tax exemption (100% for 4 to 8 years), Power Subsidy for Micro and Small units (INR 1.00/unit for 3 years in Zones 1 & 2), 50% reimbursement up to INR 5 Lakh each for Quality Certifications and Export Readiness Certifications, up to INR 5 Lakh subsidy for Industry 5.0 implementation, public procurement preferences (15% price preference), and dedicated SC/ST entrepreneurial support under SCP/TSP (75% land subsidy, 60% bank loan subsidy, soft seed capital, Rs 2/unit power subsidy).

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme provides comprehensive financial and non-financial support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Karnataka. Micro and Small enterprises receive Capital Subsidy (10% to 35% of VFA) disbursed in 2 installments, with enhanced rates and caps for Special Category entrepreneurs (SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, Ex-Servicemen). Medium enterprises can choose between Capital Subsidy (10% to 25% of VFA up to INR 10 Cr, disbursed in 4 annual installments) or Production Linked Incentives (1.0% to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years, capped at 30% to 60% of VFA). Additional top-up subsidies apply in Most Backward and More Backward Taluks. Additional support includes Stamp Duty exemption (75% to 100%), concessional registration charges (INR 1/1000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% to 100%), Electricity Tariff Tax exemption (100% for 4 to 8 years), Power Subsidy for Micro and Small units (INR 1.00/unit for 3 years in Zones 1 & 2), 50% reimbursement up to INR 5 Lakh each for Quality Certifications and Export Readiness Certifications, up to INR 5 Lakh subsidy for Industry 5.0 implementation, public procurement preferences (15% price preference), and dedicated SC/ST entrepreneurial support under SCP/TSP (75% land subsidy, 60% bank loan subsidy, soft seed capital, Rs 2/unit power subsidy).

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: As per the MSMED Act, 2006, MSMEs have been defined as follows: Micro Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 1 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 5 crore. Small Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 10 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 50 crore. Medium Enterprises ΓÇô Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 50 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 250 crore. For the calculation purpose of incentives for MSMEs, the following definitions will be used irrespective of the definitions under the MSMED Act or future Government of India Guidelines: Micro: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment < INR 1 Crore (Upto 1). Small: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 1 Crore to INR 10 Crore (>1-10). Medium: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 10 Crore to INR 50 Crore (>10-50). Existing Enterprise: Additional investment of at least 25% of existing fixed assets. Special Category Units: Units established exclusively by an SC / ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged & Ex-Servicemen Entrepreneurs as a proprietary concern or all the partners or directors of the partnership firm / Co-operative Society/Private limited companies or any other legal entity belonging to above-mentioned categories respectively. Eligible MSMEs shall commence commercial production within 3 years from the date of approval from the DLSWCC/SLSWCC. All new industrial investment projects shall create the maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 (29 excluded activities such as breweries, tobacco, sawmills, etc., except for ETP investments). Micro and Small service enterprises are excluded from Annexure 4 service package. Units in Zone 3 outside Bengaluru Rural are excluded from Capital Subsidy/PLI. Trading and resale turnover excluded.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Must commence commercial production within 3 years from DLSWCC/SLSWCC approval or possession of land/building. Name board of the unit must have minimum 60% of the upper portion in Kannada language. For Small and Medium enterprises in rented/leased premises, registered rent/lease agreement for a minimum period of 10 years is required (renewal basis accepted for Micro enterprises). Wherever MSMEs avail any kind of subsidy or grant on fixed assets under any other GoK/GoI schemes, only differential amount of subsidy would be sanctioned.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Capital Subsidy and PLI in Zone 3 are limited only to Bengaluru Rural District. Power subsidy for Micro & Small enterprises is applicable in Zone 1 & Zone 2 only. Special Category MSMEs get 75% Stamp Duty/Land Conversion exemption and 4 years Electricity Tax exemption in Zone 3.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration Certificate. Separate GST registration for Medium enterprises claiming PLI. Export enterprises must hold Importer Exporter Code (IEC) for export certification support.

incentive_details.benefit_headline: 15% price preference, free tender sets, EMD exemption, and 20% mandatory procurement reservation for Micro & Small Enterprises in Government & PSU purchases.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Registered with Department of Industries & Commerce with UAM / Registration Certificate / Udyam Registration
quantified_benefits.description: Price preference for goods manufactured by Micro & Small Enterprises located in the State against Large & Medium Enterprises of the State and enterprises of other States during Government Department purchases
quantified_benefits.source_text: Goods manufactured by Micro & Small Enterprises located in the State will be allowed a price preference of 15% against the Large & Medium Enterprises / Industries of the State and enterprises/industries of other States during the Government DepartmentΓÇÖs purchases.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Micro & Small Enterprises located in Karnataka

quantified_benefits.description: Free tender sets and exemption from earnest money deposit (EMD) during purchases by Government Departments and State-owned PSUs
quantified_benefits.source_text: To reduce the transaction cost of doing business, Micro & Small Enterprises registered with NSIC under a single point vendor registration scheme shall be facilitated by providing them tender sets free of cost, exempting from payment of earnest money during purchases by all Government Departments and State-owned PSUs.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Micro & Small Enterprises registered with NSIC under single point vendor registration scheme

incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Public Procurement Portal / Government Departments and State-owned PSUs
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Micro & Small Enterprises located within Karnataka and registered with Udyam / NSIC.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme provides comprehensive financial and non-financial support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Karnataka. Micro and Small enterprises receive Capital Subsidy (10% to 35% of VFA) disbursed in 2 installments, with enhanced rates and caps for Special Category entrepreneurs (SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, Ex-Servicemen). Medium enterprises can choose between Capital Subsidy (10% to 25% of VFA up to INR 10 Cr, disbursed in 4 annual installments) or Production Linked Incentives (1.0% to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years, capped at 30% to 60% of VFA). Additional top-up subsidies apply in Most Backward and More Backward Taluks. Additional support includes Stamp Duty exemption (75% to 100%), concessional registration charges (INR 1/1000), Land Conversion Fee reimbursement (75% to 100%), Electricity Tariff Tax exemption (100% for 4 to 8 years), Power Subsidy for Micro and Small units (INR 1.00/unit for 3 years in Zones 1 & 2), 50% reimbursement up to INR 5 Lakh each for Quality Certifications and Export Readiness Certifications, up to INR 5 Lakh subsidy for Industry 5.0 implementation, public procurement preferences (15% price preference), and dedicated SC/ST entrepreneurial support under SCP/TSP (75% land subsidy, 60% bank loan subsidy, soft seed capital, Rs 2/unit power subsidy).

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: As per the MSMED Act, 2006, MSMEs have been defined as follows: Micro Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 1 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 5 crore. Small Enterprises- Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 10 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 50 crore. Medium Enterprises ΓÇô Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment does not exceed INR 50 crore and turnover does not exceed INR 250 crore. For the calculation purpose of incentives for MSMEs, the following definitions will be used irrespective of the definitions under the MSMED Act or future Government of India Guidelines: Micro: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment < INR 1 Crore (Upto 1). Small: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 1 Crore to INR 10 Crore (>1-10). Medium: Investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment between INR 10 Crore to INR 50 Crore (>10-50). Existing Enterprise: Additional investment of at least 25% of existing fixed assets. Special Category Units: Units established exclusively by an SC / ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged & Ex-Servicemen Entrepreneurs as a proprietary concern or all the partners or directors of the partnership firm / Co-operative Society/Private limited companies or any other legal entity belonging to above-mentioned categories respectively. Eligible MSMEs shall commence commercial production within 3 years from the date of approval from the DLSWCC/SLSWCC. All new industrial investment projects shall create the maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 (29 excluded activities such as breweries, tobacco, sawmills, etc., except for ETP investments). Micro and Small service enterprises are excluded from Annexure 4 service package. Units in Zone 3 outside Bengaluru Rural are excluded from Capital Subsidy/PLI. Trading and resale turnover excluded.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Must commence commercial production within 3 years from DLSWCC/SLSWCC approval or possession of land/building. Name board of the unit must have minimum 60% of the upper portion in Kannada language. For Small and Medium enterprises in rented/leased premises, registered rent/lease agreement for a minimum period of 10 years is required (renewal basis accepted for Micro enterprises). Wherever MSMEs avail any kind of subsidy or grant on fixed assets under any other GoK/GoI schemes, only differential amount of subsidy would be sanctioned.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Capital Subsidy and PLI in Zone 3 are limited only to Bengaluru Rural District. Power subsidy for Micro & Small enterprises is applicable in Zone 1 & Zone 2 only. Special Category MSMEs get 75% Stamp Duty/Land Conversion exemption and 4 years Electricity Tax exemption in Zone 3.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration Certificate. Separate GST registration for Medium enterprises claiming PLI. Export enterprises must hold Importer Exporter Code (IEC) for export certification support.
