policy_name: Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
incentive_name: Central Financial Assistance and Concessional Custom Duty Extension

policy_goals: To continue Karnataka State's position as a preferred investment destination in the RE sector and create an ecosystem for sustainable and green energy development in the State.
To facilitate development of 10 (Ten) GW of additional RE projects with or without energy storage systems in the State, including up to 1(One) GW of Rooftop solar PV projects
To attract investment in the RE sector and development of State economy
To tap RE potential in the State and use of available resources for development of RE projects for the purpose of meeting the RE demand within the State and exporting power outside Karnataka
To achieve the RPO target(s) as specified by the KERC from time to time
To develop Renewable Energy Parks including hybrid parks in the State
To encourage private sector participation in transmission network/Green Energy Corridor projects

To develop ecosystem for distributed generation through Solarization of agriculture feeders and pumps which can help deferment of transmission and distribution capacity addition and reduction in losses
To promote adaptation of electric vehicles and de-carbonize transportation in the State by encouraging use of cleaner renewable energy in the transportation sector
To promote energy storage projects in the State

To create energy storage market in the State to integrate more RE into the grid and offer grid support services such as peak reduction, curtailment management, contribution to reliability needs, transmission deferrals, intraday and seasonal variation management, and others
To promote development of wind-solar hybrid projects
To promote development of floating solar including hybridization of floating solar with existing hydro stations
To promote generation of energy through biomass, and waste-to-energy
To promote new initiatives and emerging energy technologies in the State.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027 aims to facilitate the development of 10 GW of additional renewable energy (RE) capacity in Karnataka, including up to 1 GW of rooftop solar PV projects. The policy covers 11 focus markets: Green Energy Corridor, RE Parks, Solar, Wind, Solar-Wind Hybrid, Energy Storage, Biomass, Co-generation, Waste to Energy, Mini and Small-Hydro, and New Initiatives/R&D. Key measures include treating all RE projects as manufacturing industries to make them eligible for State Industrial Policy incentives (excluding investment promotion subsidies), deemed conversion of agricultural land upon project approval, up to 50% State equity participation in PPP-mode RE Parks, time-bound grid connectivity clearances (45-60 days), long-term lease of water bodies for floating solar, and tariff rebates for solar-powered EV charging stations.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Treatment of RE projects as manufacturing industry for State Industrial Policy concessions, deemed land conversion, and up to 50% State equity in PPP RE Parks.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Energy Department, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Rural economic development and agriculture feeder solarization

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.2. Applicability of Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
a. This Policy will be applicable to projects and programs relating to the focus markets as covered under provision 4 of this Policy.
b. All Solar, Wind, Solar-Wind Hybrid, Energy Storage, Mini and Small-Hydro, Biomass, Co-generation, Waste to Energy projects and new initiatives/pilot projects established in the State of Karnataka during the Policy period shall be eligible for benefits under this Policy.
c. Any individual or company or body corporate or association or society or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not shall be eligible for setting up RE projects, either for the purpose of captive use and/or for selling of electricity to the Distribution Licensee or Third Party including under the Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) mechanism subject to provisions of this Policy and in accordance with the Electricity Act 2003, as amended from time to time.
d. This Policy supersedes all the earlier Solar and RE policies issued. This Policy will be applicable to all the RE projects sanctioned prior to the commencement of the Policy and those RE projects in the process of development i.e. if a project developer with Government Order (GO) issued prior to the commencement of this Policy applies for timeline extension or transfer, the applicable timelines, time extension fees and transfer fees shall be as per the provisions 7.1 and 7.2 of this Policy.
6.1.a.2. The net worth of the company shall be at least 30% of the total project cost.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Investment promotion subsidies under the State Industrial Policy are excluded for RE projects. Private RE parks set up for open access route shall not be eligible to avail CFA under MNRE park schemes. Net-metering facility shall not be applicable for solar projects installed within the premises under clause 5.2.3.b.2 which are connected to the grid interface of ESCOMs or KPTCL.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: The net worth of the company shall be at least 30% of the total project cost (determined by KERC or DPR). Minimum capacity for each RE Park is 25 MW. Minimum capacity for MW scale grid connected solar project is 1 MWac (no minimum limit for captive/group captive). For repowering of wind projects, existing wind turbines must have completed at least 10 years in operation. For biomass projects, raw materials in a 40KM radius are considered to avoid overlapping.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Projects must be established in the State of Karnataka. Maximum land area utilization: 3.5 acres per MWac for Solar PV, 4 acres per WTG for Wind, and 100 Sq. ft per 1 kWp for Solar Rooftop.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Solar PV modules must comply with ALMM as per MNRE; Wind Turbine Generator models must comply with RLMM as per MNRE. Off-grid and rooftop solar projects require safety approval from the Department of Electrical Inspectorate.

Key measures include treating all RE projects as manufacturing industries to make them eligible for State Industrial Policy incentives (excluding investment promotion subsidies), deemed conversion of agricultural land upon project approval, up to 50% State equity participation in PPP-mode RE Parks, time-bound grid connectivity clearances (45-60 days), long-term lease of water bodies for floating solar, and tariff rebates for solar-powered EV charging stations.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Treatment of RE projects as manufacturing industry for State Industrial Policy concessions, deemed land conversion, and up to 50% State equity in PPP RE Parks.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Energy Department, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Rural economic development and agriculture feeder solarization

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1.2. Applicability of Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
a. This Policy will be applicable to projects and programs relating to the focus markets as covered under provision 4 of this Policy.
b. All Solar, Wind, Solar-Wind Hybrid, Energy Storage, Mini and Small-Hydro, Biomass, Co-generation, Waste to Energy projects and new initiatives/pilot projects established in the State of Karnataka during the Policy period shall be eligible for benefits under this Policy.
c. Any individual or company or body corporate or association or society or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not shall be eligible for setting up RE projects, either for the purpose of captive use and/or for selling of electricity to the Distribution Licensee or Third Party including under the Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) mechanism subject to provisions of this Policy and in accordance with the Electricity Act 2003, as amended from time to time.
d. This Policy supersedes all the earlier Solar and RE policies issued. This Policy will be applicable to all the RE projects sanctioned prior to the commencement of the Policy and those RE projects in the process of development i.e. if a project developer with Government Order (GO) issued prior to the commencement of this Policy applies for timeline extension or transfer, the applicable timelines, time extension fees and transfer fees shall be as per the provisions 7.1 and 7.2 of this Policy.
6.1.a.2. The net worth of the company shall be at least 30% of the total project cost.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Investment promotion subsidies under the State Industrial Policy are excluded for RE projects. Private RE parks set up for open access route shall not be eligible to avail CFA under MNRE park schemes. Net-metering facility shall not be applicable for solar projects installed within the premises under clause 5.2.3.b.2 which are connected to the grid interface of ESCOMs or KPTCL.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: The net worth of the company shall be at least 30% of the total project cost (determined by KERC or DPR). Minimum capacity for each RE Park is 25 MW. Minimum capacity for MW scale grid connected solar project is 1 MWac (no minimum limit for captive/group captive). For repowering of wind projects, existing wind turbines must have completed at least 10 years in operation. For biomass projects, raw materials in a 40KM radius are considered to avoid overlapping.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Projects must be established in the State of Karnataka. Maximum land area utilization: 3.5 acres per MWac for Solar PV, 4 acres per WTG for Wind, and 100 Sq. ft per 1 kWp for Solar Rooftop.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Solar PV modules must comply with ALMM as per MNRE; Wind Turbine Generator models must comply with RLMM as per MNRE. Off-grid and rooftop solar projects require safety approval from the Department of Electrical Inspectorate.

incentive_details.description: In case a renewable energy project is not allocated by the Government of Karnataka, or if the project developer requests the withdrawal of their application before it is submitted to the Government of Karnataka, 70% of the processing fee paid (which ranges from Γé╣1,000 per project for small rooftop to Γé╣2,00,000 per MW for utility projects) is refunded to the developer by KREDL.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 70% refund of project processing fees in case of non-allocation by the Government or application withdrawal prior to GoK submission.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit withdrawal request to KREDL prior to GoK submission, or claim refund upon non-allocation.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: 70 % (Seventy per cent) of processing fee
quantified_benefits.conditions: In case of non-allocation of projects by the GoK OR developer requests withdrawal of application before submission to the GoK
quantified_benefits.description: Refund of 70% of the processing fee in case of non-allocation of project or withdrawal of application before submission to GoK.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The application fee shall be non-refundable. In case of non-allocation of projects by the GoK OR in case of developer requests for withdrawal of application before submission to the GoK, 70 % (Seventy per cent) of processing fee shall be refunded to developers by KREDL.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All RE project applicants

incentive_details.application_deadline: Before submission of application to the Government of Karnataka (for withdrawal)
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Limited (KREDL)

policy_name: Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
incentive_name: Tariff Rebate for Solar-Powered EV Charging and Battery Swapping Stations

policy_goals: To continue Karnataka State's position as a preferred investment destination in the RE sector and create an ecosystem for sustainable and green energy development in the State.
To facilitate development of 10 (Ten) GW of additional RE projects with or without energy storage systems in the State, including up to 1(One) GW of Rooftop solar PV projects
To attract investment in the RE sector and development of State economy
To tap RE potential in the State and use of available resources for development of RE projects for the purpose of meeting the RE demand within the State and exporting power outside Karnataka
To achieve the RPO target(s) as specified by the KERC from time to time
To develop Renewable Energy Parks including hybrid parks in the State
To encourage private sector participation in transmission network/Green Energy Corridor projects

To develop ecosystem for distributed generation through Solarization of agriculture feeders and pumps which can help deferment of transmission and distribution capacity addition and reduction in losses
To promote adaptation of electric vehicles and de-carbonize transportation in the State by encouraging use of cleaner renewable energy in the transportation sector
To promote energy storage projects in the State

To create energy storage market in the State to integrate more RE into the grid and offer grid support services such as peak reduction, curtailment management, contribution to reliability needs, transmission deferrals, intraday and seasonal variation management, and others
To promote development of wind-solar hybrid projects
To promote development of floating solar including hybridization of floating solar with existing hydro stations
To promote generation of energy through biomass, and waste-to-energy
To promote new initiatives and emerging energy technologies in the State.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Subject to evaluation and consent of the KERC
quantified_benefits.description: Rebate on the applicable tariff for EV charging and battery swapping stations supplied by ground mount and rooftop solar PV plants within the same premises.

policy_name: Academic, Research, Skill Development, and Geospatial DPI/EO Grants Scheme
incentive_name: Financial Support for Creation of Digital Public Good (DPI/DPG) in Downstream Space

policy_goals: To sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share i.e. USD 22 billion market by 2033.
To propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share.

Leveraging NIPUNA and other initiatives of Government of Karnataka, during the policy period, 50,000 professionals and students will be trained/up-skilled upto industry standards, including at least 15,000 women professionals and students.
Attract and generate a cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period.
Dedicated space manufacturing park(s) with required common infrastructure for the sector will be set-up and testing needs of the sector are met through test centers and facilities in the state.
During the policy period, at least 500 space sector Start-Ups and MSME will be supported to grow and innovate.

During the policy period, 50+ satellites with substantial indigenization shall be designed, manufactured, assembled, integrated, tested, launched and operated by Karnataka based NewSpace enterprises for commercial/defence-space/research purposes.
Improve awareness about possibilities through space technologies among non-space entities i.e. private sector enterprises of Karnataka in a focused manner.
Improve the adoption of space technologies for governance operations and service delivery.
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme supports schools, higher education institutions (ITIs, Polytechnics, Diploma Institutes, Universities), research institutions, NIPUNA training partners, and non-profits/philanthropies in Karnataka to build a skilled talent pipeline, foster academic research, and drive downstream geospatial adoption. It provides financial support for school industrial visits, district-level space science awareness sessions, setting up a state-of-the-art Space Gallery, establishing/revamping Space Technology Labs in higher education institutions, procuring academic software licenses, student research project grants, an additional 20% training incentive for NIPUNA partners, CAPEX/OPEX support for Geospatial Digital Public Infrastructure/Goods (DPI/DPG), and special research/application grants for AI-based Foundational Earth Observation (EO) models.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to Γé╣1 Crore for higher education Space Technology Labs, Γé╣75 lakhs for a Space Gallery, Γé╣2 lakhs for software licenses and student projects, and special grants for Geospatial DPI and AI Earth Observation models.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1.2 Space Manufacturing Park Developer, Training Institutions, Academic Institutions (including schools), and Research Institutions can directly apply for incentives on the Online Portal, without the need for Space Karnataka Registration.
1.3 Academic Institution means any university, college, or educational institution recognized by the Government of Karnataka or Government of India, engaged in teaching and training in space technology or allied domains.
1.28 Research Institution means any organization, laboratory, or center recognized by the Government of Karnataka or Government of India, or established under a statutory framework, primarily engaged in scientific research, technology development, or innovation in space technology or allied domains.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Land and building costs for Space Technology Labs; personal/consumer software licenses; salary, travel, administrative overheads, and generic IT/cloud tools for DPI/DPG and EO model grants.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Higher education and research institutions must hold valid affiliation/recognition/accreditation from competent statutory authorities (DTE, AICTE, UGC, NCTE, ICAR, etc.) and have audited financial statements for the preceding 2 financial years.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Institutions and schools must be located in Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Recognized by Government of Karnataka or Government of India; Space Karnataka Registration is NOT required.
special_category_benefits: Socially and economically backward professionals (subsidised university course fees)
Women professionals and students (target of 15,000 trained under NIPUNA)

incentive_details.description: CAPEX and OPEX financial assistance to build, maintain, and operationalize open, standardized, interoperable geospatial datasets, models, APIs, and tools aligned with Digital Public Infrastructure / Digital Public Goods (DPI/DPG) principles.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: CAPEX and OPEX grant support (up to limit approved by KITS) for developing open Geospatial Digital Public Infrastructure and Goods.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit proposal in response to Expression of Interest (EoI) floated by KITS.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: subject to a maximum limit approved by the KITS
quantified_benefits.value_raw: CAPEX and OPEX assistance (subject to maximum limit approved by KITS)
quantified_benefits.conditions: All IP, datasets, models, and APIs developed must reside with the Karnataka-registered entity and be made publicly accessible/reusable as DPI/DPG.
quantified_benefits.description: CAPEX and OPEX assistance for development and adoption of geospatial DPI/DPG.
quantified_benefits.source_text: ii. This support shall consist of CAPEX and OPEX assistance for development and adoption of a geospatial DPI/DPG, subject to a maximum limit approved by the KITS per Academic Institution, Research Institution, or Start-ups, to build, maintain, and operationalize geospatial datasets, models, and tools aligned with the DPI/DPG principles.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Academic Institutions, Research Institutions, and Start-ups based in Karnataka

incentive_details.application_deadline: As per Expression of Interest (EoI) floated by KITS.
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Working Committee
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Assets or datasets created before the Policy period are not eligible.

Improve awareness about possibilities through space technologies among non-space entities i.e. private sector enterprises of Karnataka in a focused manner.
Improve the adoption of space technologies for governance operations and service delivery.

policy_goals: To sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share i.e. USD 22 billion market by 2033.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030 provides comprehensive fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises operating in the upstream and downstream space technology value chain in Karnataka. eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
3.1.1 Unless specifically allowed in this Policy, any entity/enterprise that avails benefits under any other Government of Karnataka policy during the policy period or while this policy remains in force will not be eligible for benefits under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030. However, entities/enterprises that availed benefits under other policies before the start of this Policy Period and are undertaking Expansion of Existing Unit or establishing New Unit (at a different location) during the Policy Period, will remain eligible for benefits under this Policy.
3.1.4 Any enterprise (Start-ups/MSMEs/Large Enterprises) who wishes to avail benefits through this policy shall be registered under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments act, 1961 and/or have obtained Factory Registration under the Factories Act, 1948 of a factory situated in Karnataka at the time of applying for benefits.
3.1.5 Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) shall operationalize an online registration mechanism to register all space sector enterprises and entities in Karnataka. The registration may be called ΓÇ£Space Karnataka RegistrationΓÇ¥.
3.3.6 Only the enterprises (excluding Academic Institution, Research Institution, Industrial Park Developer) which have successfully obtained Space Karnataka Registration shall be eligible to avail benefits through this Policy.
3.3.7 The entities/enterprises eligible to avail benefits through this Policy as a Space enterprise (excluding Academic Institution, Research Institution, Industrial Park Developer) shall qualify for at least one of the following:
3.3.7.1 Entities eligible to qualify as a Non-Government Entity (NGE) as defined in the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and its Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and any further notifications to the same, who are in the business of any of the activities requiring authorisation from IN-SPACe.
3.3.7.2 Indian entities who are registered vendor to ISRO and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the Focus Areas of this policy over the last one year.
3.3.7.3 Indian entities who are registered vendor to space Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) to global space agencies and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last one year. Resellers, distributors, and trading-only entities shall not be eligible under this provision; only Indian entities with direct manufacturing or service delivery capabilities and documentary evidence of direct supply to space OEMs/System Integrators during any period within the past 3 years of the Notification of the Policy.
3.3.7.4 Non-Indian entities who are globally renowned Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) /component manufacturers in space sector and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years. However, their participation in space activities in India will be subject to authorization of IN-SPACe as mentioned in the Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and any further notifications to the same.
3.3.7.5 Any other entity who is determined to be a beneficiary by the Technical Committee mentioned in Section 4.1.d. of the Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Entities/enterprises availing benefits under any other Government of Karnataka policy during the policy period (unless they availed benefits before the start of this Policy Period and are undertaking Expansion of Existing Unit or establishing New Unit at a different location). policy_goals: To sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share i.e. USD 22 billion market by 2033.
To propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share.

Leveraging NIPUNA and other initiatives of Government of Karnataka, during the policy period, 50,000 professionals and students will be trained/up-skilled upto industry standards, including at least 15,000 women professionals and students.
Attract and generate a cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period.
Dedicated space manufacturing park(s) with required common infrastructure for the sector will be set-up and testing needs of the sector are met through test centers and facilities in the state.
During the policy period, at least 500 space sector Start-Ups and MSME will be supported to grow and innovate.

During the policy period, 50+ satellites with substantial indigenization shall be designed, manufactured, assembled, integrated, tested, launched and operated by Karnataka based NewSpace enterprises for commercial/defence-space/research purposes.

Improve the adoption of space technologies for governance operations and service delivery.
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030 provides comprehensive fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises operating in the upstream and downstream space technology value chain in Karnataka. For investment proposals up to INR 100 Crore, it offers a 20% capital investment subsidy on plant and machinery (up to INR 5 Crore), a 25% subsidy on land outside Bengaluru Urban (up to 5 acres and INR 3 Crore), rental reimbursement, 50% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges, 100% land conversion fee exemption, 50% ETP subsidy (up to INR 250 lakhs), and 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years. Investments above INR 100 Crore receive customized incentive packages. Additionally, Startups and MSMEs receive dedicated support for employee skill training, technology acquisition, quality certification, testing costs, IP registration, global market access, R&D, PF/ESI reimbursement, internships, and space biotechnology research grants.

policy_name: Incentives for Space Sector Enterprises (Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises)

policy_goals: To sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share i.e. USD 22 billion market by 2033.
To propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share.

Leveraging NIPUNA and other initiatives of Government of Karnataka, during the policy period, 50,000 professionals and students will be trained/up-skilled upto industry standards, including at least 15,000 women professionals and students.
Attract and generate a cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period.
Dedicated space manufacturing park(s) with required common infrastructure for the sector will be set-up and testing needs of the sector are met through test centers and facilities in the state.
During the policy period, at least 500 space sector Start-Ups and MSME will be supported to grow and innovate.

During the policy period, 50+ satellites with substantial indigenization shall be designed, manufactured, assembled, integrated, tested, launched and operated by Karnataka based NewSpace enterprises for commercial/defence-space/research purposes.
Improve awareness about possibilities through space technologies among non-space entities i.e. private sector enterprises of Karnataka in a focused manner.
Improve the adoption of space technologies for governance operations and service delivery.
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030 provides comprehensive fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises operating in the upstream and downstream space technology value chain in Karnataka. For investment proposals up to INR 100 Crore, it offers a 20% capital investment subsidy on plant and machinery (up to INR 5 Crore), a 25% subsidy on land outside Bengaluru Urban (up to 5 acres and INR 3 Crore), rental reimbursement, 50% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges, 100% land conversion fee exemption, 50% ETP subsidy (up to INR 250 lakhs), and 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years. Investments above INR 100 Crore receive customized incentive packages. Additionally, Startups and MSMEs receive dedicated support for employee skill training, technology acquisition, quality certification, testing costs, IP registration, global market access, R&D, PF/ESI reimbursement, internships, and space biotechnology research grants.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
3.1.1 Unless specifically allowed in this Policy, any entity/enterprise that avails benefits under any other Government of Karnataka policy during the policy period or while this policy remains in force will not be eligible for benefits under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030. However, entities/enterprises that availed benefits under other policies before the start of this Policy Period and are undertaking Expansion of Existing Unit or establishing New Unit (at a different location) during the Policy Period, will remain eligible for benefits under this Policy.
3.1.4 Any enterprise (Start-ups/MSMEs/Large Enterprises) who wishes to avail benefits through this policy shall be registered under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments act, 1961 and/or have obtained Factory Registration under the Factories Act, 1948 of a factory situated in Karnataka at the time of applying for benefits.
3.1.5 Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) shall operationalize an online registration mechanism to register all space sector enterprises and entities in Karnataka. The registration may be called ΓÇ£Space Karnataka RegistrationΓÇ¥.
3.3.6 Only the enterprises (excluding Academic Institution, Research Institution, Industrial Park Developer) which have successfully obtained Space Karnataka Registration shall be eligible to avail benefits through this Policy.
3.3.7 The entities/enterprises eligible to avail benefits through this Policy as a Space enterprise (excluding Academic Institution, Research Institution, Industrial Park Developer) shall qualify for at least one of the following:
3.3.7.1 Entities eligible to qualify as a Non-Government Entity (NGE) as defined in the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and its Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and any further notifications to the same, who are in the business of any of the activities requiring authorisation from IN-SPACe.
3.3.7.2 Indian entities who are registered vendor to ISRO and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the Focus Areas of this policy over the last one year.
3.3.7.3 Indian entities who are registered vendor to space Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) to global space agencies and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last one year. Resellers, distributors, and trading-only entities shall not be eligible under this provision; only Indian entities with direct manufacturing or service delivery capabilities and documentary evidence of direct supply to space OEMs/System Integrators during any period within the past 3 years of the Notification of the Policy.
3.3.7.4 Non-Indian entities who are globally renowned Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) /component manufacturers in space sector and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years. However, their participation in space activities in India will be subject to authorization of IN-SPACe as mentioned in the Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and any further notifications to the same.
3.3.7.5 Any other entity who is determined to be a beneficiary by the Technical Committee mentioned in Section 4.1.d. of the Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Entities/enterprises availing benefits under any other Government of Karnataka policy during the policy period (unless they availed benefits before the start of this Policy Period and are undertaking Expansion of Existing Unit or establishing New Unit at a different location). Resellers, distributors, and trading-only entities shall not be eligible under the vendor to space OEMs/SI provision.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must qualify as a Non-Government Entity (NGE) requiring IN-SPACe authorisation, OR be a registered vendor to ISRO/global space OEMs/SIs with documentary evidence of supply in the focus areas, OR be a globally renowned non-Indian space OEM/SI/component manufacturer with IN-SPACe authorization. For investment incentives, investments must be approved by DLSWCC/SLSWCC/SHLCC and commercial production/operations must have commenced. Total quantum of incentives for each investment proposal shall not exceed 100% of the total value of fixed assets.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Must have a factory or establishment situated in Karnataka (Land capital subsidy is applicable anywhere in the state except Bengaluru Urban District).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961 and/or Factory Registration under the Factories Act, 1948 in Karnataka; mandatory Space Karnataka Registration with KITS (one-time lifetime fee of INR 10,000 + GST); Startups must be registered with Karnataka Startup Cell / DPIIT; MSMEs must have valid Udyam Registration in Karnataka.

policy_name: Incentives for Space Sector Enterprises (Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises)

policy_goals: To sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share i.e. USD 22 billion market by 2033.
To propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share.

Leveraging NIPUNA and other initiatives of Government of Karnataka, during the policy period, 50,000 professionals and students will be trained/up-skilled upto industry standards, including at least 15,000 women professionals and students.
Attract and generate a cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period.
Dedicated space manufacturing park(s) with required common infrastructure for the sector will be set-up and testing needs of the sector are met through test centers and facilities in the state.
During the policy period, at least 500 space sector Start-Ups and MSME will be supported to grow and innovate.

During the policy period, 50+ satellites with substantial indigenization shall be designed, manufactured, assembled, integrated, tested, launched and operated by Karnataka based NewSpace enterprises for commercial/defence-space/research purposes.
Improve awareness about possibilities through space technologies among non-space entities i.e. private sector enterprises of Karnataka in a focused manner.
Improve the adoption of space technologies for governance operations and service delivery.
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme under the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-2030 provides comprehensive fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to Startups, MSMEs, and Large Enterprises operating in the upstream and downstream space technology value chain in Karnataka. Investments above INR 100 Crore receive customized incentive packages. Additionally, Startups and MSMEs receive dedicated support for employee skill training, technology acquisition, quality certification, testing costs, IP registration, global market access, R&D, PF/ESI reimbursement, internships, and space biotechnology research grants.

policy_goals: To make Karnataka one among the top States of India in terms of domestic and international tourist visits (rank among top 3 States for domestic tourist visits and top 5 States for international tourist visits by 2029)
Support Karnataka's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032 through strong economic growth driven by tourism
To ensure every tourist to Karnataka experiences happiness, satisfaction, and cultural immersion
To enable tourism for all strata of society and provide high-quality offerings that cater to all tourist preferences
To harness tourism's potential for its effects on employment generation, economic development, and entrepreneurial opportunities
To strategically focus on emerging tourism segments as well as those where Karnataka is well-positioned to become the preferred choice
To instil confidence in tourists to travel across Karnataka by providing safety, convenience, and comfort throughout their journeys
To promote Karnataka domestically and internationally through diverse marketing channels, collaborations, and targeted strategies
To ensure quality tourism infrastructure and essential amenities for tourists at and enroute to major tourism destinations across Karnataka
To create exceptional experiences for diverse visitor profiles that encourage repeat visits and longer stays
To increase the visibility and accessibility of lesser-known destinations to promote balanced regional development
Identify, develop, and promote lesser-known tourism assets, expanding Karnataka's tourism potential
To create greater employment through tourism and its allied activities
To initiate and support skill development programs to meet the needs of Karnataka's tourism sector
To enhance the professionalism and visibility of tour guides and Tourism Service Providers and increase their presence across tourist destinations
To encourage sustainable development in tourism towards achievement of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals for Karnataka
To foster inclusive tourism by ensuring that tourism development benefits all communities especially women and marginalized groups
To make tourism inclusive and accessible for all while promoting respect for diverse backgrounds
To incorporate the promotion of local and traditional crafts, cuisines, and culture as integral components of the tourism experience
To foster tourism-driven socio-economic development in rural communities and showcasing of local traditions
To promote green initiatives in tourism, aligning tourism development with sustainability goals
To sustainably develop Coastal Karnataka into a multi-product tourism destination
To bring together stakeholders for the promotion and growth of responsible tourism in Karnataka
To encourage active involvement of locals in shaping tourism experiences and in the planning, development, and management of tourism initiatives, ensuring that benefits are shared equitably
To promote sustainable and climate resilient tourism practices that protect Karnataka's natural resources and its people
To position Karnataka as a preferred destination for tourism investments
To encourage Public-Private Partnerships to foster innovation and investment in tourism
To create an enabling framework for private sector investments and establish mechanisms to support industry-driven initiatives in tourism
To encourage startups, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, and innovative tourism offerings and foster linkages for their growth
To leverage technology and digital solutions for visitor engagement, marketing, and operational efficiency
To empower Karnataka Tourism with suitable institutional frameworks and administrative structures for the development and promotion of tourism
To leverage technology to facilitate data-driven outcome-oriented planning and policymaking
To facilitate effective inter-departmental coordination for the successful implementation of this Policy
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to position Karnataka among the top 3 Indian states for domestic tourist visits and top 5 for international tourist visits by 2029, contributing to the state's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032. The policy covers 25 tourism themes including Adventure, Agri, Caravan, Coastal, Cultural, Eco, Heritage, MICE, Spiritual, and Wellness Tourism. It provides industry status to eligible tourism projects and offers a comprehensive package of fiscal and non-fiscal benefits. These include Capital Investment Subsidies (15% to 25% of Eligible Project Cost up to Γé╣10 Crore, with an additional 5% for women, SC/ST, differently-abled entrepreneurs, and hotel projects in Kalyana and Kittur Karnataka regions), Interest Subsidies (5% p.a. up to Γé╣25 Lakh over 5 years), 50% Stamp Duty exemption, 100% Registration Charges exemption, 100% Land Conversion Fee reimbursement, Motor Vehicle Tax exemptions/reimbursements for tourist transport and caravans, Marketing Development Assistance (up to Γé╣2 Lakh per activity), and 50% capital grants up to Γé╣1 Lakh for sustainability initiatives. Special non-fiscal concessions such as domestic utility tariffs and property tax rates are extended to registered Homestays and Agri Tourism projects.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 15% to 25% capital investment subsidy up to Γé╣10 Crore (plus 5% additional for special categories/regions), 5% interest subsidy up to Γé╣25 Lakh, 50% stamp duty exemption, and 100% registration and land conversion fee waivers for tourism projects in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Tourism Project shall mean a legal entity under the relevant law that is engaged or to be engaged in providing any service related to tourism.
2. Eligible Tourism Project refers to the list of Tourism Projects identified by the Department of Tourism that shall be prioritized for development in Karnataka during the Policy Period. The Eligible Tourism Projects identified below shall be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy as outlined Section 14 Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Agri Tourism Project, 3. Apartment Hotel / Serviced Apartment, 4. Aquarium / Oceanarium, 5. Beach Shack, 6. Bed & Breakfast, 7. Amusement Park, 8. Caravan Park, 9. Caravan Tourism Project, 10. Convention Centre, 11. Cruise Tourism Project, 12. Cultural Centre, 13. Cultural Village / Tourist Village, 14. Eco Tourism Project, 15. Farm Stay, 16. Film City, 17. Golf Course, 18. Guest House, 19. Heritage Hotel, 20. Heritage Tourism Project, 21. Heritage Walk / Guided Tour, 22. Homestay, 23. Hotel ΓÇô Budget, 24. Hotel ΓÇô Premium, 25. Houseboat, 26. MICE Venue, 27. Museum and Galleries, 28. Pravasi Snehi Sankeerna (Tourist Facilitation Centre), 29. Ropeway, 30. Sound & Light Show, 31. Tented Accommodation, 32. Theme Park, 33. Timeshare Resort, 34. Tourist Guide, 35. Tourism or Hospitality Training Institute, 36. Tourism Startup, 37. Tour Operator, 38. Tourist Transport Operator, 39. Tourist Interpretation Centre, 40. Travel Agent, 41. Yatri Niwas, 42. Wellness Centre, 43. Wayside Amenities, 44. Yuva Tourism Club.
To qualify for benefits under this Policy, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
3. New Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised during the operative tenure of this Policy.
4. Existing Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised before the operative tenure of this Policy.
5. Expansion Tourism Project shall mean an existing Eligible Tourism Project that is taking up an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC for the Project. Only one expansion project of an existing Tourism Project will be eligible for assistance during the operative period of this Policy.
6. Mega Tourism Project shall mean Tourism Project with an EPC of above INR 100 Crore.
7. Tourism Service Provider shall mean any company, association, firm, or any other legal entity under the relevant law who is engaged in providing any service related to tourism. Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy.
14.1.3 Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible to avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions offered under this Section.
15.2.2 Supporting Provisions for availing Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions:
1. To avail the incentives, subsidies, and concessions for Eligible Tourism Projects identified in this Policy, the applicant must submit necessary documents and obtain the required approvals from the committee concerned as per the timelines specified in the Operational Guidelines of the Policy.
3. Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers can avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions under multiple policies of different departments of Government of Karnataka and / or Government of India. However, if the same component is claimed under different policies, the quantum is limited to the maximum of the component in any one of the Policy.
4. The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
5. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval of the applicable committee prior to before commencement of the construction work pertaining to establishment of a New Tourism Project or expansion of an Expansion Tourism Project.
6. For Tourism Projects receiving subsidies, it shall be mandatory to operate the Tourism Project for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy. If the Tourism Project fails to abide by this condition, the applicant shall have to return the subsidy amount with a 10% simple interest per annum to the Department of Tourism.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district or within the Municipal Corporation limits of Bengaluru.
2. No exemption on stamp duty with respect to the development of Tourism Projects within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
3. No reimbursement on land conversion fee for conversion of land located within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA).
4. EPC does not include: Working Capital; Pre-operative expenses and preliminary expenses; Second-hand plant and machinery purchased or shifted from within or outside India; Interest capitalised; Consumable stores; Inventories for maintenance or repairs; Investment on land required for setting up the Tourism Project, inclusive of the cost of the land; Vehicles (except those permissible for Adventure, Caravan, Cruise, and Houseboat projects); Furniture, fixtures, cutlery, crockery, utensils; Any construction which in the nature of real estate transactions is meant for sale / lease / rent (shops, flats, offices, etc.); and Intangible assets including intellectual Property rights and goodwill.
5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements:
1. Expansion Tourism Projects must take up an expansion of more than 50% of existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC.
2. Total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
3. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval prior to commencement of construction work and must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Projects must be located in Karnataka. Priority is given to projects located at Focus Tourism Destinations (FTDs) or within important Tourism Circuits. Bengaluru Urban / BBMP / BMRDA limits are excluded for Capital Investment Subsidy, Stamp Duty Exemption, and Land Conversion Fee Reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory online registration of Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers with the Department of Tourism on the Karnataka Tourism Website under the Karnataka Tourism Trade (Facilitation and Regulation) Act, 2015 (KTTF Act).
special_category_benefits: Hotel Projects (Budget and Premium) in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka regions

policy_goals: To make Karnataka one among the top States of India in terms of domestic and international tourist visits (rank among top 3 States for domestic tourist visits and top 5 States for international tourist visits by 2029)
Support Karnataka's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032 through strong economic growth driven by tourism
To ensure every tourist to Karnataka experiences happiness, satisfaction, and cultural immersion
To enable tourism for all strata of society and provide high-quality offerings that cater to all tourist preferences
To harness tourism's potential for its effects on employment generation, economic development, and entrepreneurial opportunities
To strategically focus on emerging tourism segments as well as those where Karnataka is well-positioned to become the preferred choice
To instil confidence in tourists to travel across Karnataka by providing safety, convenience, and comfort throughout their journeys
To promote Karnataka domestically and internationally through diverse marketing channels, collaborations, and targeted strategies
To ensure quality tourism infrastructure and essential amenities for tourists at and enroute to major tourism destinations across Karnataka
To create exceptional experiences for diverse visitor profiles that encourage repeat visits and longer stays
To increase the visibility and accessibility of lesser-known destinations to promote balanced regional development
Identify, develop, and promote lesser-known tourism assets, expanding Karnataka's tourism potential
To create greater employment through tourism and its allied activities
To initiate and support skill development programs to meet the needs of Karnataka's tourism sector
To enhance the professionalism and visibility of tour guides and Tourism Service Providers and increase their presence across tourist destinations
To encourage sustainable development in tourism towards achievement of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals for Karnataka
To foster inclusive tourism by ensuring that tourism development benefits all communities especially women and marginalized groups
To make tourism inclusive and accessible for all while promoting respect for diverse backgrounds
To incorporate the promotion of local and traditional crafts, cuisines, and culture as integral components of the tourism experience
To foster tourism-driven socio-economic development in rural communities and showcasing of local traditions
To promote green initiatives in tourism, aligning tourism development with sustainability goals
To sustainably develop Coastal Karnataka into a multi-product tourism destination
To bring together stakeholders for the promotion and growth of responsible tourism in Karnataka
To encourage active involvement of locals in shaping tourism experiences and in the planning, development, and management of tourism initiatives, ensuring that benefits are shared equitably
To promote sustainable and climate resilient tourism practices that protect Karnataka's natural resources and its people
To position Karnataka as a preferred destination for tourism investments
To encourage Public-Private Partnerships to foster innovation and investment in tourism
To create an enabling framework for private sector investments and establish mechanisms to support industry-driven initiatives in tourism
To encourage startups, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, and innovative tourism offerings and foster linkages for their growth
To leverage technology and digital solutions for visitor engagement, marketing, and operational efficiency
To empower Karnataka Tourism with suitable institutional frameworks and administrative structures for the development and promotion of tourism
To leverage technology to facilitate data-driven outcome-oriented planning and policymaking
To facilitate effective inter-departmental coordination for the successful implementation of this Policy
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to position Karnataka among the top 3 Indian states for domestic tourist visits and top 5 for international tourist visits by 2029, contributing to the state's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032. The policy covers 25 tourism themes including Adventure, Agri, Caravan, Coastal, Cultural, Eco, Heritage, MICE, Spiritual, and Wellness Tourism. It provides industry status to eligible tourism projects and offers a comprehensive package of fiscal and non-fiscal benefits. These include Capital Investment Subsidies (15% to 25% of Eligible Project Cost up to Γé╣10 Crore, with an additional 5% for women, SC/ST, differently-abled entrepreneurs, and hotel projects in Kalyana and Kittur Karnataka regions), Interest Subsidies (5% p.a. up to Γé╣25 Lakh over 5 years), 50% Stamp Duty exemption, 100% Registration Charges exemption, 100% Land Conversion Fee reimbursement, Motor Vehicle Tax exemptions/reimbursements for tourist transport and caravans, Marketing Development Assistance (up to Γé╣2 Lakh per activity), and 50% capital grants up to Γé╣1 Lakh for sustainability initiatives. Special non-fiscal concessions such as domestic utility tariffs and property tax rates are extended to registered Homestays and Agri Tourism projects.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 15% to 25% capital investment subsidy up to Γé╣10 Crore (plus 5% additional for special categories/regions), 5% interest subsidy up to Γé╣25 Lakh, 50% stamp duty exemption, and 100% registration and land conversion fee waivers for tourism projects in Karnataka.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Tourism Project shall mean a legal entity under the relevant law that is engaged or to be engaged in providing any service related to tourism.
2. Eligible Tourism Project refers to the list of Tourism Projects identified by the Department of Tourism that shall be prioritized for development in Karnataka during the Policy Period. The Eligible Tourism Projects identified below shall be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy as outlined Section 14 Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Agri Tourism Project, 3. Apartment Hotel / Serviced Apartment, 4. Aquarium / Oceanarium, 5. Beach Shack, 6. Bed & Breakfast, 7. Amusement Park, 8. Caravan Park, 9. Caravan Tourism Project, 10. Convention Centre, 11. Cruise Tourism Project, 12. Cultural Centre, 13. Cultural Village / Tourist Village, 14. Eco Tourism Project, 15. Farm Stay, 16. Film City, 17. Golf Course, 18. Guest House, 19. Heritage Hotel, 20. Heritage Tourism Project, 21. Heritage Walk / Guided Tour, 22. Homestay, 23. Hotel ΓÇô Budget, 24. Hotel ΓÇô Premium, 25. Houseboat, 26. MICE Venue, 27. Museum and Galleries, 28. Pravasi Snehi Sankeerna (Tourist Facilitation Centre), 29. Ropeway, 30. Sound & Light Show, 31. Tented Accommodation, 32. Theme Park, 33. Timeshare Resort, 34. Tourist Guide, 35. Tourism or Hospitality Training Institute, 36. Tourism Startup, 37. Tour Operator, 38. Tourist Transport Operator, 39. Tourist Interpretation Centre, 40. Travel Agent, 41. Yatri Niwas, 42. Wellness Centre, 43. Wayside Amenities, 44. Yuva Tourism Club.
To qualify for benefits under this Policy, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
3. New Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised during the operative tenure of this Policy.
4. Existing Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised before the operative tenure of this Policy.
5. Expansion Tourism Project shall mean an existing Eligible Tourism Project that is taking up an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC for the Project. Only one expansion project of an existing Tourism Project will be eligible for assistance during the operative period of this Policy.
6. Mega Tourism Project shall mean Tourism Project with an EPC of above INR 100 Crore.
7. Tourism Service Provider shall mean any company, association, firm, or any other legal entity under the relevant law who is engaged in providing any service related to tourism. Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy.
14.1.3 Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible to avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions offered under this Section.
15.2.2 Supporting Provisions for availing Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions:
1. To avail the incentives, subsidies, and concessions for Eligible Tourism Projects identified in this Policy, the applicant must submit necessary documents and obtain the required approvals from the committee concerned as per the timelines specified in the Operational Guidelines of the Policy.
3. Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers can avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions under multiple policies of different departments of Government of Karnataka and / or Government of India. However, if the same component is claimed under different policies, the quantum is limited to the maximum of the component in any one of the Policy.
4. The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
5. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval of the applicable committee prior to before commencement of the construction work pertaining to establishment of a New Tourism Project or expansion of an Expansion Tourism Project.
6. For Tourism Projects receiving subsidies, it shall be mandatory to operate the Tourism Project for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy. If the Tourism Project fails to abide by this condition, the applicant shall have to return the subsidy amount with a 10% simple interest per annum to the Department of Tourism.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district or within the Municipal Corporation limits of Bengaluru.
2. No exemption on stamp duty with respect to the development of Tourism Projects within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
3. No reimbursement on land conversion fee for conversion of land located within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA).
4. EPC does not include: Working Capital; Pre-operative expenses and preliminary expenses; Second-hand plant and machinery purchased or shifted from within or outside India; Interest capitalised; Consumable stores; Inventories for maintenance or repairs; Investment on land required for setting up the Tourism Project, inclusive of the cost of the land; Vehicles (except those permissible for Adventure, Caravan, Cruise, and Houseboat projects); Furniture, fixtures, cutlery, crockery, utensils; Any construction which in the nature of real estate transactions is meant for sale / lease / rent (shops, flats, offices, etc.); and Intangible assets including intellectual Property rights and goodwill.
5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements:
1. Expansion Tourism Projects must take up an expansion of more than 50% of existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC.
2. Total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
3. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval prior to commencement of construction work and must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Projects must be located in Karnataka. Priority is given to projects located at Focus Tourism Destinations (FTDs) or within important Tourism Circuits. Bengaluru Urban / BBMP / BMRDA limits are excluded for Capital Investment Subsidy, Stamp Duty Exemption, and Land Conversion Fee Reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory online registration of Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers with the Department of Tourism on the Karnataka Tourism Website under the Karnataka Tourism Trade (Facilitation and Regulation) Act, 2015 (KTTF Act).
special_category_benefits: Hotel Projects (Budget and Premium) in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka regions

quantified_benefits.description: Exemption from payment of Motor Vehicle Tax for up to 3 years from the date of registration for new Caravan vehicles
quantified_benefits.source_text: During the validity period of this Policy, new Caravan vehicles of transport category, i.e., commercial vehicles for tourism, shall be exempted from the payment of Motor Vehicle Tax for a period of up to 3 (three) years from the date of registration of the vehicle.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Tourism Service Providers registered with the Department of Tourism purchasing new commercial Caravan vehicles

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within the first 3 years from the date of issue of applicable notification or first 200 caravans, whichever is earlier.
incentive_details.application_authority: Department of Tourism and Transport Department, Government of Karnataka.
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Valid only for Tourism Service Providers registered with the Department of Tourism, and limited to the first 200 caravans registered with the Transport Department or the number of caravans registered in the first 3 years from notification date, whichever is earlier.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to position Karnataka among the top 3 Indian states for domestic tourist visits and top 5 for international tourist visits by 2029, contributing to the state's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032. The policy covers 25 tourism themes including Adventure, Agri, Caravan, Coastal, Cultural, Eco, Heritage, MICE, Spiritual, and Wellness Tourism. It provides industry status to eligible tourism projects and offers a comprehensive package of fiscal and non-fiscal benefits. These include Capital Investment Subsidies (15% to 25% of Eligible Project Cost up to Γé╣10 Crore, with an additional 5% for women, SC/ST, differently-abled entrepreneurs, and hotel projects in Kalyana and Kittur Karnataka regions), Interest Subsidies (5% p.a. up to Γé╣25 Lakh over 5 years), 50% Stamp Duty exemption, 100% Registration Charges exemption, 100% Land Conversion Fee reimbursement, Motor Vehicle Tax exemptions/reimbursements for tourist transport and caravans, Marketing Development Assistance (up to Γé╣2 Lakh per activity), and 50% capital grants up to Γé╣1 Lakh for sustainability initiatives. Special non-fiscal concessions such as domestic utility tariffs and property tax rates are extended to registered Homestays and Agri Tourism projects.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Tourism Project shall mean a legal entity under the relevant law that is engaged or to be engaged in providing any service related to tourism.
2. Eligible Tourism Project refers to the list of Tourism Projects identified by the Department of Tourism that shall be prioritized for development in Karnataka during the Policy Period. The Eligible Tourism Projects identified below shall be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy as outlined Section 14 Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Agri Tourism Project, 3. Apartment Hotel / Serviced Apartment, 4. Aquarium / Oceanarium, 5. Beach Shack, 6. Bed & Breakfast, 7. Amusement Park, 8. Caravan Park, 9. Caravan Tourism Project, 10. Convention Centre, 11. Cruise Tourism Project, 12. Cultural Centre, 13. Cultural Village / Tourist Village, 14. Eco Tourism Project, 15. Farm Stay, 16. Film City, 17. Golf Course, 18. Guest House, 19. Heritage Hotel, 20. Heritage Tourism Project, 21. Heritage Walk / Guided Tour, 22. Homestay, 23. Hotel ΓÇô Budget, 24. Hotel ΓÇô Premium, 25. Houseboat, 26. MICE Venue, 27. Museum and Galleries, 28. Pravasi Snehi Sankeerna (Tourist Facilitation Centre), 29. Ropeway, 30. Sound & Light Show, 31. Tented Accommodation, 32. Theme Park, 33. Timeshare Resort, 34. Tourist Guide, 35. Tourism or Hospitality Training Institute, 36. Tourism Startup, 37. Tour Operator, 38. Tourist Transport Operator, 39. Tourist Interpretation Centre, 40. Travel Agent, 41. Yatri Niwas, 42. Wellness Centre, 43. Wayside Amenities, 44. Yuva Tourism Club.
To qualify for benefits under this Policy, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
3. New Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised during the operative tenure of this Policy.
4. Existing Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised before the operative tenure of this Policy.
5. Expansion Tourism Project shall mean an existing Eligible Tourism Project that is taking up an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC for the Project. Only one expansion project of an existing Tourism Project will be eligible for assistance during the operative period of this Policy.
6. Mega Tourism Project shall mean Tourism Project with an EPC of above INR 100 Crore.
7. Tourism Service Provider shall mean any company, association, firm, or any other legal entity under the relevant law who is engaged in providing any service related to tourism. Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy.
14.1.3 Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible to avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions offered under this Section.
15.2.2 Supporting Provisions for availing Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions:
1. To avail the incentives, subsidies, and concessions for Eligible Tourism Projects identified in this Policy, the applicant must submit necessary documents and obtain the required approvals from the committee concerned as per the timelines specified in the Operational Guidelines of the Policy.
3. Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers can avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions under multiple policies of different departments of Government of Karnataka and / or Government of India. However, if the same component is claimed under different policies, the quantum is limited to the maximum of the component in any one of the Policy.
4. The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
5. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval of the applicable committee prior to before commencement of the construction work pertaining to establishment of a New Tourism Project or expansion of an Expansion Tourism Project.
6. For Tourism Projects receiving subsidies, it shall be mandatory to operate the Tourism Project for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy. If the Tourism Project fails to abide by this condition, the applicant shall have to return the subsidy amount with a 10% simple interest per annum to the Department of Tourism.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions:
1. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district or within the Municipal Corporation limits of Bengaluru.
2. No exemption on stamp duty with respect to the development of Tourism Projects within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
3. No reimbursement on land conversion fee for conversion of land located within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA).
4. EPC does not include: Working Capital; Pre-operative expenses and preliminary expenses; Second-hand plant and machinery purchased or shifted from within or outside India; Interest capitalised; Consumable stores; Inventories for maintenance or repairs; Investment on land required for setting up the Tourism Project, inclusive of the cost of the land; Vehicles (except those permissible for Adventure, Caravan, Cruise, and Houseboat projects); Furniture, fixtures, cutlery, crockery, utensils; Any construction which in the nature of real estate transactions is meant for sale / lease / rent (shops, flats, offices, etc.); and Intangible assets including intellectual Property rights and goodwill.
5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa.

1. Expansion Tourism Projects must take up an expansion of more than 50% of existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC.

3. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval prior to commencement of construction work and must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy.

1. Tourism Project shall mean a legal entity under the relevant law that is engaged or to be engaged in providing any service related to tourism.
2. Eligible Tourism Project refers to the list of Tourism Projects identified by the Department of Tourism that shall be prioritized for development in Karnataka during the Policy Period. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Agri Tourism Project, 3. Apartment Hotel / Serviced Apartment, 4. Aquarium / Oceanarium, 5. Beach Shack, 6. Bed & Breakfast, 7. Amusement Park, 8. Caravan Park, 9. Caravan Tourism Project, 10. Convention Centre, 11. Cruise Tourism Project, 12. Cultural Centre, 13. Cultural Village / Tourist Village, 14. Eco Tourism Project, 15. Farm Stay, 16. Film City, 17. Golf Course, 18. Guest House, 19. Heritage Hotel, 20. Heritage Tourism Project, 21. Heritage Walk / Guided Tour, 22. Homestay, 23. Hotel ΓÇô Budget, 24. Hotel ΓÇô Premium, 25. Houseboat, 26. MICE Venue, 27. Museum and Galleries, 28. Pravasi Snehi Sankeerna (Tourist Facilitation Centre), 29. Ropeway, 30. Sound & Light Show, 31. Tented Accommodation, 32. Theme Park, 33. Timeshare Resort, 34. Tourist Guide, 35. Tourism or Hospitality Training Institute, 36. Tourism Startup, 37. Tour Operator, 38. Tourist Transport Operator, 39. Tourist Interpretation Centre, 40. Travel Agent, 41. Yatri Niwas, 42. Wellness Centre, 43. Wayside Amenities, 44. Yuva Tourism Club.
To qualify for benefits under this Policy, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
3. New Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised during the operative tenure of this Policy.
4. Existing Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised before the operative tenure of this Policy.
5. Expansion Tourism Project shall mean an existing Eligible Tourism Project that is taking up an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC for the Project. Only one expansion project of an existing Tourism Project will be eligible for assistance during the operative period of this Policy.
6. Mega Tourism Project shall mean Tourism Project with an EPC of above INR 100 Crore.
7. Tourism Service Provider shall mean any company, association, firm, or any other legal entity under the relevant law who is engaged in providing any service related to tourism. Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy.
14.1.3 Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible to avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions offered under this Section.
15.2.2 Supporting Provisions for availing Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions:
1. To avail the incentives, subsidies, and concessions for Eligible Tourism Projects identified in this Policy, the applicant must submit necessary documents and obtain the required approvals from the committee concerned as per the timelines specified in the Operational Guidelines of the Policy.
3. Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers can avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions under multiple policies of different departments of Government of Karnataka and / or Government of India. However, if the same component is claimed under different policies, the quantum is limited to the maximum of the component in any one of the Policy.
4. The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
5. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval of the applicable committee prior to before commencement of the construction work pertaining to establishment of a New Tourism Project or expansion of an Expansion Tourism Project.
6. For Tourism Projects receiving subsidies, it shall be mandatory to operate the Tourism Project for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy. If the Tourism Project fails to abide by this condition, the applicant shall have to return the subsidy amount with a 10% simple interest per annum to the Department of Tourism.
