policy_goals: To make Karnataka one among the top States of India in terms of domestic and international tourist visits (rank among top 3 States for domestic tourist visits and top 5 States for international tourist visits by 2029)
Support Karnataka's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032 through strong economic growth driven by tourism
To ensure every tourist to Karnataka experiences happiness, satisfaction, and cultural immersion
To enable tourism for all strata of society and provide high-quality offerings that cater to all tourist preferences
To harness tourism's potential for its effects on employment generation, economic development, and entrepreneurial opportunities
To strategically focus on emerging tourism segments as well as those where Karnataka is well-positioned to become the preferred choice
To instil confidence in tourists to travel across Karnataka by providing safety, convenience, and comfort throughout their journeys
To promote Karnataka domestically and internationally through diverse marketing channels, collaborations, and targeted strategies
To ensure quality tourism infrastructure and essential amenities for tourists at and enroute to major tourism destinations across Karnataka
To create exceptional experiences for diverse visitor profiles that encourage repeat visits and longer stays
To increase the visibility and accessibility of lesser-known destinations to promote balanced regional development
Identify, develop, and promote lesser-known tourism assets, expanding Karnataka's tourism potential
To create greater employment through tourism and its allied activities
To initiate and support skill development programs to meet the needs of Karnataka's tourism sector
To enhance the professionalism and visibility of tour guides and Tourism Service Providers and increase their presence across tourist destinations
To encourage sustainable development in tourism towards achievement of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals for Karnataka
To foster inclusive tourism by ensuring that tourism development benefits all communities especially women and marginalized groups
To make tourism inclusive and accessible for all while promoting respect for diverse backgrounds
To incorporate the promotion of local and traditional crafts, cuisines, and culture as integral components of the tourism experience
To foster tourism-driven socio-economic development in rural communities and showcasing of local traditions
To promote green initiatives in tourism, aligning tourism development with sustainability goals
To sustainably develop Coastal Karnataka into a multi-product tourism destination
To bring together stakeholders for the promotion and growth of responsible tourism in Karnataka
To encourage active involvement of locals in shaping tourism experiences and in the planning, development, and management of tourism initiatives, ensuring that benefits are shared equitably
To promote sustainable and climate resilient tourism practices that protect Karnataka's natural resources and its people
To position Karnataka as a preferred destination for tourism investments
To encourage Public-Private Partnerships to foster innovation and investment in tourism
To create an enabling framework for private sector investments and establish mechanisms to support industry-driven initiatives in tourism
To encourage startups, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, and innovative tourism offerings and foster linkages for their growth
To leverage technology and digital solutions for visitor engagement, marketing, and operational efficiency
To empower Karnataka Tourism with suitable institutional frameworks and administrative structures for the development and promotion of tourism
To leverage technology to facilitate data-driven outcome-oriented planning and policymaking
To facilitate effective inter-departmental coordination for the successful implementation of this Policy
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to position Karnataka among the top 3 Indian states for domestic tourist visits and top 5 for international tourist visits by 2029, contributing to the state's goal of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032. The policy covers 25 tourism themes including Adventure, Agri, Caravan, Coastal, Cultural, Eco, Heritage, MICE, Spiritual, and Wellness Tourism. It provides industry status to eligible tourism projects and offers a comprehensive package of fiscal and non-fiscal benefits. These include Capital Investment Subsidies (15% to 25% of Eligible Project Cost up to Γé╣10 Crore, with an additional 5% for women, SC/ST, differently-abled entrepreneurs, and hotel projects in Kalyana and Kittur Karnataka regions), Interest Subsidies (5% p.a. up to Γé╣25 Lakh over 5 years), 50% Stamp Duty exemption, 100% Registration Charges exemption, 100% Land Conversion Fee reimbursement, Motor Vehicle Tax exemptions/reimbursements for tourist transport and caravans, Marketing Development Assistance (up to Γé╣2 Lakh per activity), and 50% capital grants up to Γé╣1 Lakh for sustainability initiatives. Special non-fiscal concessions such as domestic utility tariffs and property tax rates are extended to registered Homestays and Agri Tourism projects.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
1. Tourism Project shall mean a legal entity under the relevant law that is engaged or to be engaged in providing any service related to tourism.
2. Eligible Tourism Project refers to the list of Tourism Projects identified by the Department of Tourism that shall be prioritized for development in Karnataka during the Policy Period. The Eligible Tourism Projects identified below shall be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy as outlined Section 14 Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Agri Tourism Project, 3. Apartment Hotel / Serviced Apartment, 4. Aquarium / Oceanarium, 5. Beach Shack, 6. Bed & Breakfast, 7. Amusement Park, 8. Caravan Park, 9. Caravan Tourism Project, 10. Convention Centre, 11. Cruise Tourism Project, 12. Cultural Centre, 13. Cultural Village / Tourist Village, 14. Eco Tourism Project, 15. Farm Stay, 16. Film City, 17. Golf Course, 18. Guest House, 19. Heritage Hotel, 20. Heritage Tourism Project, 21. Heritage Walk / Guided Tour, 22. Homestay, 23. Hotel ΓÇô Budget, 24. Hotel ΓÇô Premium, 25. Houseboat, 26. MICE Venue, 27. Museum and Galleries, 28. Pravasi Snehi Sankeerna (Tourist Facilitation Centre), 29. Ropeway, 30. Sound & Light Show, 31. Tented Accommodation, 32. Theme Park, 33. Timeshare Resort, 34. Tourist Guide, 35. Tourism or Hospitality Training Institute, 36. Tourism Startup, 37. Tour Operator, 38. Tourist Transport Operator, 39. Tourist Interpretation Centre, 40. Travel Agent, 41. Yatri Niwas, 42. Wellness Centre, 43. Wayside Amenities, 44. Yuva Tourism Club.
To qualify for benefits under this Policy, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
3. New Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised during the operative tenure of this Policy.
4. Existing Tourism Project shall mean an Eligible Tourism Project that has been established and operationalised before the operative tenure of this Policy.
5. Expansion Tourism Project shall mean an existing Eligible Tourism Project that is taking up an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC for the Project. Only one expansion project of an existing Tourism Project will be eligible for assistance during the operative period of this Policy.
6. Mega Tourism Project shall mean Tourism Project with an EPC of above INR 100 Crore.
7. Tourism Service Provider shall mean any company, association, firm, or any other legal entity under the relevant law who is engaged in providing any service related to tourism. Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under the Policy.
14.1.3 Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers must be registered with the Department of Tourism to be eligible to avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions offered under this Section.
15.2.2 Supporting Provisions for availing Incentives, Subsidies and Concessions:
1. To avail the incentives, subsidies, and concessions for Eligible Tourism Projects identified in this Policy, the applicant must submit necessary documents and obtain the required approvals from the committee concerned as per the timelines specified in the Operational Guidelines of the Policy.
3. Tourism Projects and Tourism Service Providers can avail incentives, subsidies, and concessions under multiple policies of different departments of Government of Karnataka and / or Government of India. However, if the same component is claimed under different policies, the quantum is limited to the maximum of the component in any one of the Policy.
4. The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
5. Tourism Projects availing subsidies must obtain in-principle approval of the applicable committee prior to before commencement of the construction work pertaining to establishment of a New Tourism Project or expansion of an Expansion Tourism Project.
6. For Tourism Projects receiving subsidies, it shall be mandatory to operate the Tourism Project for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy. If the Tourism Project fails to abide by this condition, the applicant shall have to return the subsidy amount with a 10% simple interest per annum to the Department of Tourism.

5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa.

7.1.2 Eligibility (Capital Investment Subsidy):
1. New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects for the following Eligible Tourism Projects shall be eligible for availing Capital Investment Subsidy: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Caravan Park Project, 3. Caravan Tourism Project, 4. Hotel Project ΓÇô Budget, 5. Hotel Project ΓÇô Premium, 6. Houseboat Project, 7. Wayside Amenities, 8. Wellness Centre.

To ensure every tourist to Karnataka experiences happiness, satisfaction, and cultural immersion
To enable tourism for all strata of society and provide high-quality offerings that cater to all tourist preferences
To harness tourism's potential for its effects on employment generation, economic development, and entrepreneurial opportunities
To strategically focus on emerging tourism segments as well as those where Karnataka is well-positioned to become the preferred choice
To instil confidence in tourists to travel across Karnataka by providing safety, convenience, and comfort throughout their journeys
To promote Karnataka domestically and internationally through diverse marketing channels, collaborations, and targeted strategies
To ensure quality tourism infrastructure and essential amenities for tourists at and enroute to major tourism destinations across Karnataka
To create exceptional experiences for diverse visitor profiles that encourage repeat visits and longer stays
To increase the visibility and accessibility of lesser-known destinations to promote balanced regional development
Identify, develop, and promote lesser-known tourism assets, expanding Karnataka's tourism potential
To create greater employment through tourism and its allied activities
To initiate and support skill development programs to meet the needs of Karnataka's tourism sector
To enhance the professionalism and visibility of tour guides and Tourism Service Providers and increase their presence across tourist destinations
To encourage sustainable development in tourism towards achievement of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals for Karnataka
To foster inclusive tourism by ensuring that tourism development benefits all communities especially women and marginalized groups
To make tourism inclusive and accessible for all while promoting respect for diverse backgrounds
To incorporate the promotion of local and traditional crafts, cuisines, and culture as integral components of the tourism experience
To foster tourism-driven socio-economic development in rural communities and showcasing of local traditions
To promote green initiatives in tourism, aligning tourism development with sustainability goals
To sustainably develop Coastal Karnataka into a multi-product tourism destination
To bring together stakeholders for the promotion and growth of responsible tourism in Karnataka
To encourage active involvement of locals in shaping tourism experiences and in the planning, development, and management of tourism initiatives, ensuring that benefits are shared equitably
To promote sustainable and climate resilient tourism practices that protect Karnataka's natural resources and its people
To position Karnataka as a preferred destination for tourism investments
To encourage Public-Private Partnerships to foster innovation and investment in tourism
To create an enabling framework for private sector investments and establish mechanisms to support industry-driven initiatives in tourism
To encourage startups, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, and innovative tourism offerings and foster linkages for their growth
To leverage technology and digital solutions for visitor engagement, marketing, and operational efficiency
To empower Karnataka Tourism with suitable institutional frameworks and administrative structures for the development and promotion of tourism
To leverage technology to facilitate data-driven outcome-oriented planning and policymaking
To facilitate effective inter-departmental coordination for the successful implementation of this Policy

To create exceptional experiences for diverse visitor profiles that encourage repeat visits and longer stays

Volume 1 covers Capital Investment Subsidy (15% to 25% of EPC up to Γé╣5 Crore for 8 project types, plus 5% additional for Women/SC/ST/differently-abled entrepreneurs or Premium Hotels in Kalyana Karnataka) and Interest Subsidy (5% p.a. up to Γé╣25 Lakh over 5 years for 4 project categories). Volume 2 covers Incentives including KTTF Registration, Facilitation Support, Assistance for Sustainability Initiatives (50% up to Γé╣1 Lakh), and Marketing Development Assistance (50% to 75% up to Γé╣1 Lakh). To qualify for incentives, subsidies, and concessions under Karnataka Tourism Policy 2020-26, Eligible Tourism Projects must be registered with the Department and must meet the conditions as per the Operational Guidelines.
7.1.2 Eligibility (Capital Investment Subsidy):
1. New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects for the following Eligible Tourism Projects shall be eligible for availing Capital Investment Subsidy: 1. Adventure Tourism Project, 2. Caravan Park Project, 3. Caravan Tourism Project, 4. Hotel Project ΓÇô Budget, 5. Hotel Project ΓÇô Premium, 6. Houseboat Project, 7. Wayside Amenities, 8. Wellness Centre.
3. Tourism Project must be undertaken on land owned by the Applicant to be eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy. However, Adventure Tourism Project and Wayside Amenities may be undertaken on leased land as well to be eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy. The term of the lease must be for a minimum of 10 years as on the date of application for In-Principle Approval.
5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa.
6. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district.
7. To be eligible for the Additional Capital Investment Subsidy where Tourism Project is undertaken by Women, SC, ST or differently abled entrepreneur, the Project must be established exclusively by an entrepreneur from one of these categories. Hence, depending on the type of legal entity that is applying for the subsidy, the proprietor of the sole proprietorship or all the partners or all the directors of the partnership / LLP / company / society or any other type of legal entity should belong to one of the special categories viz. Women, SC, ST or differently abled entrepreneur.
19.5 The total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed by a Tourism Project shall not exceed 30% of the EPC of the project.
19.7 A Tourism Project may avail of capital investment subsidy or interest subsidy only once during the Policy Period.

incentive_details.description: Interest subsidy at 5% per annum on term loans taken from Banks, SFCs, or SIDCs on fixed capital investment for New and Expansion Tourism Projects in Agri Tourism, Cultural Tourism (Cultural Village, Museum & Gallery), Heritage Tourism (Heritage Hotel, Sound & Light Show), and Safety & Hygiene Tourism (Mobile Toilet Van Project).
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 5% p.a. interest subsidy on term loans for 5 years, up to Γé╣7.5 Lakh per annum and Γé╣25 Lakh total, for Agri, Cultural, Heritage, and Mobile Toilet Van projects.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply for In-Principle Approval with loan sanction letter before construction; apply for Final Approval with loan release letter and Fixed Investment Certificate within 1 year of commercial operation; execute Subsidy Agreement and submit annual disbursal applications with Bank Certificate for Payment of Loan Instalment.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: maximum of INR 25 Lakh for a period of five years (shall not exceed INR 7.5 Lakh per annum)
quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable only for loans from Banks, SFCs, SIDCs, and equivalent State-level financial institutions; reimbursed annually after 12 months of operation upon timely repayment of loan instalments.
quantified_benefits.description: 5% per annum interest subsidy on term loan for 5 years, up to Γé╣7.5 Lakh per year and Γé╣25 Lakh total
quantified_benefits.source_text: New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects shall be eligible to get interest subsidy at 5% per annum on the term loan taken on the fixed capital investment for the Tourism Project, subject to a maximum of INR 25 Lakh for a period of five years. The interest subsidy shall not exceed INR 7.5 Lakh per annum for the Tourism Project and shall be provided only for timely repayment of loan instalment along with interest.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New and Expansion Projects in: 1. Agri Tourism Project, 2. Cultural Tourism Project (Cultural Village, Museum & Gallery), 3. Heritage Tourism Project (Heritage Hotel, Sound & Light Show), 4. Safety and Hygiene Tourism Project (Mobile Toilet Van Project)

incentive_details.application_deadline: Phase 1 (In-Principle): Before commencement of construction. Phase 2 (Final Approval): Within 1 year from date of commencement of commercial operation. Phase 3 (Disbursal): After completion of 12 months from commencement of operations and annually on anniversary thereof.
incentive_details.application_authority: Convener of the District Tourism Committee (for EPC up to INR 5 Crore) or Empowered Committee for Tourism (for EPC above INR 5 Crore).
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Must be undertaken on land owned by the Applicant. Any default period in loan repayment is ineligible and deducted from the 5-year eligible period.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Micro, Small Enterprises ΓÇô Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP), implemented by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, and facilitated in Karnataka by the Karnataka Council for Technological Upgradation (KCTU), aims to enhance the productivity, competitiveness, and capacity building of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) through a cluster development approach. The scheme provides substantial Government of India financial grants (ranging from 50% to 80% of the total project cost) for two main components: setting up Common Facility Centres (CFCs) for testing, training, raw material depots, effluent treatment, and complementing production processes (project costs between Rs 5 Crore and Rs 30 Crore), and Infrastructure Development for new or existing industrial areas/clusters (project costs between Rs 5 Crore and Rs 15 Crore). Projects must be implemented through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered as a Section 8 Company or Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) comprising at least 10 to 20 MSEs/Startups/FPOs. eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
Characteristics of the Cluster
A cluster is a group of enterprises located within an identifiable and contiguous area (to a large extent) or a value chain that may go beyond a geographical area and producing same / similar products / complementary products/ services, which can be linked together by common physical infrastructure facilities. It must address their common challenges which is the core reason to take up the project under this scheme.
The essential characteristics of enterprises in a cluster are (a) Similarity or complementarity in the methods of production, quality control & testing, energy consumption, pollution control, etc., (b) Similar level of technology & marketing strategies / practices, (c) Similar channels for communication among the members of the cluster, (d) Common market & skill needs and/ or (e) Common challenges & opportunities that the cluster faces.
Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)
There shall be a SPV for the projects for CFC, which would be a Company registered under Section 8 of the Company.
Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)/ Farmer Producer Company (FPC) registered under Section 8 of the Company Act with minimum number of MSEs as their member as provisioned in the guidelines of the Scheme shall also be allowed as the SPV.
Units
1. Minimum 20 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFC with project cost of above Rs 10 crore and above.
2. Minimum 10 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFCs with project cost of below Rs 10 crore.
The SPV may take efforts to increase the number of members (shareholders) to ensure that CFC is a collective initiative and is able to meet the aspirations of a higher number of units.
Land
The CFC should be housed in Land/ Building owned by the SPV (acquired through contribution of the members). CFC can be set up in leased premises. However, the lease should be legally tenable and for a fairly long duration but not less than 15 years. In case CFC is established on leased land, the Lease Period should not be less than 25 years. The Land/Building ownership/lease related documents including non-agricultural conversion if applicable must be submitted along with DPR.
Long Term Lease could be selectively allowed if the property (CFC) is on land owned by an Industry Association or any other Institutional land. In any case lease shall not be allowed for any property owned by members or their family members.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: In any case lease shall not be allowed for any property owned by members or their family members.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 20 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFC with project cost of Rs 10 crore and above; Minimum 10 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFCs with project cost below Rs 10 crore. Land/Building must be owned by the SPV or held on legally tenable lease (minimum 15 years for leased premises, minimum 25 years for leased land).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Enterprises must be located within an identifiable and contiguous area (to a large extent) or a value chain that may go beyond a geographical area. Enhanced funding applies to projects located in Aspirational districts, NER, Hill states, Island territories, and LWE affected districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: SPV must be a Company registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act (including FPO/FPC registered under Section 8). Member MSEs must provide Udyam Registration Number in the DPR.

policy_name: Nipuna Karnataka Initiative

keywords: Dept of E IT and Bt
policy_goals: Enhance the skills and employability of the state's workforce by bridging the gap between industry requirements and current skill levels.

Provide upskilling, reskilling, and vocational training opportunities to the youth of Karnataka in areas such as Information Technology, Biotechnology, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Cybersecurity.
Create a future-ready, globally competitive workforce capable of driving Karnataka's economic growth through public-private partnerships.
Establish state-of-the-art training centres throughout the state and ensure trainees are equipped with industry-validated certifications and placement opportunities.
policy_details.policy_summary: Nipuna Karnataka is a state-wide skill development initiative by the Government of Karnataka (Department of Electronics, IT & Bt) aimed at bridging the gap between industry requirements and current workforce skill levels. Operating through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, the program collaborates with established companies, academic institutions, and skill aggregators to deliver holistic training programs in emerging technologies (IT, Biotechnology, AI, Data Science, Cybersecurity) encompassing practical learning, on-the-job training, and soft skills development. The Government of Karnataka provides up to 40% co-funding for approved training programs, disbursed in three placement-linked tranches, while partnering organizations and CSR funds cover the remaining costs. Partner organizations must ensure at least 70% placement of freshers and unemployed trainees within 8 months of course completion.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 40% Government co-funding under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models for industry-led workforce skilling, reskilling, and vocational training programs in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology (Dept. of E, IT & Bt), Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
2.1.1 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR COMPANIES:
- Companies must have been in existence for at least 10 years and have a minimum of two years of established operations in Karnataka.
- They should employ at least 500 full-time staff in their Karnataka-based operations since atleast a year.
- Companies must demonstrate the capacity and commitment to train or financially support the training of at least 1,000 trainees annually.
(The capacity of the companies will be evaluated based on the No of trainees trained in last 2 years; analysis of the budget allocation for training in last 2 years; their partnership with educational institutions, external training providers, and skill development institutions; internal policies regarding continuous skilling of employees etc.)

2.1.2 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS
- The institution must be a registered educational institution. This includes government, private, or aided institutions.
- The institution must have a minimum enrolment of 500 students across relevant programs or disciplines
- The institution should have a minimum of 5 years of experience in delivering academic programs, demonstrating stability and proven expertise in the field of education.

2.1.3 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SKILL AGGREGATORS
- Must have trained a minimum of 5,000 individuals across various sectors, with at least 50% of trainees successfully placed within the last three years.
- Should have active partnerships with a minimum of 10 companies across diverse industries, enabling a broad range of placement opportunities for candidates.
- Should have been operational for at least five years with a minimum of two years of demonstrated impact within Karnataka.
- Proven experience in leveraging digital platforms or tools for skilling and job matching, enhancing accessibility and scalability.

2.2 CATEGORIES OF TRAINEES:
2.2.1 STUDENTS: This category includes individuals who are currently enrolled in universities, colleges, or other educational institutions government/ aided/ private. Trainees may be pursuing their under graduation, postgraduation, diploma, or postgraduate diploma programs and are in their final year of education. It also includes individuals who have completed their 12th grade or an equivalent level of education and are seeking further skills training.
2.2.2 EMPLOYEES SEEKING UPSKILLING: This category encompasses current employees who are looking to upgrade or enhance their existing skills. It also includes individuals who are currently unemployed but seeking to improve their qualifications to re-enter the workforce. Similar to the student category, individuals who have completed their 12th grade or an equivalent level of education are eligible for this training.

GENERAL GUIDELINES:
- An organisation partnering with government for the initiative cannot train their own employee under this program.
- The total number of trainee should consist minimum of 70% freshers, 20% unemployed and 10% employed. For example, if there are 100 trainees (70 freshers, 20 unemployed, and 10 employed), the company should ensure placement of at least 70% of the first 90 trainees (excluding the 10 employed).
- A partnering company must ensure the placement of at least 70% of trained resources, excluding those already employed.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: An organisation partnering with government for the initiative cannot train their own employee under this program.

minimum_employees.raw_text: They should employ at least 500 full-time staff in their Karnataka-based operations since atleast a year.

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: For Companies: Must be in existence for at least 10 years, have at least 2 years of operations in Karnataka, and demonstrate capacity to train or financially support at least 1,000 trainees annually. For Academic Institutions: Minimum 5 years experience in delivering academic programs and minimum enrolment of 500 students across relevant disciplines. For Skill Aggregators: Operational for at least 5 years (min 2 years impact in Karnataka), trained min 5,000 individuals with at least 50% placed in last 3 years, and active partnerships with min 10 companies. Trainee batch composition must be minimum 70% freshers, 20% unemployed, and 10% employed. Partner must ensure placement of at least 70% of trained resources (excluding already employed) within 8 months.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Minimum of two years of established operations or demonstrated impact within Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Academic institutions must be registered educational institutions (government, private, or aided).

incentive_details.description: Under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, the Government of Karnataka jointly funds and manages training programs alongside partnering organizations (companies, academic institutions, skill aggregators, CSR). The funding covers direct training costs such as tuition, materials, and trainers' costs, with Government participation capped at 40% of the budget. The government funding is released in three tranches tied to proposal approval and trainee placement milestones.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme supports FPOs, cooperatives, proprietorship firms, partnership firms, limited companies, and SHGs involved in food processing to establish market linkages by participating in domestic and international trade fairs. policy_name: Assistance for Creation of Eco Stores / Modern Retail Outlets (Annexure - III)
incentive_name: Financial Assistance for Creation of Infrastructure for Modern Organic Retail Outlets / Eco-Stores

policy_goals: To bring organic farming into mainstream agricultural production system which would help in transforming at least 10% of the cultivable area of the state into organic farming by 2022
To enable organics and millets farmers of the State realise 25 to 30% additional income by leverage the demands of organic market
To focus on commodity/crop specific clusters to generate bulk quantity of organic foods and millets to meet the growing demand of domestic as well as export market
To improve the quality of organic foods and millets by extending state support to investors for the establishment of necessary supply chain and infrastructure facilities to process and market

To safeguard the interest of the consumers by putting in place suitable regulatory measures, which would facilitate in upholding the principles of traceability, accountability and transparency in production, handling and marketing of organic produce
To maximise production and productivity of organics and millets
To enable farmers to mitigate and adapt to the climate change and drought situations effectively
To maximise crop and farm diversification thereby enhancing protection against crop losses due to adverse weather conditions
To increase farmer's income by facilitating value addition to organic produce and millets thereby reducing post harvest losses and other wastages
To create and strengthen local institutions for effective service delivery and sharing of knowledge and skills
To bring in more transparency in production, handling and marketing of organic produce and to safe guard the consumers interest
policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme aims to create greater consumer demand and ensure the shelf life of perishable organic produce by expanding the retail network of eco-stores and modern organic outlets across Karnataka. It provides financial assistance to individuals, farmer associations, producer companies, and private organizations for creating infrastructure facilities to open modern organic retail outlets, establishes separate organic corners in existing HOPCOMS outlets, provides exhibition space in consumer fairs, and organizes Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) through Agri-Business Management Departments of State Agricultural Universities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Financial assistance for infrastructure creation to open modern organic retail outlets/eco-stores, exhibition space in consumer fairs, and EDP training for agri-entrepreneurs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme promotes the establishment and modernization of collection, grading, value addition, and processing centres on a project mode in the vicinity of production centres across Karnataka. It targets potential crops such as paddy, pulses, millets, sugarcane, vegetables, fruits, and spices (e.g., jaggery units at Belagavi, Tur units at Kalaburagi, Chilli units at Haveri). The policy provides financial assistance for setting up new centres or upgrading conventional centres, offers free or subsidised processing technologies from premier research institutions (CFTRI, DFRL, KCTU, IICPT, SAUs), and facilitates bank linkages and project proposal preparation through NABARD.

policy_details.policy_summary: This scheme aims to encourage bulk and uniform quality production of organic crops and millets through a cluster approach across potential districts in Karnataka for domestic and export markets. It focuses on 13 specific crop clusters including sugarcane, pulses, minor millets, paddy, other cereals, honey/spices/coffee, vegetables, fruits, onion, oilseeds, cotton, Byadagi chilli, and dried grapes. The programme supports the formation and upgradation of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), federations, and companies, and provides comprehensive assistance for capacity building, technology transfer from institutes like CFTRI/DFRL and State Agricultural Universities, common collection/grading/packing infrastructure, subsidized cold storage, revolving funds for working capital, quality testing, refrigerated transport, and market development.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive cluster development support including revolving funds for working capital, subsidized storage in APMC/KAPPEC godowns, and financial assistance for collection centres, quality testing, and refrigerated transport vehicles.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
Target Beneficiaries
Identified farmers associations/FPOs/producer companies/federations, etc. with recommendations of District Organic Farming Committee/KSOCA.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: The policy shall take firm stand against GM crops and shall make adequate mechanisms to check unscrupulous elements to push GMOs in the certified/notified organic areas. These cannot be packed or shipped in containers containing synthetic fungicide, preservative or fumigant. The animals shall not be given growth-producing hormones or antibiotics.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Recommendations of District Organic Farming Committee/KSOCA required. Focus on one or two predominant crops of the region at taluk/hobli level.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Specific potential districts identified for 13 crop clusters: 1. Sugarcane (for organic jaggery): Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalakote, Mandya; 2. Pulses: Kalaburagi, Yadagiri, Bidar, Vijayapura; 3. Minor millets: Haveri, Chitradurga, Davanagere, Koppala; 4. Paddy: Hassan (Holenarsapur Taluk for Rajmudi Rice), Davangere, Raichur, Mandya, Mysuru, Belagavi, Ballari, Uttara Kannada; 5. Other cereals: Raichur, Mandya, Mysuru, Dharwad, Bagalkote, Gadag, Haveri; 6. Honey, Spices and Coffee: Chickmaglur, Shivamogga, Dakshina Kannada, Hassan, Kodagu, Uttara Kannada; 7. Vegetables: Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Chikkaballapur, Kolar, Belagavi, Mysuru, Bidar, Vijayapura; 8. Fruits: Dharwad, Chitradurga, Koppal, Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Belagavi; 9. Onion: Ballari, Raichur, Vijayapura; 10. Oil seeds: Tumkur, Dharwad, Belagavi, Haveri, Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Koppala, Bidar; 11. Cotton: Chamarajanagar; 12. Byadagi chilli: Haveri, Gadag, Dharwad; 13. Dried Grapes (Raisins): Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Belagavi.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Participatory Guarantee System of Certification shall be made compulsory for domestic market; Third party certification for export and niche markets; Mandatory registration under FSSAI for wholesale dealers and retailers.

The programme supports the formation and upgradation of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), federations, and companies, and provides comprehensive assistance for capacity building, technology transfer from institutes like CFTRI/DFRL and State Agricultural Universities, common collection/grading/packing infrastructure, subsidized cold storage, revolving funds for working capital, quality testing, refrigerated transport, and market development.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive cluster development support including revolving funds for working capital, subsidized storage in APMC/KAPPEC godowns, and financial assistance for collection centres, quality testing, and refrigerated transport vehicles.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka

policy_goals: To bring organic farming into mainstream agricultural production system which would help in transforming at least 10% of the cultivable area of the state into organic farming by 2022
To enable organics and millets farmers of the State realise 25 to 30% additional income by leverage the demands of organic market
To focus on commodity/crop specific clusters to generate bulk quantity of organic foods and millets to meet the growing demand of domestic as well as export market
To improve the quality of organic foods and millets by extending state support to investors for the establishment of necessary supply chain and infrastructure facilities to process and market

To safeguard the interest of the consumers by putting in place suitable regulatory measures, which would facilitate in upholding the principles of traceability, accountability and transparency in production, handling and marketing of organic produce
To maximise production and productivity of organics and millets
To enable farmers to mitigate and adapt to the climate change and drought situations effectively
To maximise crop and farm diversification thereby enhancing protection against crop losses due to adverse weather conditions
To increase farmer's income by facilitating value addition to organic produce and millets thereby reducing post harvest losses and other wastages
To create and strengthen local institutions for effective service delivery and sharing of knowledge and skills
To bring in more transparency in production, handling and marketing of organic produce and to safe guard the consumers interest

policy_details.policy_summary: Under the overarching implementation strategies of the Karnataka Organic Farming Policy 2017, the State Government provides several cross-cutting incentives to promote organic cultivation, quality control, eco-agri tourism, and exports. Key measures include treating conventional subsidies on chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation as an opportunity cost paid as a price incentive to organic farmers; special incentives for fully certified organic farms with no parallel production; additional incentives over the state tourism policy for Eco-Agri Tourism; special export incentives for packing, labelling, branding, and participating in international exhibitions; support for setting up pesticide residue and nutrition analysis laboratories; and grants to 14 Regional Federations of Organic Farmers' Associations.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Price incentives equivalent to conventional fertilizer/pesticide/irrigation subsidies for organic farmers, additional Eco-Agri Tourism incentives over the Tourism Policy, export branding/exhibition incentives, and support for residue testing labs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Eco Agri Tourism in bio/organic villages
Western Ghats taluks/districts identified as fully organic

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Target groups across sections 3.2, 3.5, and 3.6 include: organic farmers, fully certified organic farms with no parallel production, bio/organic villages and organic farms involved in training and educating farmers/public on organic agriculture, 14 Regional Federations of Organic Farmers' Associations, exporters of organics and millets, and entities setting up laboratories for pesticide residue testing and nutrition analysis.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GMOs in certified/notified organic areas; parallel production (for the fully certified farm incentive).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Pesticide residue analysis and soil testing shall be made mandatory in certification process.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Karnataka (certain favourable taluks/districts of Western Ghats identified as fully organic).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: 3rd party certification for export and niche markets; Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification compulsory for domestic market; FSSAI registration for dealers and retailers.

policy_details.benefit_headline: Price incentives equivalent to conventional fertilizer/pesticide/irrigation subsidies for organic farmers, additional Eco-Agri Tourism incentives over the Tourism Policy, export branding/exhibition incentives, and support for residue testing labs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Eco Agri Tourism in bio/organic villages
Western Ghats taluks/districts identified as fully organic

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Target groups across sections 3.2, 3.5, and 3.6 include: organic farmers, fully certified organic farms with no parallel production, bio/organic villages and organic farms involved in training and educating farmers/public on organic agriculture, 14 Regional Federations of Organic Farmers' Associations, exporters of organics and millets, and entities setting up laboratories for pesticide residue testing and nutrition analysis.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GMOs in certified/notified organic areas; parallel production (for the fully certified farm incentive).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Pesticide residue analysis and soil testing shall be made mandatory in certification process.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Karnataka (certain favourable taluks/districts of Western Ghats identified as fully organic).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: 3rd party certification for export and niche markets; Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification compulsory for domestic market; FSSAI registration for dealers and retailers.

incentive_details.description: Support to set up laboratories for pesticide residue testing, nitrate and heavy metal residue detection, soil testing, and nutrition analysis to enforce quality control in organic certification.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: State support for establishing laboratories for pesticide residue testing, heavy metal detection, soil testing, and nutrition analysis.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Support to set up laboratories (quantum finalised by SLEC)
quantified_benefits.description: Support for setting up laboratories for pesticide residue testing, nitrate/heavy metal detection, and nutrition analysis (quantum finalised by SLEC).
quantified_benefits.source_text: 3.6.6 Support to set up laboratories for pesticide residue testing and nutrition analysis. Pesticide residue analysis and soil testing shall be made mandatory in certification process.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Entities establishing quality control and testing laboratories

policy_details.policy_summary: Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) is a World Bank supported Central Sector Scheme launched by the Government of India to support the overall Covid Resilience and Recovery Programme of the Ministry of MSME. Implemented in Karnataka by the nodal agency Karnataka Council for Technological Upgradation (KCTU), the scheme aims at improving market access, access to credit, strengthening institutions and governance at the Centre and State, improving Centre-State linkages and partnerships, addressing issues of delayed payments through online dispute resolution, and greening of MSMEs. Key proposed interventions in Karnataka include competitiveness support, market access, digitalization, cluster-level technical interventions, financial institution partnerships, support to women-headed MSMEs, funding support, skill development, sector-specific interventions, and MSME business facilitation networks.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive institutional, financial, technological, and market access support for MSMEs in Karnataka under the World Bank-supported RAMP programme.
